Patel AutoPrint v2.0
Product Requirements Document (PRD)
Chapter 1 – Executive Summary & Product Vision
Document Version: 2.0
Project Name: Patel AutoPrint
Product Type: Cloud-Based Multi-Tenant Print Shop Management & Automatic Printing Platform (SaaS)
Document Status: Draft
Target Audience: Product Owners, Developers, UI/UX Designers, QA Engineers, DevOps Engineers, AI Coding Assistants (Codex), Investors, and Future Development Teams.
________________________________________
1. Executive Summary
Patel AutoPrint is a next-generation cloud-based software platform designed to digitize and automate the workflow of modern print shops.
Unlike traditional online printing websites that only allow customers to upload files and select basic print settings, Patel AutoPrint is intended to replicate the complete experience of a professional print shop while remaining simple enough for non-technical users.
The platform is designed to eliminate manual communication between customers and print shop operators by allowing customers to configure complex print jobs themselves while providing operators with intelligent tools for reviewing, approving, and automatically printing orders.
The software should serve as a scalable SaaS platform that can be used by thousands of independent print shops, each operating under its own account with separate printers, pricing, branding, customers, employees, and business rules.
The long-term goal is to become the operating system for print shops.
________________________________________
2. Product Mission
The mission of Patel AutoPrint is:
To make professional printing accessible, automated, accurate, and simple for every customer while reducing manual work for print shop operators.
The software must bridge the gap between technical printing terminology and customer expectations by converting complex print operations into intuitive workflows.
Customers should never need to understand printer-specific concepts such as duplex edge flipping, page imposition, printer drivers, or print queues.
Instead, the software should make intelligent decisions on behalf of the customer whenever possible.
________________________________________
3. Product Vision
Patel AutoPrint aims to become the industry-standard software platform for print shops.
The platform should enable any print shop to:
•	Accept online print orders. 
•	Configure unlimited printers. 
•	Manage multiple employees. 
•	Provide customers with advanced print customization. 
•	Automatically route jobs to the correct printer. 
•	Track every order from upload to completion. 
•	Generate reports and business insights. 
•	Operate entirely through the cloud while using a local Windows Print Agent for secure printing. 
The software should eventually support not only document printing but also photo printing, ID card printing, passport photos, spiral binding, lamination, large-format printing, merchandising, and additional print services through modular extensions.
________________________________________
4. Core Philosophy
Every design decision must follow five principles.
Principle 1 – Customer First
The software should be understandable by first-time users.
Many customers are students, parents, office workers, or government document users with little technical knowledge.
The interface must reduce confusion rather than expose every printer setting.
________________________________________
Principle 2 – Think Like a Print Shop Operator
The software should automatically perform tasks that an experienced operator would normally do manually.
Examples include:
•	Selecting the correct duplex flip direction. 
•	Detecting page orientation. 
•	Identifying color pages. 
•	Suggesting optimal print layouts. 
•	Calculating sheet counts. 
•	Routing jobs to the appropriate printer. 
________________________________________
Principle 3 – Automation Over Manual Work
The system should automate repetitive tasks wherever possible.
Operators should spend their time serving customers, not configuring printers.
Examples include:
•	Automatic printer selection. 
•	Automatic Office document conversion. 
•	Automatic page layout generation. 
•	Automatic pricing. 
•	Automatic print-ready PDF generation. 
•	Automatic order status updates. 
________________________________________
Principle 4 – Modular Architecture
Every major capability should exist as an independent module.
Examples:
•	Upload Engine 
•	Preview Engine 
•	Pricing Engine 
•	Print Processing Engine 
•	Windows Print Agent 
•	Notification Service 
•	Payment Service 
•	Analytics Service 
Modules should communicate through well-defined APIs so new features can be added without affecting unrelated functionality.
________________________________________
Principle 5 – Multi-Tenant by Design
The platform must never assume it is running for a single shop.
Every piece of data belongs to a specific shop.
Each print shop should have:
•	Its own branding. 
•	Its own users. 
•	Its own customers. 
•	Its own printers. 
•	Its own pricing. 
•	Its own reports. 
•	Its own payment configuration. 
•	Its own print agent. 
No shop should ever be able to access another shop's data.
________________________________________
5. Business Goals
Patel AutoPrint is intended to achieve the following business objectives:
•	Reduce waiting time in print shops. 
•	Allow customers to configure print jobs independently. 
•	Minimize operator errors. 
•	Increase print shop productivity. 
•	Standardize printing workflows. 
•	Provide cloud-based management. 
•	Enable remote order submission. 
•	Create a scalable subscription-based SaaS platform. 
•	Support future expansion into international markets. 
________________________________________
6. Target Customers
The platform serves two categories of users.
A. Print Shop Businesses
Examples include:
•	Local Xerox shops 
•	Stationery stores 
•	University print centers 
•	Corporate print rooms 
•	Government document centers 
•	Internet cafés with printing services 
•	Commercial printing businesses 
________________________________________
B. End Customers
Examples include:
•	Students 
•	Teachers 
•	Office employees 
•	Government exam applicants 
•	Business professionals 
•	Designers 
•	Photographers 
•	Freelancers 
•	General consumers 
________________________________________
7. Primary User Roles
The platform should support multiple user roles.
Customer
Uploads files, configures print settings, previews output, pays online, and tracks orders.
Shop Owner
Manages the entire business, printers, pricing, employees, subscriptions, and reports.
Manager
Supervises operations, approves jobs, and monitors staff.
Operator
Reviews customer jobs, selects printers when needed, approves printing, and resolves print issues.
System Administrator
Maintains the SaaS platform, manages subscriptions, monitors system health, and supports all registered print shops.
________________________________________
8. Product Scope
The first commercial release should include:
•	Multi-shop support. 
•	Cloud-based customer portal. 
•	Windows Print Agent. 
•	Automatic printer routing. 
•	Live print preview. 
•	Mixed print rules. 
•	N-up printing. 
•	Office document conversion. 
•	Image layouts. 
•	PowerPoint layouts. 
•	Dynamic pricing. 
•	Payment integration. 
•	Admin dashboard. 
•	Reporting. 
•	Printer management. 
•	User management. 
•	Search by mobile number, order ID, and customer name. 
________________________________________
9. Long-Term Vision
Patel AutoPrint should evolve into a complete ecosystem for print businesses.
Future capabilities may include:
•	AI Print Assistant 
•	WhatsApp Printing 
•	Email-to-Print 
•	OCR for scanned documents 
•	Automatic color page detection 
•	Passport photo generator 
•	ID card generator 
•	Photo editing tools 
•	Bulk corporate printing 
•	Franchise management 
•	Inventory management 
•	Customer loyalty programs 
•	Mobile applications 
•	Public API for third-party integrations 
•	Marketplace for premium modules 
________________________________________

10. Definition of Success
Patel AutoPrint will be considered successful when:
•	Customers can submit complex print jobs without staff assistance. 
•	Operators can approve and print jobs in seconds. 
•	Multiple print shops can use the same platform without custom development. 
•	The software scales reliably as the customer base grows. 
•	The platform becomes the preferred operating system for modern print shops.

Chapter 4 – Multi-Tenant SaaS Architecture & Database Design
Version: 2.0
________________________________________
4.1 Purpose
The objective of this chapter is to define a scalable cloud architecture capable of serving thousands of independent print shops using the same application.
Every print shop must operate as if it owns a dedicated system, while all shops share the same cloud infrastructure.
The architecture must be secure, modular, fault-tolerant, and extensible.
________________________________________
4.2 Multi-Tenant Architecture
Patel AutoPrint must use a multi-tenant architecture.
A tenant represents one independent print shop.
Examples:
•	Patel Xerox & Stationery 
•	ABC Digital Print 
•	University Print Center 
•	City Copy House 
Each tenant has completely isolated:
•	Users 
•	Customers 
•	Orders 
•	Files 
•	Printers 
•	Pricing 
•	Payment Settings 
•	Reports 
•	Branding 
•	Windows Print Agents 
Every database table that stores tenant-specific data must include a shopId (or equivalent tenant identifier).

4.9 Security
Requirements:
•	HTTPS for all communication. 
•	Passwords stored using a strong hashing algorithm (e.g., Argon2id or bcrypt with appropriate cost). 
•	JWT or secure session management. 
•	Role-based authorization checks. 
•	File access restricted to the owning shop. 
•	Virus scanning for uploads (recommended). 
•	Rate limiting on authentication and public endpoints. 
•	Signed URLs or equivalent for temporary file downloads.

4.10 Scalability
The architecture should support:
•	Multiple application servers. 
•	Horizontal scaling. 
•	Separate storage for files. 
•	Background workers for document conversion and preview generation. 
•	Queue-based processing for large print jobs. 
Long-running tasks should not block user requests.

4.11 Backup & Recovery

4.13 Design Decision: Print Instructions vs Orders
This is a key architectural choice.
•	An Order represents the customer's entire purchase. 
•	An Order File represents each uploaded document. 
•	A Print Instruction represents one printable configuration derived from a file. 
This separation allows a single PDF to be printed with different settings (e.g., pages 1–10 single-sided, pages 11–20 duplex) while preserving a clear audit trail and simplifying processing.

Chapter 5 – Print Processing Engine (Core of the System)
This is the heart of Patel AutoPrint.
The Print Processing Engine is responsible for transforming customer uploads into print-ready documents. It applies all customer-selected settings, generates accurate previews, calculates pricing, and prepares files for automatic printing. The engine must be modular, deterministic, and independent of any specific printer driver.
________________________________________
5.1 Objectives
The engine must:
•	Accept multiple file types. 
•	Convert Office documents to PDF where necessary. 
•	Apply print settings. 
•	Generate accurate previews. 
•	Create print-ready PDFs. 
•	Calculate sheet counts. 
•	Route jobs to the correct printer after approval. 
________________________________________
5.2 Processing Pipeline
Every uploaded file follows the same pipeline:
Upload
   ↓
File Analysis
   ↓
Validation
   ↓
Conversion (if required)
   ↓
Print Rule Engine
   ↓
Preview Generation
   ↓
Pricing Calculation
   ↓
Print-ready PDF Generation
   ↓
Admin Approval
   ↓
Printer Routing
   ↓
Windows Print Agent
   ↓
Printing
Each stage must be independently testable and replaceable.
________________________________________
5.3 Supported Input Types
Mandatory:
•	PDF 
•	DOC / DOCX 
•	PPT / PPTX 
•	XLS / XLSX 
•	JPG / JPEG 
•	PNG 
•	WEBP 
Future:
•	TIFF 
•	SVG 
•	ZIP 
•	PSD (preview only) 
________________________________________
5.4 File Analysis
Immediately after upload, analyze:
•	Page count 
•	Page size 
•	Portrait / Landscape pages 
•	Color page count 
•	Blank pages 
•	Image resolution 
•	Password protection 
•	Corruption 
This information is stored and reused throughout processing.
________________________________________
5.5 Print Rule Engine
Every uploaded file can contain multiple print instructions.
Example:
Assignment.pdf
Rule 1
•	Pages: 1–10 
•	B/W 
•	Single Side 
Rule 2
•	Pages: 11–20 
•	Duplex 
Rule 3
•	Pages: 21–25 
•	Color 
Rule 4
•	Pages: 26–40 
•	Duplex 
•	2 Pages Per Sheet 
The engine processes each rule independently before combining them into the final order.
________________________________________
5.6 Automatic Duplex Logic
Customers only choose:
•	Single Side 
•	Double Side 
The software determines the correct printer setting.
Rules:
•	Final printed sheet is Portrait → Flip on Long Edge. 
•	Final printed sheet is Landscape → Flip on Short Edge. 
The decision is based on the final output layout, not the original uploaded document.
Examples:
•	Landscape PDF → 2 pages per sheet → Final output Portrait → Use Long Edge. 
•	Portrait PDF → 2 pages per sheet → Final output Landscape → Use Short Edge (if applicable). 
The customer never sees or configures flip direction.
________________________________________
5.7 N-up Engine
Supported layouts:
•	1 
•	2 
•	4 
•	6 
•	8 
•	9 
•	16 pages per sheet 
Responsibilities:
•	Arrange pages correctly. 
•	Preserve reading order. 
•	Respect orientation. 
•	Update sheet count. 
•	Update preview. 
•	Update pricing. 
________________________________________
5.8 Image Layout Engine
Supported layouts:
•	1 image 
•	2 images 
•	4 images 
•	6 images 
•	9 images 
•	16 images per page 
Options:
•	Fit 
•	Fill 
•	Stretch 
•	Maintain aspect ratio 
•	Auto rotate 
•	Borderless (if printer supports it) 
•	Margins 
•	Spacing 
________________________________________
5.9 PowerPoint Engine
Support:
•	1 slide 
•	2 slides 
•	3 slides 
•	4 slides 
•	6 slides 
•	9 slides per page 
Preview should closely match Microsoft PowerPoint handout layouts.
________________________________________
5.10 ID Card Layout Engine
Provide templates for:
•	Aadhaar 
•	PAN 
•	Driving Licence 
•	Passport 
•	Voter ID 
Customer uploads front and back images.
The system automatically positions them correctly on the page. Operators should not need to manually align them.
________________________________________
5.11 Preview Generator
The preview must represent the final printed result after all processing.
It must reflect:
•	Paper size 
•	Orientation 
•	N-up layout 
•	Image layout 
•	Slide layout 
•	Margins 
•	Scaling 
•	Binding margin 
•	Watermarks 
•	Headers/Footers 
The preview should be regenerated whenever a print setting changes.
________________________________________
5.12 Print-Ready PDF Generator
The final output sent to the Windows Print Agent should be a print-ready PDF.
The generator must apply:
•	Page ranges 
•	Mixed print rules 
•	Duplex layout 
•	N-up 
•	Image layouts 
•	Slide layouts 
•	Scaling 
•	Rotation 
No additional processing should be required by the print agent.
________________________________________
5.13 Error Handling
If processing fails:
•	Keep the original uploaded file. 
•	Preserve the customer's settings. 
•	Record the error. 
•	Inform the customer and operator. 
•	Allow retry after correction where possible. 
________________________________________
5.14 Performance Targets
Suggested goals:
•	Preview generation: < 2 seconds for typical documents. 
•	Office conversion: As fast as practical for document size. 
•	Print-ready PDF generation: Optimized for large jobs. 
•	Background processing for lengthy operations to keep the UI responsive. 
________________________________________
5.15 Future Enhancements
The engine should be extensible for:
•	AI-recommended print settings. 
•	OCR for scanned PDFs. 
•	Automatic blank-page removal. 
•	Automatic color-page detection with customer confirmation. 
•	Watermarking. 
•	Booklet printing. 
•	Book binding margins. 
•	Poster printing across multiple sheets. 
•	QR code insertion. 
•	Barcode generation. 
________________________________________
Chapter Summary
The Print Processing Engine is the foundation of Patel AutoPrint. Every uploaded document flows through a standardized pipeline that analyzes, transforms, previews, prices, and prepares files for printing. By separating processing into independent modules, the system remains scalable, maintainable, and adaptable to future features without major architectural changes.

Chapter 6 – Windows Print Agent & Automatic Printer Management
________________________________________
6.1 Purpose
The Windows Print Agent is a lightweight desktop application installed on the print shop's computer.
It runs silently in the background and securely connects the cloud platform with the shop's local printers.
The operator should never need to manually download files or open documents to print them.
The Print Agent receives approved jobs, prepares them if needed, sends them to the selected printer, and reports the result back to the cloud.
________________________________________
6.2 Core Responsibilities
The Windows Print Agent must:
•	Connect securely to the cloud. 
•	Authenticate with the shop account. 
•	Discover installed printers. 
•	Monitor printer availability. 
•	Receive approved jobs. 
•	Download print-ready PDFs. 
•	Print automatically. 
•	Report success or errors. 
•	Retry failed jobs when appropriate. 
•	Synchronize printer status. 
________________________________________
6.3 Installation
Each shop installs the Print Agent on one or more Windows computers.
During installation:
1.	Operator signs in with shop credentials. 
2.	Agent registers the computer. 
3.	Agent generates a unique Agent ID. 
4.	Agent scans all installed printers. 
5.	Agent uploads printer information to the cloud. 
6.	Agent starts automatically with Windows. 
________________________________________
6.4 Background Operation
The Print Agent should:
•	Start automatically when Windows starts. 
•	Run silently in the system tray. 
•	Consume minimal CPU and memory. 
•	Continue operating if no user is logged into the dashboard. 
•	Automatically reconnect after temporary network interruptions. 
________________________________________
6.5 Printer Discovery
At startup and whenever requested, the agent should detect all available printers.
For each printer, collect:
•	Printer Name 
•	Driver Name 
•	Printer Type (B/W, Color, Photo, Plotter if available) 
•	Supported Paper Sizes 
•	Duplex Capability 
•	Online / Offline Status 
•	Default Printer 
•	Current Queue Length (if available) 
The operator can edit or categorize printers after discovery.
________________________________________
6.6 Printer Categories
Printers should be assigned to categories such as:
•	B/W Laser 
•	Color Laser 
•	Inkjet 
•	Photo Printer 
•	Large Format / Plotter 
These categories help the routing engine recommend the correct printer.
________________________________________
6.7 Printer Registration
Each printer registered with the cloud stores:
•	Printer Name 
•	Friendly Display Name 
•	Category 
•	Supported Paper Sizes 
•	Duplex Support 
•	Status 
•	Priority 
•	Assigned Agent 
The shop owner may rename printers for clarity (e.g., "Front Counter Canon" instead of the Windows device name).
________________________________________
6.8 Automatic Printer Recommendation
When an operator opens an order, the system recommends the most appropriate printer.
Example:
Recommended Printer

Canon iR-ADV 6575

Reason:

✓ Supports A4
✓ Supports Duplex
✓ Configured for B/W
✓ Currently Online
The recommendation should consider:
•	Color vs. B/W 
•	Paper size 
•	Duplex support 
•	Printer status 
•	Queue length (future) 
•	Shop routing rules 
________________________________________
6.9 Manual Printer Override
The operator may change the recommended printer before approval.
This is useful when:
•	A printer is under maintenance. 
•	One printer has a long queue. 
•	A higher-quality printer is preferred. 
•	The shop has multiple identical printers. 
Overrides should be logged for auditing.
________________________________________
6.10 Automatic Printer Routing
The shop owner can define routing rules.
Examples:
•	Color → Konica Bizhub 
•	B/W → Canon iR-ADV 
•	Photo → Epson 
•	A3 → Canon A3 
•	Legal → HP LaserJet 
When an order is approved, the routing engine automatically selects the best printer according to these rules.
________________________________________
6.11 Multiple Printer Support
A shop may have any number of printers.
Examples:
•	2 B/W printers 
•	2 Color printers 
•	1 Photo printer 
•	1 Plotter 
The system must support unlimited printers, subject to the shop's subscription plan.
________________________________________
6.12 Multiple Windows Agents
Some shops operate multiple computers.
The platform must support multiple Print Agents under the same shop.
Example:
Computer 1

Canon A

Canon B

Computer 2

Konica

Epson
The cloud routes jobs to the appropriate agent based on the assigned printer.
________________________________________
6.13 Print Queue
Each printer maintains its own queue.
Possible statuses:
•	Waiting 
•	Downloading 
•	Preparing 
•	Ready 
•	Printing 
•	Completed 
•	Failed 
•	Cancelled 
Operators can monitor queue progress from the dashboard.
________________________________________
6.14 Retry Logic
If printing fails because of a temporary issue (e.g., printer offline or network interruption):
•	Mark the job as "Retry Pending." 
•	Retry according to configurable limits. 
•	Notify the operator if retries are exhausted. 
Permanent failures should require operator intervention.
________________________________________
6.15 Printer Status Monitoring
The Print Agent should periodically report:
•	Online / Offline 
•	Idle / Printing 
•	Current queue length (if available) 
•	Last heartbeat 
•	Last successful print 
•	Agent version 
Where printer drivers expose additional information, toner or paper status may also be displayed.
________________________________________
6.16 Security
The Print Agent must:
•	Authenticate securely with the cloud. 
•	Encrypt communication. 
•	Accept jobs only for its registered shop. 
•	Verify downloaded files before printing. 
•	Avoid exposing local file paths or sensitive information. 
________________________________________
6.17 Logging
The Print Agent should maintain local logs for troubleshooting.
Log events include:
•	Agent startup 
•	Login 
•	Printer discovery 
•	Job download 
•	Job printed 
•	Print failure 
•	Retry 
•	Network errors 
•	Software updates 
Logs should be viewable from the application and exportable for support.
________________________________________
6.18 Automatic Updates
The agent should support automatic updates.
When a new version is available:
•	Download in the background. 
•	Verify the package. 
•	Install during an idle period or after operator confirmation. 
•	Restart the agent if required. 
________________________________________
6.19 Offline Mode
If the internet connection is lost:
•	Finish printing any jobs already downloaded. 
•	Pause fetching new jobs. 
•	Continue monitoring printers. 
•	Reconnect automatically when the connection returns. 
________________________________________
6.20 Future Enhancements
Potential future capabilities:
•	Load balancing across multiple printers. 
•	Automatic rerouting if a printer fails. 
•	Printer maintenance scheduling. 
•	Predictive failure alerts. 
•	Cross-platform print agents (Linux/macOS). 
•	Remote diagnostics. 
________________________________________
6.21 Chapter Summary
The Windows Print Agent is the bridge between the cloud platform and the physical print shop. It automates printer discovery, job retrieval, routing, printing, and status reporting while minimizing manual work for operators. It is designed to support multiple printers, multiple computers, and future expansion without requiring changes to the core cloud platform.

11.31 Real Print Shop Rules (Very Important)
These behaviors should be built into the software because they reflect real-world shop operations:
Rule 1
A single order may contain dozens of files, each with different print settings.
Rule 2
A single file may have multiple print rules.
Rule 3
Pricing should always reflect the final printed output according to the shop's configured pricing model.
Rule 4
The preview should match the actual printed result as closely as possible.
Rule 5
The system should reduce operator work, not add more steps.
Rule 6
The customer should not need to understand printer terminology.
Rule 7
Every complex operation should have a simple interface.
Rule 8
No document should be modified permanently. Always preserve the original upload.
Rule 9

Rule 10
Every significant action should be logged for auditing and troubleshooting.

•	Logging

12.10 Error Handling
Every module should return structured errors.
Example categories:
•	Validation Error 
•	Authentication Error 
•	File Error 
•	Printer Error 
•	Payment Error 
•	Internal Server Error 
Never expose stack traces to customers.
________________________________________

•	Upload

•	Approval 
•	Printing 
•	Payment 
•	Errors

•	JWT Authentication 
•	Password Hashing 
•	File Validation 
•	Upload Limits 
•	Rate Limiting 
•	CSRF protection where applicable 
•	Secure HTTP headers 
________________________________________
12.13 Performance Goals
Target:
•	Dashboard Load < 2 sec 
•	Preview < 2 sec (typical documents)

input.content:
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// MULTI-TENANT CORE
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  name          String
  ownerName     String
  slug          String   @unique
  address       String?
  gstNumber     String?
  contactNumber String?
  email         String?
  logo          String?
  theme         Json?
  currency      String   @default("INR")
  timeZone      String   @default("Asia/Kolkata")
  status        ShopStatus @default(ACTIVE)
  subscription  SubscriptionPlan @default(TRIAL)
  subscriptionExpiry DateTime?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt

  users         User[]
  customers     Customer[]
  printers      Printer[]
  agents        WindowsPrintAgent[]
  pricingRules  PricingRule[]
  orders        Order[]
  auditLogs     AuditLog[]
  notifications Notification[]
  branding      ShopBranding?

  @@map("shops")
}

enum ShopStatus {
  ACTIVE
  SUSPENDED
  TRIAL
  INACTIVE
}

enum SubscriptionPlan {
  TRIAL
  STARTER
  PROFESSIONAL
  ENTERPRISE
}

// ============================================
// AUTHENTICATION & USERS
// ============================================

model User {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId        String
  name          String
  email         String
  mobileNumber  String?
  passwordHash  String
  role          UserRole
  status        UserStatus @default(ACTIVE)
  lastLogin     DateTime?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  deletedAt     DateTime?

  shop          Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  orders        Order[]  @relation("OperatorOrders")
  auditLogs     AuditLog[]

  @@unique([shopId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

enum UserRole {
  SUPER_ADMIN
  SHOP_OWNER
  MANAGER
  OPERATOR
}

enum UserStatus {
  ACTIVE
  INACTIVE
  LOCKED
}

// ============================================
// CUSTOMERS
// ============================================

model Customer {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId        String
  name          String
  mobileNumber  String
  email         String?
  address       String?
  loyaltyPoints Int      @default(0)
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt

  shop          Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  orders        Order[]

  @@unique([shopId, mobileNumber])
  @@map("customers")
}

// ============================================
// ORDERS
// ============================================

model Order {
  id                    String   @id @default(uuid())
  publicOrderNumber     String   @unique
  shopId                String
  customerId            String
  status                OrderStatus @default(UPLOADED)
  paymentStatus         PaymentStatus @default(UNPAID)
  totalAmount           Float    @default(0)
  estimatedCompletionTime Int?
  customerNotes         String?
  operatorNotes         String?
  createdAt             DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt             DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt            DateTime?
  printingAt            DateTime?
  completedAt           DateTime?
  cancelledAt           DateTime?

  shop                  Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  customer              Customer @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])
  operator              User?    @relation("OperatorOrders", fields: [operatorId], references: [id])
  operatorId            String?
  files                 OrderFile[]
  printInstructions     PrintInstruction[]
  payments              Payment[]
  priceSnapshot         PriceSnapshot?

  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@index([shopId, createdAt])
  @@map("orders")
}

enum OrderStatus {
  UPLOADED
  PROCESSING
  WAITING_PAYMENT
  WAITING_APPROVAL
  APPROVED
  HOLD
  PRINTING
  COMPLETED
  READY_FOR_PICKUP
  CANCELLED
  FAILED
}

enum PaymentStatus {
  UNPAID
  PAID
  REFUNDED
  PARTIALLY_REFUNDED
}

// ============================================
// ORDER FILES
// ============================================

model OrderFile {
  id                String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId           String
  fileName          String
  fileType          String
  originalPath      String
  convertedPdfPath  String?
  previewPath       String?
  thumbnailPath     String?
  pageCount         Int      @default(0)
  portraitPages     Int      @default(0)
  landscapePages    Int      @default(0)
  colorPageCount    Int      @default(0)
  blankPageCount    Int      @default(0)
  isPasswordProtected Boolean @default(false)
  isCorrupted       Boolean  @default(false)
  imageResolution   Json?
  fileSize          Int      @default(0)
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt

  order             Order    @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  printInstructions PrintInstruction[]
  analysisResult    FileAnalysis?

  @@map("order_files")
}

// ============================================
// FILE ANALYSIS
// ============================================

model FileAnalysis {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderFileId     String   @unique
  pageCount       Int      @default(0)
  paperSize       String?
  portraitPages   Int      @default(0)
  landscapePages  Int      @default(0)
  colorPageCount  Int      @default(0)
  blankPageCount  Int      @default(0)
  imageResolution Json?
  unsupportedFonts String[]
  isPasswordProtected Boolean @default(false)
  isCorrupted     Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())

  orderFile       OrderFile @relation(fields: [orderFileId], references: [id])

  @@map("file_analyses")
}

// ============================================
// PRINT INSTRUCTIONS
// ============================================

model PrintInstruction {
  id                String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderFileId       String
  orderId           String
  ruleName          String?
  pageRange         String   @default("all")
  paperSize         PaperSize @default(A4)
  orientation       Orientation @default(AUTO)
  colorMode         ColorMode @default(AUTO)
  duplex            DuplexMode @default(SINGLE)
  copies            Int      @default(1)
  nUpLayout         Int      @default(1)
  scaling           Float    @default(100)
  bindingMargin     BindingMargin @default(NONE)
  watermark         String?
  header            String?
  footer            String?
  finalSheetCount   Int      @default(0)
  assignedPrinterId String?
  processingStatus  ProcessingStatus @default(PENDING)
  printReadyPdfPath String?
  previewPath       String?
  priority          Priority @default(NORMAL)
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt

  orderFile         OrderFile @relation(fields: [orderFileId], references: [id])
  order             Order     @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  assignedPrinter   Printer?  @relation(fields: [assignedPrinterId], references: [id])
  printJobs         PrintJob[]

  @@map("print_instructions")
}

enum PaperSize {
  A4
  A3
  LEGAL
  LETTER
  CUSTOM
}

enum Orientation {
  AUTO
  PORTRAIT
  LANDSCAPE
}

enum ColorMode {
  AUTO
  BLACK_WHITE
  COLOR
}

enum DuplexMode {
  SINGLE
  DUPLEX
}

enum BindingMargin {
  NONE
  LEFT
  RIGHT
  TOP
}

enum ProcessingStatus {
  PENDING
  ANALYZING
  CONVERTING
  GENERATING_PREVIEW
  CALCULATING_PRICE
  GENERATING_PRINT_READY
  COMPLETED
  FAILED
}

enum Priority {
  NORMAL
  HIGH
  URGENT
}

// ============================================
// PRINTERS
// ============================================

model Printer {
  id                String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId            String
  agentId           String?
  name              String
  displayName       String?
  category          PrinterCategory
  supportedPaperSizes PaperSize[]
  duplexSupport     Boolean  @default(false)
  status            PrinterStatus @default(OFFLINE)
  isDefault         Boolean  @default(false)
  priority          Int      @default(0)
  lastHeartbeat     DateTime?
  lastSuccessfulPrint DateTime?
  currentQueueLength Int      @default(0)
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt

  shop              Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  agent             WindowsPrintAgent? @relation(fields: [agentId], references: [id])
  printInstructions PrintInstruction[]
  printJobs         PrintJob[]

  @@map("printers")
}

enum PrinterCategory {
  BW_LASER
  COLOR_LASER
  INKJET
  PHOTO
  LARGE_FORMAT
}

enum PrinterStatus {
  ONLINE
  OFFLINE
  PRINTING
  ERROR
  LOW_TONER
  LOW_PAPER
}

// ============================================
// WINDOWS PRINT AGENTS
// ============================================

model WindowsPrintAgent {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId        String
  deviceName    String
  operatingSystem String
  version       String?
  lastHeartbeat DateTime?
  status        AgentStatus @default(OFFLINE)
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt

  shop          Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  printers      Printer[]
  printJobs     PrintJob[]

  @@map("windows_print_agents")
}

enum AgentStatus {
  ONLINE
  OFFLINE
  UPDATING
}

// ============================================
// PRINT JOBS
// ============================================

model PrintJob {
  id                String   @id @default(uuid())
  printInstructionId String
  printerId         String
  agentId           String
  status            PrintJobStatus @default(WAITING)
  retryCount        Int      @default(0)
  maxRetries        Int      @default(3)
  errorMessage      String?
  startedAt         DateTime?
  completedAt       DateTime?
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt

  printInstruction  PrintInstruction @relation(fields: [printInstructionId], references: [id])
  printer           Printer @relation(fields: [printerId], references: [id])
  agent             WindowsPrintAgent @relation(fields: [agentId], references: [id])

  @@map("print_jobs")
}

enum PrintJobStatus {
  WAITING
  DOWNLOADING
  PREPARING
  READY
  PRINTING
  COMPLETED
  FAILED
  CANCELLED
  RETRY_PENDING
}

// ============================================
// PRICING
// ============================================

model PricingRule {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId        String
  paperSize     PaperSize
  colorMode     ColorMode
  duplex        DuplexMode
  perSheetPrice Float
  perPagePrice  Float?
  minimumCharge Float    @default(0)
  isActive      Boolean  @default(true)
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt

  shop          Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@unique([shopId, paperSize, colorMode, duplex])
  @@map("pricing_rules")
}

model PriceSnapshot {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId       String   @unique
  unitPrices    Json
  discounts     Json?
  taxes         Json?
  subtotal      Float
  totalDiscount Float    @default(0)
  totalTax      Float    @default(0)
  finalTotal    Float
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

  order         Order    @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])

  @@map("price_snapshots")
}

// ============================================
// PAYMENTS
// ============================================

model Payment {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId         String
  method          PaymentMethod
  amount          Float
  status          PaymentRecordStatus @default(PENDING)
  gatewayReference String?
  gatewayResponse Json?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  order           Order    @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])

  @@map("payments")
}

enum PaymentMethod {
  UPI
  CARD
  CASH
  NET_BANKING
  WALLET
}

enum PaymentRecordStatus {
  PENDING
  SUCCESS
  FAILED
  REFUNDED
}

// ============================================
// NOTIFICATIONS
// ============================================

model Notification {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId        String
  type          NotificationType
  title         String
  message       String
  data          Json?
  isRead        Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

  shop          Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("notifications")
}

enum NotificationType {
  NEW_ORDER
  PAYMENT_RECEIVED
  ORDER_APPROVED
  PRINTING_STARTED
  READY_FOR_PICKUP
  ORDER_CANCELLED
  PRINTER_OFFLINE
  PRINT_FAILURE
  AGENT_DISCONNECTED
}

// ============================================
// SHOP BRANDING
// ============================================

model ShopBranding {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId          String   @unique
  primaryColor    String   @default("#1976d2")
  secondaryColor  String   @default("#dc004e")
  welcomeMessage  String?
  footerText      String?
  customCss       String?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  shop            Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("shop_brandings")
}

// ============================================
// AUDIT LOGS
// ============================================

model AuditLog {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId        String
  userId        String?
  action        String
  entity        String
  entityId      String?
  details       Json?
  ipAddress     String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

  shop          Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  user          User?    @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  @@index([shopId, createdAt])
  @@map("audit_logs")
}

input.content:
# Patel AutoPrint v2.0

Cloud-Based Multi-Tenant Print Shop Management & Automatic Printing Platform (SaaS)

## Tech Stack

### Backend
- Node.js + Express.js
- PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM
- JWT Authentication
- WebSocket (Real-time updates)
- PDF-Lib (PDF processing)
- Sharp (Image processing)

### Frontend
- React 18
- Material UI
- React Router
- React Query (TanStack Query)
- React Hook Form
- PDF.js (Preview)
- Tailwind CSS

### Print Agent
- Node.js (Windows)
- PowerShell (Printer discovery)
- Auto-update support

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+
- PostgreSQL 14+
- Redis (for job queues)

### Installation

1. Clone the repository
```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd patel-autoprint
```

2. Install dependencies
```bash
npm install
```

3. Set up environment
```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
# Edit backend/.env with your database credentials
```

4. Initialize database
```bash
cd backend
npx prisma migrate dev
npm run db:seed
```

5. Start development servers
```bash
# From root directory
npm run dev
```

This starts both backend (port 5000) and frontend (port 5173).

### Demo Credentials

After seeding:
- **Shop Owner:** admin@patelxerox.com / admin123
- **Manager:** manager@patelxerox.com / manager123
- **Operator:** operator@patelxerox.com / operator123

## Project Structure

```
patel-autoprint/
├── backend/           # Express.js API server
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── controllers/
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── middleware/
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   ├── utils/
│   │   └── server.js
│   └── prisma/
│       ├── schema.prisma
│       └── seed.js
├── frontend/          # React application
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── pages/
│   │   ├── components/
│   │   ├── layouts/
│   │   ├── contexts/
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   └── utils/
│   └── index.html
├── print-agent/       # Windows Print Agent
│   └── src/
│       └── index.js
└── shared/            # Shared types & constants
    ├── types/
    └── constants/
```

## API Endpoints

### Authentication
- `POST /api/v1/auth/register` - Register new shop
- `POST /api/v1/auth/login` - Login
- `GET /api/v1/auth/profile` - Get profile

### Orders
- `POST /api/v1/orders` - Create order
- `GET /api/v1/orders/queue` - Get order queue
- `GET /api/v1/orders/search` - Search orders
- `POST /api/v1/orders/:id/approve` - Approve order
- `POST /api/v1/orders/:id/hold` - Hold order
- `POST /api/v1/orders/:id/reject` - Reject order

### Files
- `POST /api/v1/files/upload/:orderId` - Upload files
- `GET /api/v1/files/order/:orderId` - Get order files
- `GET /api/v1/files/:fileId/analyze` - Analyze file

### Printers
- `GET /api/v1/printers` - List printers
- `POST /api/v1/printers` - Add printer
- `PUT /api/v1/printers/:id` - Update printer
- `DELETE /api/v1/printers/:id` - Delete printer

### Pricing
- `GET /api/v1/pricing` - List pricing rules
- `POST /api/v1/pricing` - Create pricing rule
- `POST /api/v1/pricing/calculate` - Calculate price

## Features

### Customer Portal
- Drag & drop file upload
- Multi-file support
- Independent print settings per file
- Mixed print rules
- Live preview
- Real-time pricing
- Multiple payment methods
- Order tracking
- Print again feature

### Admin Dashboard
- Real-time order queue
- Search by Order ID, Mobile, Name
- One-click approve/hold/reject
- Printer recommendation
- Revenue reports
- Customer management
- User management
- Pricing configuration

### Print Processing Engine
- Automatic file analysis
- Office document conversion
- N-up printing
- Image layouts
- PowerPoint layouts
- Duplex auto-detection
- Binding margins
- Watermarks
- Print-ready PDF generation

### Windows Print Agent
- Automatic printer discovery
- Silent printing
- Job queue management
- Retry logic
- Status monitoring
- Auto-update

## License

Proprietary - Patel AutoPrint

The **Patel AutoPrint v2.0** project has been fully scaffolded. Here's a summary:

## Project Structure Created

### Backend (Express.js + Prisma)
- **Database Schema**: 20+ models (Shop, User, Customer, Order, OrderFile, PrintInstruction, Printer, WindowsPrintAgent, PricingRule, Payment, Notification, etc.)
- **API Routes**: Auth, Shop, Customer, Order, File, Printer, Pricing, Payment, Admin, Agent
- **Services**: Auth, Order, File Analysis, Pricing, Printer, Print Processing, Notification
- **Middleware**: JWT Auth, RBAC, Validation, Error Handling
- **WebSocket**: Real-time order status updates
- **Seed Data**: Demo shop with printers, pricing rules, and users

### Frontend (React + Material UI)
- **Customer Portal**: Home, Upload, Configure, Preview, Payment, Order Tracking
- **Admin Dashboard**: Dashboard stats, Order Queue, Order Detail, Printers, Pricing, Customers, Users, Settings
- **Auth Pages**: Login, Register
- **Layouts**: Customer layout, Admin layout with sidebar navigation
- **Context**: AuthContext, ShopContext

### Windows Print Agent
- Printer discovery via PowerShell
- Job polling and silent printing
- Heartbeat and status reporting

### Shared
- TypeScript types for all entities
- Constants (enums, file types, paper sizes)

## To Run

```bash
cd patel-autoprint
npm install
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
cd backend
npx prisma migrate dev
npm run db:seed
cd ..
npm run dev
```

display.text:
# Patel AutoPrint v2.0

Cloud-Based Multi-Tenant Print Shop Management & Automatic Printing Platform (SaaS)

## Tech Stack

### Backend
- Node.js + Express.js
- PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM
- JWT Authentication
- WebSocket (Real-time updates)
- PDF-Lib (PDF processing)
- Sharp (Image processing)

### Frontend
- React 18
- Material UI
- React Router
- React Query (TanStack Query)
- React Hook Form
- PDF.js (Preview)
- Tailwind CSS

### Print Agent
- Node.js (Windows)
- PowerShell (Printer discovery)
- Auto-update support

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+
- PostgreSQL 14+
- Redis (for job queues)

### Installation

1. Clone the repository
```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd patel-autoprint
```

2. Install dependencies
```bash
npm install
```

3. Set up environment
```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
# Edit backend/.env with your database credentials
```

4. Initialize database
```bash
cd backend
npx prisma migrate dev
npm run db:seed
```

5. Start development servers
```bash
# From root directory
npm run dev
```

This starts both backend (port 5000) and frontend (port 5173).

### Demo Credentials

After seeding:
- **Shop Owner:** admin@patelxerox.com / admin123
- **Manager:** manager@patelxerox.com / manager123
- **Operator:** operator@patelxerox.com / operator123

## Project Structure

```
patel-autoprint/
├── backend/           # Express.js API server
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── controllers/
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── middleware/
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   ├── utils/
│   │   └── server.js
│   └── prisma/
│       ├── schema.prisma
│       └── seed.js
├── frontend/          # React application
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── pages/
│   │   ├── components/
│   │   ├── layouts/
│   │   ├── contexts/
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   └── utils/
│   └── index.html
├── print-agent/       # Windows Print Agent
│   └── src/
│       └── index.js
└── shared/            # Shared types & constants
    ├── types/
    └── constants/
```

## API Endpoints

### Authentication
- `POST /api/v1/auth/register` - Register new shop
- `POST /api/v1/auth/login` - Login
- `GET /api/v1/auth/profile` - Get profile

### Orders
- `POST /api/v1/orders` - Create order
- `GET /api/v1/orders/queue` - Get order queue
- `GET /api/v1/orders/search` - Search orders
- `POST /api/v1/orders/:id/approve` - Approve order
- `POST /api/v1/orders/:id/hold` - Hold order
- `POST /api/v1/orders/:id/reject` - Reject order

### Files
- `POST /api/v1/files/upload/:orderId` - Upload files
- `GET /api/v1/files/order/:orderId` - Get order files
- `GET /api/v1/files/:fileId/analyze` - Analyze file

### Printers
- `GET /api/v1/printers` - List printers
- `POST /api/v1/printers` - Add printer
- `PUT /api/v1/printers/:id` - Update printer
- `DELETE /api/v1/printers/:id` - Delete printer

### Pricing
- `GET /api/v1/pricing` - List pricing rules
- `POST /api/v1/pricing` - Create pricing rule
- `POST /api/v1/pricing/calculate` - Calculate price

## Features

### Customer Portal
- Drag & drop file upload
- Multi-file support
- Independent print settings per file
- Mixed print rules
- Live preview
- Real-time pricing
- Multiple payment methods
- Order tracking
- Print again feature

### Admin Dashboard
- Real-time order queue
- Search by Order ID, Mobile, Name
- One-click approve/hold/reject
- Printer recommendation
- Revenue reports
- Customer management
- User management
- Pricing configuration

### Print Processing Engine
- Automatic file analysis
- Office document conversion
- N-up printing
- Image layouts
- PowerPoint layouts
- Duplex auto-detection
- Binding margins
- Watermarks
- Print-ready PDF generation

### Windows Print Agent
- Automatic printer discovery
- Silent printing
- Job queue management

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// CORE MODELS
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  name      String
  settings  Json?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  users         User[]
  customers     Customer[]
  orders        Order[]
  printers      Printer[]
  pricingRules  PricingRule[]
  orderFiles    OrderFile[]
  printJobs     PrintJob[]

  @@map("shops")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId       String
  email        String
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("OPERATOR") // OWNER, MANAGER, OPERATOR, CUSTOMER
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@unique([shopId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId    String
  name      String
  phone     String?
  email     String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  shop   Shop    @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  orders Order[]

  @@map("customers")
}

model Order {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  customerId    String?
  shopId        String
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, APPROVED, PRINTING, COMPLETED, REJECTED
  paymentStatus String   @default("UNPAID")  // UNPAID, PAID, REFUNDED
  paymentMethod String?
  totalPrice    Float    @default(0)
  discount      Float    @default(0)
  tax           Float    @default(0)
  notes         String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt    DateTime?
  printedAt     DateTime?

  shop      Shop        @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  customer  Customer?   @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])
  files     OrderFile[]
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@index([shopId, createdAt])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderFile {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId       String
  originalName  String
  storagePath   String
  fileType      String
  size          Int
  pageCount     Int      @default(0)
  colorPageCount Int     @default(0)
  orientation   String   @default("portrait")
  settings      Json?
  shopId        String

  order    Order      @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  shop     Shop       @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@map("order_files")
}

model PrintJob {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId        String
  fileId         String
  sectionIndex   Int      @default(0)
  pages          String   // JSON array of page numbers
  colorMode      String   @default("auto")   // auto, bw, color
  printStyle     String   @default("single") // single, duplex
  paperSize      String   @default("A4")
  flipDirection  String   @default("long-edge")
  copies         Int      @default(1)
  status         String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, PROCESSING, COMPLETED, FAILED
  assignedPrinter String?
  shopId         String

  order     Order  @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  shop      Shop   @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("print_jobs")
}

model Printer {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  ip             String?
  paperSizes     Json     @default("[\"A4\"]")
  colorSupport   Boolean  @default(false)
  duplexSupport  Boolean  @default(false)
  status         String   @default("ONLINE") // ONLINE, OFFLINE, PRINTING, ERROR
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("printers")
}

model PricingRule {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  colorRate      Float    @default(10)
  bwRate         Float    @default(2)
  duplexDiscount Float    @default(20)
  nupDiscount    Float    @default(15)
  taxRate        Float    @default(18)
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("pricing_rules")
}

## Architecture

### frontend/package.json
Dependencies: react, react-dom, react-router-dom, @mui/material, @mui/icons-material, @emotion/react, @emotion/styled, axios, react-hot-toast, recharts
DevDeps: @vitejs/plugin-react, vite, @types/react, @types/react-dom

Clean HTML with error boundary script to catch runtime errors

### frontend/vite.config.js
React plugin, port 5173, proxy /api to http://localhost:5000

### frontend/src/index.css
Minimal CSS - NO @tailwind, NO @layer utilities. Just basic resets and scrollbar styles.

### frontend/src/main.jsx
React 18 createRoot with BrowserRouter, AuthProvider, ThemeProvider, CssBaseline, Toaster, ErrorBoundary

### frontend/src/utils/theme.js
MUI theme with primary blue (#1976d2), clean modern look

### frontend/src/services/api.js
Axios instance with:
- baseURL: '/api'
- Request interceptor: adds Bearer token from localStorage
- Response interceptor: returns response.data (unwraps axios wrapper)
- On 401: clear localStorage, redirect to /login
- Error interceptor: rejects with error.response.data (the API envelope)

### frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx
- Stores user and token in state + localStorage
- login(email, password) → calls API, stores token+user
- register(data) → calls API, stores token+user
- logout() → clears storage
- useEffect: on mount, restore from localStorage and verify with /api/auth/profile
- Exports: useAuth() hook returning {user, loading, login, register, logout, isAuthenticated}

2. **RegisterPage.jsx** - Name/email/password form, register button, link to login

3. **CustomerPortal.jsx** - Main customer page with 4 steps:
   - Step 1: Upload - drag & drop zone, customer name/phone/email fields, "Upload & Analyze" button

   - Step 3: Preview & Pay - show price breakdown, payment method selection (Cash/Card/UPI/Online), "Place Order" button
   - Step 4: Confirmation - show order ID, status, "Place New Order" button

4. **OrderTracking.jsx** - Customer enters order ID, sees order status and details

5. **AdminLayout.jsx** - Sidebar with navigation: Dashboard, Orders, Printers, Pricing, Settings. Top bar with "View Store" button
6. **DashboardPage.jsx** - Stats cards (total orders, pending, printing, completed, revenue) + recent orders table

11. **OrderStatusBadge.jsx** - Colored badge component for order status

## Design Guidelines:
- Clean, modern UI with MUI components
- Customer portal should feel like a simple 4-step wizard (not overwhelming)
- Admin dashboard should be functional and fast
- Use React state for the wizard (no URL routing for steps)
- Use proper loading states and error handling with toast notifications
- Customer portal does NOT require login (walk-in customer model)
- Admin pages require login
- Price amounts are in ₹ (Indian Rupees)

1. NO @tailwind in CSS
2. Every import must be valid
3. The API interceptor returns response.data (axios wrapper stripped). Consumers get the API envelope {success, data, ...}. So to get the actual data: `const result = await api.get(...); const data = result.data;` because `result` is already the API envelope after the interceptor.

1. **Data field name mismatch**: The backend uses `totalPrice` but the frontend references `totalAmount` (DashboardPage line 69, OrderQueuePage line 168)
2. **Order ID field mismatch**: The backend returns `id` but the frontend references `_id` throughout3. **Status values mismatch**: Backend uses `APPROVED` but frontend checks for `confirmed`

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// CORE MODELS
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  name      String
  settings  Json?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  users         User[]
  customers     Customer[]
  orders        Order[]
  printers      Printer[]
  pricingRules  PricingRule[]
  orderFiles    OrderFile[]
  printJobs     PrintJob[]

  @@map("shops")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId       String
  email        String
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("OPERATOR") // OWNER, MANAGER, OPERATOR, CUSTOMER
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@unique([shopId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId    String
  name      String
  phone     String?
  email     String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  shop   Shop    @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  orders Order[]

  @@map("customers")
}

model Order {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  customerId    String?
  shopId        String
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, APPROVED, PRINTING, COMPLETED, REJECTED
  paymentStatus String   @default("UNPAID")  // UNPAID, PAID, REFUNDED
  paymentMethod String?
  totalPrice    Float    @default(0)
  discount      Float    @default(0)
  tax           Float    @default(0)
  notes         String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt    DateTime?
  printedAt     DateTime?

  shop      Shop        @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  customer  Customer?   @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])
  files     OrderFile[]
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@index([shopId, createdAt])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderFile {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId       String
  originalName  String
  storagePath   String
  fileType      String
  size          Int
  pageCount     Int      @default(0)
  colorPageCount Int     @default(0)
  orientation   String   @default("portrait")
  settings      Json?
  shopId        String

  order    Order      @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  shop     Shop       @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@map("order_files")
}

model PrintJob {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId        String
  fileId         String
  sectionIndex   Int      @default(0)
  pages          String   // JSON array of page numbers
  colorMode      String   @default("auto")   // auto, bw, color
  printStyle     String   @default("single") // single, duplex
  paperSize      String   @default("A4")
  flipDirection  String   @default("long-edge")
  copies         Int      @default(1)
  status         String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, PROCESSING, COMPLETED, FAILED
  assignedPrinter String?
  shopId         String

  order     Order     @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  file      OrderFile @relation(fields: [fileId], references: [id])
  shop      Shop      @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("print_jobs")
}

model Printer {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  ip             String?
  paperSizes     Json     @default("[\"A4\"]")
  colorSupport   Boolean  @default(false)
  duplexSupport  Boolean  @default(false)
  status         String   @default("ONLINE") // ONLINE, OFFLINE, PRINTING, ERROR
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("printers")
}

model PricingRule {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  colorRate      Float    @default(10)
  bwRate         Float    @default(2)
  duplexDiscount Float    @default(20)
  nupDiscount    Float    @default(15)
  taxRate        Float    @default(18)
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("pricing_rules")
}

parts.text:
The frontend code looks correct. The issue is most likely that:

1. **Printer discovery was blocking the event loop** - `execSync` was being used, which blocks ALL Node.js operations. When the Printers page loaded, it called `GET /api/printers`, which called `discoverPrinters()` synchronously, blocking the server for up to 10 seconds. During that time, ALL other requests (including the approve request) would be queued or fail. This is the root cause of both issues:
   - "Can't add printer" = The server was busy doing printer discovery
   - "Internal error on approve" = The server was blocked by printer discovery, causing a timeout or crash

2. I already fixed the printer discovery to use async `exec()` instead of `execSync`. This should fix both issues.

Now let me rebuild the frontend and restart the backend.

The root cause of both issues is clear now: **`execSync` in `discoverPrinters()` was blocking the entire Node.js event loop**. When the Printers page loaded, `GET /api/printers` would block the server for up to 10 seconds. During that time:
- Any "Add Printer" request would timeout/hang
- Any "Approve" request would also hang → "internal error"

My fix (async `exec` with caching) resolves both. Let me rebuild and restart:

All fixed. Here's what was wrong:

**Root cause of both "can't add printer" and "internal error on approve":**
1. **`execSync` blocking the event loop** — `discoverPrinters()` used synchronous `execSync` to run PowerShell, freezing the entire Node.js server for up to 10 seconds per request. Any other request during that time would timeout.
2. **`orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }` on Printer model** — the Printer schema has no `createdAt` field, causing a Prisma validation error → 500 on the printers page.

**Fixes applied:**
- `backend/src/services/printer.js`: Replaced `execSync` with async `exec` + promise wrapper, added 30-second caching to avoid re-discovering on every request
- `backend/src/server.js`: Changed printer query to `orderBy: { name: 'asc' }` (Printer has no `createdAt`)
- `backend/src/services/printProcessor.js`: `processAndDispatchOrder` now handles JSON array format `"[0]"` stored in `printJob.pages`, plus better error handling for individual print job failures
- `backend/src/middleware/errorHandler.js`: Added `err.stack` to error logs for debugging

162: function Step2Configure({ files, fileSettings, setFileSettings }) {

169:     const localSettings = fileSettings[fileIndex] || {};
170:     return { ...dbSettings, ...localSettings };
171:   };
172: 
173:   const updateSetting = (fileIndex, key, value) => {
174:     setFileSettings((prev) => ({
175:       ...prev,
176:       [fileIndex]: { ...prev[fileIndex], [key]: value },
177:     }));
178:   };

180:   const addSection = (fileIndex) => {
181:     const current = getSettings(fileIndex);
182:     const sections = current.sections || [];
183:     const totalPages = files[fileIndex]?.pageCount || 1;
184:     const lastSection = sections[sections.length - 1];

186:     if (startPage > totalPages) {
187:       toast.error('No more pages available');
188:       return;

191:       id: Date.now(),

206:     updateSetting(fileIndex, 'sections', sections);
207:   };

512: export default function CustomerPortal() {
513:   const [activeStep, setActiveStep] = useState(0);
514:   const [files, setFiles] = useState([]);
515:   const [customerInfo, setCustomerInfo] = useState({ name: '', phone: '', email: '' });
516:   const [fileSettings, setFileSettings] = useState({});
517:   const [uploadedOrder, setUploadedOrder] = useState(null);
518:   const [paymentMethod, setPaymentMethod] = useState('cash');
519:   const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
520:   const [priceData, setPriceData] = useState(null);
521:   const [loadingPrice, setLoadingPrice] = useState(false);
522:   const theme = useTheme();
523:   const isMobile = useMediaQuery(theme.breakpoints.down('sm'));
524: 
525:   const handleUpload = async () => {
526:     if (files.length === 0) { toast.error('Please select files'); return; }
527:     if (!customerInfo.name || !customerInfo.phone) { toast.error('Please fill name and phone'); return; }
528:     setLoading(true);
529:     try {
530:       const formData = new FormData();
531:       files.forEach((f) => formData.append('files', f));
532:       formData.append('customerName', customerInfo.name);
533:       formData.append('customerPhone', customerInfo.phone);
534:       formData.append('customerEmail', customerInfo.email);
535: 
536:       const result = await api.post('/guest/upload', formData, {
537:         headers: { 'Content-Type': 'multipart/form-data' },
538:       });
539:       if (result.success) {
540:         setUploadedOrder(result.data);
541:         toast.success(`${result.data.files?.length || 0} file(s) analyzed!`);
542:         setActiveStep(1);
543:       }
544:     } catch (err) {
545:       toast.error(err.message || 'Upload failed');
546:     } finally {
547:       setLoading(false);
548:     }
549:   };
550: 
551:   const handleSaveSettings = async () => {
552:     if (!uploadedOrder) return;
553:     setLoading(true);
554:     try {
555:       for (const [fileIndex, settings] of Object.entries(fileSettings)) {
556:         const fileId = uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.id;
557:         if (fileId) {
558:           await api.put(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/settings`, {
559:             fileId,
560:             settings: { ...uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.settings, ...settings },
561:           });
562:         }
563:       }
564:       const updated = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}`);
565:       if (updated.success) setUploadedOrder(updated.data);
566:       toast.success('Settings saved!');
567:       setActiveStep(2);
568:     } catch (err) {
569:       toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to save settings');
570:     } finally {
571:       setLoading(false);
572:     }
573:   };
574: 
575:   const fetchPrice = async () => {
576:     if (!uploadedOrder) return;
577:     setLoadingPrice(true);
578:     try {
579:       const result = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/price`);
580:       if (result.success) setPriceData(result.data);
581:     } catch (err) {
582:       toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to get price');
583:     } finally {
584:       setLoadingPrice(false);
585:     }
586:   };
587: 
588:   useEffect(() => {
589:     if (activeStep === 2 && uploadedOrder) fetchPrice();
590:   }, [activeStep, uploadedOrder?.id]);
591: 
592:   const handlePlaceOrder = async () => {
593:     if (!uploadedOrder || !paymentMethod) { toast.error('Select payment method'); return; }
594:     setLoading(true);
595:     try {
596:       const result = await api.post(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/confirm`, { paymentMethod });
597:       if (result.success) {
598:         setUploadedOrder(result.data);
599:         toast.success('Order placed!');
600:         setActiveStep(3);
601:       }
602:     } catch (err) {
603:       toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to place order');
604:     } finally {
605:       setLoading(false);
606:     }
607:   };
608: 
609:   const handleNext = async () => {
610:     if (activeStep === 0) await handleUpload();
611:     else if (activeStep === 1) await handleSaveSettings();
612:     else if (activeStep === 2) await handlePlaceOrder();
613:   };
614: 
615:   const handleBack = () => setActiveStep((prev) => prev - 1);
616: 
617:   const handleNewOrder = () => {
618:     setActiveStep(0);
619:     setFiles([]);
620:     setCustomerInfo({ name: '', phone: '', email: '' });
621:     setFileSettings({});
622:     setUploadedOrder(null);
623:     setPaymentMethod('cash');
624:     setPriceData(null);
625:   };
626: 
627:   return (
628:     <Container maxWidth="sm" sx={{ py: { xs: 2, sm: 4 }, px: { xs: 1.5, sm: 3 } }}>
629:       <Typography variant="h5" align="center" gutterBottom sx={{ fontWeight: 700, fontSize: { xs: '1.4rem', sm: '1.8rem' } }}>

## ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS

**The bug is in `api.js` line 6.** Here is the exact chain of events:

1. **api.js** creates an axios instance with a hardcoded default header:
   ```javascript
   headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
   ```

2. When `CustomerPortal.jsx` calls `api.post('/guest/upload', formData)`, it passes a `FormData` object as the body. Normally, axios automatically detects that the body is a `FormData` instance and sets the `Content-Type` header to `multipart/form-data; boundary=----...` (with the correct boundary string).

3. **However**, because the axios instance already has a default `Content-Type: application/json` header, axios uses that default instead of auto-detecting. The `Content-Type` is never overridden to `multipart/form-data`.

4. The request arrives at the Express server with `Content-Type: application/json` instead of `multipart/form-data`.

5. Express's `express.json()` middleware (line 61) tries to parse the body as JSON. It cannot parse binary multipart data, so the body comes through as empty/corrupted.

6. Multer's middleware runs but finds no multipart form data to parse. It produces an empty `req.files` array (or `undefined`).

7. The handler at line 466-467 checks `if (!req.files || req.files.length === 0)` and throws `AppError('No files uploaded', 400, 'NO_FILES')`.

**The fix** is to remove the hardcoded `'Content-Type': 'application/json'` from the axios default config in `api.js`. Axios handles Content-Type automatically based on the body type:
- String/object bodies get `application/json`
- `FormData` bodies get `multipart/form-data` with the correct boundary
- `URLSearchParams` bodies get `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`

Alternatively, if you need to keep the default for other calls, the upload handler should explicitly delete the Content-Type header before sending:
```javascript
const result = await api.post('/guest/upload', formData, {
  headers: { 'Content-Type': undefined }  // or 'multipart/form-data'
});
```
Setting it to `undefined` tells axios to remove the default and auto-detect from the FormData body.

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// CORE MODELS
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  name      String
  settings  Json?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  users         User[]
  customers     Customer[]
  orders        Order[]
  printers      Printer[]
  pricingRules  PricingRule[]
  orderFiles    OrderFile[]
  printJobs     PrintJob[]

  @@map("shops")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId       String
  email        String
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("OPERATOR") // OWNER, MANAGER, OPERATOR, CUSTOMER
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@unique([shopId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId    String
  name      String
  phone     String?
  email     String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  shop   Shop    @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  orders Order[]

  @@map("customers")
}

model Order {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  customerId    String?
  shopId        String
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, APPROVED, PRINTING, COMPLETED, REJECTED
  paymentStatus String   @default("UNPAID")  // UNPAID, PAID, REFUNDED
  paymentMethod String?
  totalPrice    Float    @default(0)
  discount      Float    @default(0)
  tax           Float    @default(0)
  notes         String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt    DateTime?
  printedAt     DateTime?

  shop      Shop        @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  customer  Customer?   @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])
  files     OrderFile[]
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@index([shopId, createdAt])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderFile {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId       String
  originalName  String
  storagePath   String
  fileType      String
  size          Int
  pageCount     Int      @default(0)
  colorPageCount Int     @default(0)
  orientation   String   @default("portrait")
  settings      Json?
  shopId        String

  order    Order      @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  shop     Shop       @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@map("order_files")
}

model PrintJob {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId        String
  fileId         String
  sectionIndex   Int      @default(0)
  pages          String   // JSON array of page numbers
  colorMode      String   @default("auto")   // auto, bw, color
  printStyle     String   @default("single") // single, duplex
  paperSize      String   @default("A4")
  flipDirection  String   @default("long-edge")
  copies         Int      @default(1)
  status         String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, PROCESSING, COMPLETED, FAILED
  assignedPrinter String?
  shopId         String

  order     Order     @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  file      OrderFile @relation(fields: [fileId], references: [id])
  shop      Shop      @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("print_jobs")
}

model Printer {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  ip             String?
  paperSizes     Json     @default("[\"A4\"]")
  colorSupport   Boolean  @default(false)
  duplexSupport  Boolean  @default(false)
  status         String   @default("ONLINE") // ONLINE, OFFLINE, PRINTING, ERROR
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("printers")
}

model PricingRule {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  colorRate      Float    @default(10)
  bwRate         Float    @default(2)
  duplexDiscount Float    @default(20)
  nupDiscount    Float    @default(15)
  taxRate        Float    @default(18)
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("pricing_rules")
}

async function createPrintJobsForFile(file, orderId, shopId, printers) {
  const s = file.settings || {};
  const sections = s.sections || [];
  
  if (sections.length > 0) {
    // Create one print job per section
    const jobs = [];
    for (const [index, section] of sections.entries()) {
      const pages = section.pageRange === 'all' || !section.pageRange
        ? Array.from({ length: file.pageCount }, (_, i) => i)
        : parsePageRange(section.pageRange, file.pageCount);
      
      // If section has startPage/endPage, use those
      let sectionPages;
      if (section.startPage && section.endPage) {
        sectionPages = [];
        for (let p = section.startPage - 1; p < section.endPage; p++) {
          sectionPages.push(p);
        }
      } else {
        sectionPages = pages;
      }
      
      const job = {
        orderId,
        fileId: file.id,
        sectionIndex: index,
        pages: JSON.stringify(sectionPages),
        colorMode: section.colorMode || s.colorMode || 'auto',
        printStyle: section.printStyle || s.printStyle || 'single',
        paperSize: section.paperSize || s.paperSize || 'A4',
        flipDirection: determineFlipDirection(
          file.orientation,

          section.pagesPerSheet || s.pagesPerSheet || 1,
          section.orientation || s.orientation
        ),
        copies: section.copies || s.copies || 1,
        shopId,
      };
      
      const routed = routeJob(job, printers);
      const printJob = await prisma.printJob.create({ data: routed });
      jobs.push(printJob);
    }
    return jobs;
  } else {
    // Original behavior - one print job per file

      ? Array.from({ length: file.pageCount }, (_, i) => i)

      shopId,
    };
    
    const routed = routeJob(job, printers);

    return [printJob];
  }
}

4. **Print dialog UX**: Should mimic the Windows print dialog experience (like right-click → print on images with layout options like 2, 4, 9 photos per page)

7. **Token system**: Each customer gets a numeric short token number, admin can search by token
8. **Payment**: Online QR code (admin can attach their own UPI QR), COD option
9. **Printer management**: Admin can add/configure printers, multiple B&W and color printers
