generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// CORE MODELS
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  name      String
  settings  Json?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  users         User[]
  customers     Customer[]
  orders        Order[]
  printers      Printer[]
  pricingRules  PricingRule[]
  orderFiles    OrderFile[]
  printJobs     PrintJob[]

  @@map("shops")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId       String
  email        String
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("OPERATOR") // OWNER, MANAGER, OPERATOR, CUSTOMER
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@unique([shopId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId    String
  name      String
  phone     String?
  email     String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  shop   Shop    @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  orders Order[]

  @@map("customers")
}

model Order {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  customerId    String?
  shopId        String
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, APPROVED, PRINTING, COMPLETED, REJECTED
  paymentStatus String   @default("UNPAID")  // UNPAID, PAID, REFUNDED
  paymentMethod String?
  totalPrice    Float    @default(0)
  discount      Float    @default(0)
  tax           Float    @default(0)
  notes         String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt    DateTime?
  printedAt     DateTime?

  shop      Shop        @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  customer  Customer?   @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])
  files     OrderFile[]
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@index([shopId, createdAt])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderFile {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId       String
  originalName  String
  storagePath   String
  fileType      String
  size          Int
  pageCount     Int      @default(0)
  colorPageCount Int     @default(0)
  orientation   String   @default("portrait")
  settings      Json?
  shopId        String

  order    Order      @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  shop     Shop       @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@map("order_files")
}

model PrintJob {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId        String
  fileId         String
  sectionIndex   Int      @default(0)
  pages          String   // JSON array of page numbers
  colorMode      String   @default("auto")   // auto, bw, color
  printStyle     String   @default("single") // single, duplex
  paperSize      String   @default("A4")
  flipDirection  String   @default("long-edge")
  copies         Int      @default(1)
  status         String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, PROCESSING, COMPLETED, FAILED
  assignedPrinter String?
  shopId         String

  order     Order     @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  file      OrderFile @relation(fields: [fileId], references: [id])
  shop      Shop      @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("print_jobs")
}

model Printer {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  ip             String?
  paperSizes     Json     @default("[\"A4\"]")
  colorSupport   Boolean  @default(false)
  duplexSupport  Boolean  @default(false)
  status         String   @default("ONLINE") // ONLINE, OFFLINE, PRINTING, ERROR
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("printers")
}

model PricingRule {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  colorRate      Float    @default(10)
  bwRate         Float    @default(2)
  duplexDiscount Float    @default(20)
  nupDiscount    Float    @default(15)
  taxRate        Float    @default(18)
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("pricing_rules")
}

Now I have a complete picture of the codebase. Let me implement all the changes:

1. **Pricing**: Change to simple per-page pricing:
   - B&W: ₹1/page (any print style)
   - Color single: ₹5/page
   - Color duplex: ₹10/page
   - Tax: 18% (configurable)

2. **Token system**: Add `token` field to Order model (auto-incrementing per shop numeric), display in UI

3. **Printer routing**: The `routeJob` function already routes by colorSupport, which is good. Just need to make sure it's working correctly.

4. **UPI QR**: Add `upiQrPath` field to Shop model, admin settings page to upload QR

Let me implement these changes.

For the pricing, the user's requirement is:
- B&W: ₹1 per page regardless of single/duplex
- Color single side: ₹5 per page
- Color duplex: ₹10 per page
- Tax: 18%

This means:
- Pricing is per-PAGE, not per-SHEET
- Duplex doesn't change B&W price (still ₹1/page)
- Duplex doubles the color price (₹5 → ₹10 per page)

The `calculateSheets` function needs to change:
- For B&W: totalPrice = totalPages * bwRate (no sheet calculation needed)
- For Color single: totalPrice = totalPages * colorRate
- For Color duplex: totalPrice = totalPages * (colorRate * 2)

Actually, let me think about this more carefully. The user says:
- B&W: ₹1 per page, no matter single or duplex
- Color single: ₹5 per page
- Color duplex: ₹10 per page

So "per page" means per PDF page, not per physical sheet. This simplifies things:
- B&W: charge = pageCount * 1
- Color single: charge = pageCount * 5
- Color duplex: charge = pageCount * 10
- N-up reduces the effective page count

Wait, N-up: if you put 2 pages on 1 sheet, you still pay for 2 pages. So N-up doesn't reduce the price either.

Actually, let me re-read the user's message:
- "one rs for one paper of black and white" - this sounds like per paper (sheet), not per page
- "if our one page goes we charge 1 rs for b/w" - ok, per page
- "colour we charge 5 rs for one page but in colour if there will be a duplex then 10 rs for one page and for single 5 rs"

So:
- B&W: ₹1 per PDF page (single or duplex doesn't matter)
- Color single: ₹5 per PDF page
- Color duplex: ₹10 per PDF page

This is simpler than the current "per sheet" model. Let me rewrite the pricing module.

Let me also check: what about N-up? If someone does 2-up (2 pages per sheet), they pay for 2 pages. If they do duplex + 2-up... the user didn't specify. Let me keep it simple: N-up reduces the page count that gets charged. Actually wait, re-reading:

"if our one page goes we charge 1 rs for b/w no matter its single side or duplex print"

So "one page" = one PDF page. They charge per PDF page, not per physical sheet. So N-up doesn't affect pricing. Let me make it: charge = PDF pages × rate per page.

Actually wait, that doesn't make business sense. If a customer uploads a 10-page document and does 2-up (5 sheets), the shop still uses 5 sheets of paper. With ₹1/page, they'd charge ₹10 for 10 pages on 5 sheets. That's ₹2/sheet, which is good profit.

If they do duplex (5 sheets for 10 pages), they'd charge ₹10 for 10 pages. Same.

If they do both (2-up + duplex = 3 sheets for 10 pages), still ₹10.

So the pricing is: totalPages × rate, where rate = ₹1 for B&W, ₹5 for color single, ₹10 for color duplex.

But what about when some pages are color and some are B&W? The user says "if there is color, 5/page single, 10/page duplex". So:
- B&W pages: ₹1 each
- Color pages (single): ₹5 each
- Color pages (duplex): ₹10 each

Total = (bwPages × 1) + (colorSinglePages × 5) + (colorDuplexPages × 10)

Wait, but the user said the shop charges per page based on the print style. Let me simplify:
- If colorMode is 'bw': ₹1 × totalPages
- If colorMode is 'color' and printStyle is 'single': ₹5 × totalPages
- If colorMode is 'color' and printStyle is 'duplex': ₹10 × totalPages
- If colorMode is 'auto': use the detected color pages

Actually for 'auto', the user didn't specify. Let me handle it by splitting:
- B&W portion (detected): ₹1 × bwPages
- Color portion (detected): ₹5 × colorPages if single, ₹10 × colorPages if duplex

Or more simply: if the document has any color pages, the rate is:
- For the B&W pages: ₹1 each
- For the color pages: ₹5 each (single) or ₹10 each (duplex)

Let me implement this cleanly.

For the token system, I need to:
1. Add a `token` field to the Order model (Int)
2. When creating an order, assign the next token number (MAX(token) + 1) for the shop
3. Display token in the order queue and customer confirmation
4. Allow searching by token

For UPI QR, I need to:
1. Add `upiQrPath` to Shop model (stored as a setting or separate field in Shop.settings JSON)
2. Admin settings page to upload QR code
3. Customer portal to display QR at payment step

Let me implement all these changes now.

Starting with the schema changes:

```prisma
model Order {
  // ... existing fields
  token         Int?
  @@unique([shopId, token])
  @@index([shopId, token])
}
```

Wait, token needs to be unique per shop. Let me make it an Int with `@@unique([shopId, token])`.

But actually, for auto-incrementing per shop, I could use a sequence or just find the max. Let me do it the simple way: when creating an order, find the MAX token for that shop and add 1.

581:   const handleUpload = async () => {
582:     if (files.length === 0) { toast.error('Please select files'); return; }
583:     if (!customerInfo.name || !customerInfo.phone) { toast.error('Please fill name and phone'); return; }
584:     setLoading(true);

PrintersPage.jsx doesn't use `size={{` or Grid at all - it uses Table, Dialog, and Box layouts. This should be fine.

OK let me think about this from a completely different angle. The user says "admin has overlapping everthing". Maybe the issue is that the frontend build succeeded, but there's a CSS issue caused by the MUI Grid syntax change. Specifically, the `item` prop was NOT being used before, but now I'm using `item` prop.

Wait, actually - when I changed `size={{ xs: 6, sm: 4, md: 3 }}` to `item xs={6} sm={4} md={3}`, the rendering behavior changes:

**Before (MUI v6 syntax, silently ignored by MUI v5):**
- `<Grid size={{ xs: 6, sm: 4, md: 3 }}>`
- In MUI v5, the `size` prop is NOT recognized
- The Grid item has NO `item` prop
- Without `item`, the Grid component renders as a container, not an item
- This means the item has no flex-basis constraints → it takes full width
- But since there's no `item`, it might also try to be a container, causing nested Grid behavior

**After (MUI v5 syntax, correctly recognized):**
- `<Grid item xs={6} sm={4} md={3}>`
- In MUI v5, the `item` prop is recognized, and `xs`, `sm`, `md` are recognized
- The item renders as a proper grid item with correct flex-basis

So after my fix, the Grid items should render CORRECTLY. Before, they were rendering as full-width items (because the `size` prop was ignored).

Wait, but the user is saying the layout is WORSE after my fix? Or is it still overlapping?

Let me re-read: "still admin has overlapping everthing and not responsible"

"still" suggests the issue persisted even after my Grid fix. But "not responsible" might mean "not responsive" (i.e., not adjusting to screen size).

Hmm, maybe the issue is something completely different. Let me look at the CSS that's being generated. The `md={2.4}` value - wait, let me check if MUI v5 Grid actually handles `2.4` correctly.

I think the safest fix is to change `md={2.4}` to proper integer values. Instead of 5 items at 20% each, let me change to 6 items at `md={2}` (16.6%) or 4 items at `md={3}` (25%). But wait, there are 5 stat cards, not 6.

Actually, let me reconsider the DashboardPage layout. Originally it was using `size={{ xs: 12, sm: 6, md: 2.4 }}` which was from the MUI v6 syntax. But even in MUI v6, `2.4` would work with the new Grid2 component (which supports flex values). In MUI v5 Grid v1, non-integer values might not work.

Let me change `md={2.4}` to `md={2}` for 6 per row, or to a custom CSS approach. Actually, the simplest fix is to change to `md={4}` for 3 per row on desktop, or `md={3}` for 4 per row. Let me use `md={4}` (3 per row, so 2 rows for 5 items) which is cleaner.

But wait - the user said "admin" not "dashboard". If the issue affects ALL admin pages, it's not a Dashboard-specific problem.

Let me think about what ALL admin pages have in common:
1. They're rendered inside `AdminLayout.jsx`
2. They use MUI components

AdminLayout was NOT modified by my PowerShell script. It uses standard MUI v5 syntax. It should be fine.

Wait, could the issue be that the AdminLayout uses `md` breakpoint and the pages also use `md`, creating a conflict?

Actually, no. The AdminLayout uses `width: { md: \`calc(100% - ${DRAWER_WIDTH}px)\` }` which is a responsive Box width. The pages use Grid items with `md` prop. These are different components and shouldn't conflict.

Hmm, let me look at CustomerPortal.jsx more carefully. The user said "admin" has the issue, but CustomerPortal is not admin. Let me focus on actual admin pages.

Actually wait, the user originally said "still admin has overlapping everthing and not responsible". Then in the next message "i think its not responsible for desktop , laptop its not showing all textes its hiding with other div or element".

So "not responsible" = "not responsive". The desktop/laptop layout is broken with text hiding/overlapping.

This sounds like a CSS issue where text overflows its container. Let me check if there's a `whiteSpace: 'nowrap'` or `overflow: 'hidden'` causing text clipping.

In DashboardPage:
```jsx
<Box sx={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <TableContainer component={Paper}>
    <Table size="small" sx={{ minWidth: 600 }}>
```

The `overflowX: 'auto'` and `minWidth: 600` on the Table should create a horizontal scrollbar if the table is too wide. This is fine.

In OrderDetailPage - I used `sx={{ maxWidth: 200, overflow: 'hidden', textOverflow: 'ellipsis', whiteSpace: 'nowrap' }}` for the file name cell. This clips long file names. But that's intentional.

Hmm, I'm really struggling to identify the issue without seeing it. Let me just do a comprehensive check - make sure all the files I rewrote compile and look correct. Then rebuild.

Actually, let me check if there's a problem with the `overflow: 'auto'` on the admin layout main box. With `overflow: 'auto'`, the main content gets a scrollbar if needed. But what if there's a nested element with `overflow: 'hidden'` that clips the content?

Or what if the issue is with the Grid `spacing` prop? MUI v5 Grid uses negative margins and padding to create spacing. If the parent doesn't account for these negative margins, content could be clipped at the edges.

Actually, MUI Grid handles spacing by using negative margins on the container and padding on the items. This should work correctly as long as the container doesn't have `overflow: 'hidden'`.

OK, I think I need to see what the user is seeing. Let me ask them to take a screenshot using the Windows Snipping Tool or ShareX, and upload it. But wait - I can't view images!

Let me try a different approach. Let me look at the Settings page - the user might be referring to the Settings page's pricing section layout.

Actually, I just realized: maybe the problem is that after my Grid fix, the items are NOW rendering correctly (with proper sizing), but the container is too narrow, causing items to overlap or wrap. Before my fix, the `size={{ }}` syntax was silently ignored, so items rendered as full-width blocks (stacked vertically). Now they render as proper grid items at specified widths, which might be too narrow for the content.

For example, in SettingsPage.jsx:
```jsx
<Grid container spacing={2}>
    <Grid item xs={12} sm={6}>B&W field</Grid>
    <Grid item xs={12} sm={6}>Color Single field</Grid>
    <Grid item xs={12} sm={6}>Color Duplex field</Grid>
</Grid>
```

At `sm={6}`, each item takes 50% width. On a 600px-wide container, that's 300px per field. With padding and label, that should be fine.

At `xs={12}`, each item takes 100% width. Fine.

Hmm, but what about the customer portal page? The container is `maxWidth="sm"` (600px). At `md={3}`, each item is 25% of 600px = 150px. At `md={2}` for section items, each is 16.6% of 600px = 100px. That's very narrow.

Wait, but the `md` breakpoint requires the viewport to be at least 900px wide. With a `maxWidth="sm"` container (600px max), the `md` breakpoint is never reached because the container itself is only 600px. So the `sm` breakpoint would apply instead.

At `sm` breakpoint (600px+), the container is 600px wide:
- Main settings items: `sm={4}` = 33.3% = 200px each → 3 per row
- Section items: `sm={4}` = 33.3% = 200px each → 3 per row

But at `sm` breakpoint for section items, I used `sm={4}` (3 per row). That's 200px per FormControl. Should be fine.

At `xs` breakpoint (<600px):
- Main settings: `xs={6}` = 50% of viewport width → 2 per row
- Section items: `xs={6}` = 50% → 2 per row

Should be fine.

OK I really can't figure out the exact issue without seeing it. But looking at the section grid in CustomerPortal, I had changed items from the original `sm={2}` (6 per row) to `sm={4}` (3 per row). Let me verify this change is correct and doesn't cause issues.

Actually, let me just try a different approach. Instead of analyzing further, let me check if there's a very simple CSS issue - like missing width or flex properties on the Grid container.

Actually, wait. I just noticed something in the CustomerPortal.jsx file I wrote. Let me check the Grid items for section cards. I wrote:

```jsx
<Grid container spacing={1}>
    <Grid item xs={6} sm={4} md={2}>
```

But `md={2}` means 2/12 = 16.6%. With 6 items per row, each is 16.6%. On a 600px container (maxWidth="sm"), each item = 100px. That's quite narrow.

But wait - the `md` breakpoint requires 900px viewport width. The container is max 600px. So `md={2}` would never be the active breakpoint for this container. The `sm={4}` (33.3%) would be active at 600px+, giving 200px per item. At 600-900px viewport, the container is 600px (because maxWidth="sm" caps at 600px). So at `sm`, items are 200px each.

No wait, at viewport 900px+ (md breakpoint):
- The container is still max 600px (maxWidth="sm")
- But the Grid breakpoint is based on viewport width, not container width
- So at 900px viewport, the Grid uses `md={2}` even though the container is only 600px
- Each item would be 16.6% of 600px = 100px

100px for a FormControl with a Select/TextField and label is too narrow! The text would overlap or be cut off.

AH HA! I think that's the issue. On desktop/laptop (viewport > 900px), the Grid uses `md={2}` for section items. But the container is only 600px wide (maxWidth="sm"). So each item is 100px, which is too narrow for text fields.

On mobile (< 600px), the Grid uses `xs={6}` = 50% of viewport (<300px). 2 per row. Better.

On tablet (600-900px), the Grid uses `sm={4}` = 33.3% of 600px = 200px. 3 per row. Fine.

The fix: change `md={2}` for section items to `md={3}` or `md={4}` so that each item is wider on desktop.

But the user specifically said "admin" has the issue. The admin pages don't use `maxWidth="sm"`. Let me check the admin pages.

DashboardPage:
```jsx
<Grid container spacing={3} sx={{ mb: 4 }}>
    <Grid item xs={12} sm={6} md={2.4}>
```

On desktop (md breakpoint, 900px+), each item is 20% of the main content area. The main content is `width: calc(100% - 240px)` (full width minus sidebar). On a 1920px screen, that's 1680px. Each item = 336px. Fine.

Hmm, so the Dashboard should be fine.

OrderDetailPage:
```jsx
<Grid container spacing={3}>
    <Grid item xs={12} md={6}>Customer Info</Grid>
    <Grid item xs={12} md={6}>Order Info</Grid>
```

On desktop: each is 50% of the main content area. With spacing=3, these should be fine.

SettingsPage:
```jsx
<Grid container spacing={2}>
    <Grid item xs={12} sm={6}>B&W field</Grid>
    <Grid item xs={12} sm={6}>Color Single field</Grid>
    <Grid item xs={12} sm={6}>Color Duplex field</Grid>
</Grid>
```

On desktop (sm breakpoint+): each is 50% of main content. Fine (3 items = row1: 2 items, row2: 1 item).

So the admin pages should be fine. Let me check the CustomerPortal again.

CustomerPortal:
```jsx
<Container maxWidth="sm" sx={{ py: { xs: 2, sm: 4 }, px: { xs: 1.5, sm: 3 } }}>
```

This container is 600px max. Inside, the section card Grid items at `md={2}` = 100px each on desktop. This IS too narrow.

But the user is asking about "admin" not "customer portal". So maybe the issue IS with the customer portal too but they phrased it as "admin".

Actually, let me re-read the conversation: user first said "still admin has overlapping everthing and not responsible" and then "i think its not responsible for desktop , laptop its not showing all textes its hiding with other div or element".

Maybe the first message was about admin and the second is a general description of the problem across the board.

OK, let me take the practical approach: make the section item Grid wider by changing `md={2}` to `md={4}` (4 items per row instead of 6). And check if there are any other narrow Grid items.
I think I found it — the section cards in the configure page have `md={2}` which makes each field only 100px wide on desktop (container is capped at 600px). Let me widen them:

const width = `${Math.round((value / 12) * 10e7) / 10e5}%`;

  flexBasis: `${Math.round((value / 12) * 10e5) / 10e4}%`,
  maxWidth: `${Math.round((value / 12) * 10e5) / 10e4}%`,
};

1. **Backend requirements**: The app uses:

3. **Architecture issues**:
   - The app currently serves frontend from the backend (`express.static`)
   - Printing requires physical printer access (the server sends jobs to local printers via pdf-to-printer)

So the answer is: it's complicated. The frontend can be deployed to Vercel easily, but the backend needs:
- A hosted PostgreSQL database (like Neon, Railway, or Supabase)
- A proper Node.js hosting platform (like Railway, Render, Fly.io, or AWS)

**Frontend** (React/Vite) → can deploy to Vercel ✓  
**Backend** (Express + PostgreSQL + local printer dispatch) → **Vercel is not ideal** for these reasons:

1. **Express server** — Vercel supports Express via Serverless Functions, but it's not straightforward (needs `vercel.json` config)
2. **PostgreSQL** — You'd need a cloud DB service like [Neon](https://neon.tech) (free tier available) or [Supabase](https://supabase.com)

export default function CustomerPortal() {
  const [activeStep, setActiveStep] = useState(0);
  const [files, setFiles] = useState([]);
  const [customerInfo, setCustomerInfo] = useState({ name: '', phone: '', email: '' });
  const [fileSettings, setFileSettings] = useState({});
  const [uploadedOrder, setUploadedOrder] = useState(null);
  const [paymentMethod, setPaymentMethod] = useState('cash');
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [priceData, setPriceData] = useState(null);
  const [loadingPrice, setLoadingPrice] = useState(false);
  const [upiQrUrl, setUpiQrUrl] = useState('');
  const theme = useTheme();
  const isMobile = useMediaQuery(theme.breakpoints.down('sm'));

  const handleUpload = async () => {
    if (files.length === 0) { toast.error('Please select files'); return; }
    if (!customerInfo.name || !customerInfo.phone) { toast.error('Please fill name and phone'); return; }
    setLoading(true);
    try {
      const formData = new FormData();
      files.forEach((f) => formData.append('files', f));
      formData.append('customerName', customerInfo.name);
      formData.append('customerPhone', customerInfo.phone);
      formData.append('customerEmail', customerInfo.email);

      const result = await api.post('/guest/upload', formData);
      if (result.success) {
        setUploadedOrder(result.data);
        toast.success(`${result.data.files?.length || 0} file(s) analyzed!`);
        setActiveStep(1);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Upload failed');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const handleSaveSettings = async () => {
    if (!uploadedOrder) return;
    setLoading(true);
    try {
      for (const [fileIndex, settings] of Object.entries(fileSettings)) {
        const fileId = uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.id;
        if (fileId) {
          await api.put(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/settings`, {
            fileId,
            settings: { ...uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.settings, ...settings },
          });
        }
      }
      const updated = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}`);
      if (updated.success) setUploadedOrder(updated.data);
      toast.success('Settings saved!');
      setActiveStep(2);
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to save settings');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const fetchPrice = async () => {
    if (!uploadedOrder) return;
    setLoadingPrice(true);
    try {
      const result = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/price`);
      if (result.success) setPriceData(result.data);
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to get price');
    } finally {
      setLoadingPrice(false);
    }
  };

  const fetchUpiQr = async () => {
    try {
      const result = await api.get('/settings/public/upi-qr');
      if (result.success && result.data.url) setUpiQrUrl(result.data.url);
    } catch {}
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    if (activeStep === 2) fetchUpiQr();
  }, [activeStep]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (activeStep === 2 && uploadedOrder) fetchPrice();
  }, [activeStep, uploadedOrder?.id]);

  const handlePlaceOrder = async () => {
    if (!uploadedOrder || !paymentMethod) { toast.error('Select payment method'); return; }
    setLoading(true);
    try {
      const result = await api.post(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/confirm`, { paymentMethod });
      if (result.success) {
        setUploadedOrder(result.data);
        toast.success('Order placed!');
        setActiveStep(3);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to place order');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const handleNext = async () => {

Server is running. Here's how mixed color/B&W orders are now divided:

## Routing logic (auto-distribute)

When a customer order has a mix — e.g. Section 1 B&W, Section 2 Color, Section 3 B&W:

| Section | Mode | Routes to |
|---------|------|-----------|
| 1 (pages 1-5) | B&W | One of your **4 B&W machines** |
| 2 (pages 6-10) | Color | One of your **4 Color machines** |
| 3 (pages 11-15) | B&W | **Same B&W machine** as section 1 |

So B&W parts go to B&W machines, Color parts to Color machines — automatically, with no manual choice needed.

## Load balancing

With 4 B&W + 4 Color machines, incoming orders now **spread across** them (round-robin per type) instead of piling onto machine #1:
- Order A (B&W) → B&W machine 1
- Order B (B&W) → B&W machine 2
- Order C (mixed) → B&W machine 3 + Color machine 1
- etc.

But **all sections of one order stay on a single machine per type**, so sequence is preserved.

## Manual override

The admin printer dropdown now shows each printer's type (`• Color` / `• B/W`), and "Auto-distribute (by color)" is the default. If you manually pick a B&W machine for a mixed order, the Color sections print grayscale on it — so for mixed orders, leave it on Auto-distribute.

parts.text:
## Objective
- Patel AutoPrint v2.0 print shop system: customer portal (upload, configure, pay) + admin panel (approve/print). Currently adding Windows-style **contact-sheet / N-up photo printing**: upload multiple images → choose "pictures per page" (2/4/6/9/16) → images tiled onto sheets.

## Important Details
- **Backend**: CommonJS (`require`/`module.exports`), Express + Prisma + PostgreSQL 15, now running on **Node v24.18.0** (was 18.15.0). Sharp may now work since Node ≥18.17.
- **Frontend**: React 18 / MUI v5 (NOT v6) / Vite, served from `frontend/dist` at `http://localhost:5000`
- **Credentials**: `admin@patelautoprint.com` / `admin123`
- **MUI v5 Grid**: use `item xs={6} sm={4} md={3}` (NOT v6 `size={{...}}`)
- **PostgreSQL has no Windows service** — start manually each session: `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden -FilePath "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\15\bin\postgres.exe" -ArgumentList "-D \`"C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\15\data\`""`. Remove stale `postmaster.pid` first.
- **App server start**: `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden -FilePath "node" -ArgumentList '"C:\Users\mayank\Documents\New OpenCode Project\patel-autoprint\backend\src\server.js"'`
- **Printers**: 4 B&W machines + 4 Color machines configured. Routing is color-aware (B&W→B&W, Color→Color), round-robin per color-type across orders, one machine per order-mode for sequence.
- **Default color mode** is now `'bw'` everywhere (upload, createPrintJobsForFile, pricing, frontend getSettings normalizes 'auto'→'bw'). Guest upload route line 582 previously did `colorMode: analysis.colorPageCount > 0 ? 'color' : 'bw'` — changed to `'bw'`.
- **Image upload default** should likely be `'color'` (photos are color) — NOT yet changed; pending decision.
- `api.js` has no default Content-Type (FormData works).
- `pagesPerSheetOptions = [1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 16]` (frontend CustomerPortal.jsx:50). `applyNUp` cols/rows switch: 2→2×1, 4→2×2, 6→2×3, 8→2×4, 9→3×3, 16→4×4.
- **Supported image types**: jpg, jpeg, png, webp (analyzer.js FILE_TYPES). pdf-lib `embedJpg`/`embedPng` work; webp needs sharp conversion.
- **Pricing per-sheet**: B&W ₹1/sheet, Color single ₹5/sheet, Color duplex ₹10/sheet. `calculatePrice(totalPages, colorPages, settings, config)` uses `sheetsForPages` = ceil(pages/nUp) for N-up.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed default color → B/W everywhere (backend upload/confirm/createPrintJobsForFile/pricing; frontend getSettings normalization; removed 'auto' from dropdown).
- Added **two printer selectors** in admin OrderDetailPage: **B/W Printer** + **Color Printer** dropdowns (filtered by colorSupport). Backend accepts `bwPrinterName`/`colorPrinterName`; routes B&W sections→B/W machine, Color sections→Color machine; ignores unused selector.
- Fixed **section printing bugs**:
  - Filename collision: `processPDF` now writes `${printJob.id}_printready.pdf` (was `${file.id}_printready.pdf`) — fixed parallel-section overwrite.
  - Removed `options.pages` from `dispatchPrintJob` (processed PDF already has correct pages).
  - **Sequential processing**: `processAndDispatchOrder` now loops in `sectionIndex` order (was `Promise.all` parallel → random order).
  - **One printer per order**: `routeJob` picks first matching printer per color-mode via per-order `modePrinterCache`; round-robin `bwRouteIndex`/`colorRouteIndex` across orders.
- Fixed "internal error" on Start Printing: status route now deletes old print jobs and recreates fresh ones before dispatch.
- From/To + Copies number inputs: allow clearing (string state + onBlur reset) in CustomerPortal sections.
- PostgreSQL + app server restarted and verified healthy (`/api/health` returns ok).

### Active
- **Implementing contact-sheet / N-up photo printing** (Windows print-dialog style):
  - Backend `printProcessor.js`: plan to add `isImageFile()`, `createContactSheet(imageFiles, nUp, paperSize, jobId)` using pdf-lib (grid of N images/page), and `processOne` detection of contact-sheet jobs (pages = JSON array of file-ID strings).
  - Backend `server.js`: in status + reprint routes, separate image files from others; create ONE contact-sheet print job encoding image file IDs in `pages` field; non-images use existing `createPrintJobsForFile`.
  - Frontend `CustomerPortal.jsx`: when all uploaded files are images, show "Pictures per page" selector that sets `pagesPerSheet` for all image files; relabel N-up control for images.
  - Pricing: contact sheet should charge per resulting SHEET (ceil(numImages/nUp)), not per image — needs adjustment in `pricing.js`/settings save.
  - Image upload default colorMode likely should be `'color'` (pending).

### Blocked
- PostgreSQL has no Windows service (manual start each session; remove stale `postmaster.pid` first).
- Sharp availability on Node 24 unconfirmed for webp conversion (pdf-lib handles jpg/png directly).

## Next Move
1. Implement `createContactSheet()` in `printProcessor.js` (pdf-lib grid layout, handle jpg/jpeg/png, webp via sharp fallback) + `processOne` contact-sheet detection.
2. Add `createContactSheetPrintJob()` in `server.js` (status + reprint routes) encoding image file IDs in `pages`; set colorMode from image settings (default 'color' for images).
3. Frontend: image-only upload → "Pictures per page" control applying `pagesPerSheet` to all image files.
4. Adjust pricing for combined image sheets (charge per sheet, not per image).
5. Rebuild frontend, restart server, test with 9 images at 9/page → 1 page 3×3 grid.

## Relevant Files
- `backend/src/services/printProcessor.js`: `processFile()`, `processPDF()`, `applyNUp()` (cols/rows switch), `dispatchPrintJob()`, `processAndDispatchOrder()` (sequential loop, `processOne`). Needs `createContactSheet` + contact-sheet detection.
- `backend/src/server.js`: `createPrintJobsForFile(file, orderId, shopId, printers, bwOverridePrinter, colorOverridePrinter)`, status route (lines ~845-891, accepts `bwPrinterName`/`colorPrinterName`), reprint route (~912), guest upload (line 536, defaultSettings colorMode), guest confirm (743).
- `backend/src/services/analyzer.js`: `FILE_TYPES`, `getFileType()`, `analyzeImage()` (colorPageCount=1 for images).
- `backend/src/services/pricing.js`: `calculatePrice(totalPages, colorPages, settings, config)` per-sheet.
- `backend/src/services/duplex.js`: `PAPER_SIZES` in mm (A4 210×297); contact sheet needs points (A4 595.28×841.89).
- `frontend/src/pages/CustomerPortal.jsx`: `pagesPerSheetOptions` (line 50), upload accept (line 90), Step2Configure tabs/settings.
- `frontend/src/pages/admin/OrderDetailPage.jsx`: B/W + Color printer selectors, `handleStatusChange`/`handleReprint` pass `bwPrinterName`/`colorPrinterName`.
- `backend/prisma/schema.prisma`: PrintJob has `pages String`, `fileId String`, `pagesPerSheet Int @default(1)`, `colorMode String`, `copies Int`. No `isContactSheet` flag (avoid schema change; detect via pages = array of string IDs).

Done. The **contact-sheet / N-up photo printing** feature is implemented and verified end-to-end.

## What was built
- **`printProcessor.js`**: `createContactSheet()` tiles N images per A4 page (grid 2/4/6/9/16), `isImageFile()` helper, and `processOne()` now detects contact-sheet jobs (where `pages` is an array of file-ID strings) and builds the sheet.
- **`server.js`**: image files are auto-grouped into one contact-sheet print job in both the status (Start Printing) and reprint routes; image uploads default to `colorMode: 'color'`; pricing charges per combined sheet (9 photos ×9/page = 1 color sheet = ₹5).
- **`CustomerPortal.jsx`**: when all uploads are images, shows a "Photo contact sheet" panel with **Pictures per page** chips (2/4/6/9/16) that apply to all images at once; per-file N-up also applies to all; dropped webp (no sharp available).

## Verified
9 PNGs uploaded → 1 print job (`pagesPerSheet=9`, `colorMode=color`, `status=COMPLETED`) → contact sheet PDF with **1 page** (3×3 grid), priced at **₹5**. Frontend builds clean.

## Notes / caveats
- **webp is disabled** in the upload accept (sharp isn't installed for win32-x64), so only jpg/jpeg/png work for contact sheets. Re-add `.webp` if sharp gets installed.
- No DB schema change — contact sheets are detected by `pages` being a JSON array of string IDs.

Both changes are done and verified.

## 1. B/W pricing bug fixed
The backend pricing was already correct (B/W → ₹1). The bug was **frontend-only**: the per-file Color dropdown only changed the active image's `colorMode`, so other images kept the `'color'` default, and `createContactSheetPrintJob` charged color if *any* image was color. Now the Color selector applies to **all** image files when the upload is all-images (same as the "Pictures per page" control). Selecting B/W on any photo sets all to B/W → priced as B/W only.

## 2. Admin "Print Summary" card added
In `OrderDetailPage.jsx`, a new **Print Summary** card shows:
- **B/W Pages** count
- **Color Pages** count
- Total pages (with a note that photos are counted as contact-sheet sheets)

It computes from `order.files`:
- Documents: per-section/page-range `colorMode` (or `auto` ratio) × copies → split into B/W vs Color.
- Images: combined contact sheets = `ceil(imageCount / nUp) × copies`, all one mode.

Both backend logic and frontend build were verified. The server is already running with the latest backend; the new frontend build is served from `dist`.

But there's a problem: the office file's `printJob.pages` and page range / N-up / copies aren't applied because we skip `processFile`. The user said layout must be preserved like the real system print dialog — which means we can't do N-up or page-range extraction without conversion anyway. For office files, native printing sends the whole document. That matches "real system print dialog print" expectation. Page range/copies handled by the OS.

However, `processFile` currently returns the raw path for non-pdf, but for office files the `pageRange`/`pagesPerSheet` are ignored (correct, since native print can't do those). Good.

Now there's another issue: the `createPrintJobsForFile` builds `pages` as a range and `parsePageRange`. For office files that's fine; the native print ignores pages. But the analysis gives pptx `pageCount: 1`, so pricing would charge 1 page. That's a separate accuracy issue but acceptable for now. The user's main complaint is "didn't printing" — that's fixed by native dispatch.

Also note: the status/reprint routes only create contact-sheet jobs for images and `createPrintJobsForFile` for the rest. For office files, `createPrintJobsForFile` runs `analyzeOfficeFile`-based logic and creates a job with the file. Good.

Now, there's a concern: `Start-Process -Verb Print` prints to the default printer. I set default printer temporarily. But the office app (PowerPoint) may take time to start and the `-Verb Print` is async (returns immediately). The `Start-Sleep` waits a bit. For multiple copies, native print with `-Verb Print` doesn't easily support copies, so I sleep per copy — that's a rough approximation. Acceptable.

The server.err is flooded with `sharp` errors (from image analysis on the contact-sheet E2E tests earlier — 800+ repeats). These are harmless (caught). The crucial finding: the **native print path for pptx wasn't exercised** in the E2E — instead the error log shows a pdf-to-printer SumatraPDF attempt on a `.pptx` file from an OLD job (job 076ce5f9), which was from a PREVIOUS session before my native-print code. 

But my fresh pptx E2E reported `status COMPLETED` and `pages [0]`. The `[0]` means `createPrintJobsForFile` built `pages` from `file.pageCount` (which was 1 at upload time because... wait, the upload analyzer should now return 5). But E2E showed pageCount 1. 

Let me focus: the real issue is **at upload, `pageCount` was 1**, but my direct test returned 5. The difference must be that the upload's `analyzeFile` is being called with the file BEFORE it's fully written, OR the regex isn't matching because of line-ending/zipping differences in the actual uploaded temp file.

Actually — the uploaded file goes through `multer` to a temp path, then `analyzeFile(file.path, fileType)`. My direct test on test.pptx returned 5. So upload should too. Unless the upload route maps fileType differently. Let me check `getFileType` returns 'pptx' for .pptx — yes. And `analyzeFile('...', 'pptx')` → `analyzeOfficeFile(filePath, 'pptx')` → my zip scan. 

Wait, maybe the upload uses a DIFFERENT analyzer import or the file isn't a valid pptx at upload (multer may store with a different name but same bytes). My test.pptx is valid (5 slides). Let me re-verify by checking the actual uploaded file. Actually, simpler: let me check if maybe `analyzeOfficeFile` catches an error silently. The server.err only shows sharp errors, no office errors. So the zip scan ran and returned... pageCount 1 means it hit `getFallbackAnalysis()`. That means `pageCount` stayed 0 → my `if (pageCount > 0)` was false.

But my direct node test of the SAME analyzer on the SAME test.pptx returned 5! The only difference: in the E2E, the file content is identical (same test.pptx bytes via multipart). 

OH. I see it. The E2E reads `fs.readFileSync('C:/.../test.pptx')` and uploads it. The analyzer reads `filePath` = the multer-stored temp path. Same bytes. So it SHOULD return 5.

Unless... the server running is an OLD version from BEFORE my analyzer fix! The uptime was 7s when I checked, but maybe my restart.bat didn't actually restart (the earlier `ChildProcess.kill` issue). Let me verify the running server has my analyzer changes by checking git-free: add a temporary log. Simpler — let me just check the current process and re-run restart definitively, then re-test.

Actually, let me reconsider the sharp errors: there are 800+ of them, meaning image analysis (sharp) has been failing for a LONG time across many runs — these accumulated from ALL prior E2E tests (contact sheet used base64 PNGs but `analyzeImage` calls sharp → fails → fallback pageCount 1, colorPageCount 1). So images always got pageCount 1. That's the analyzer's image path, unrelated to pptx.

2. **`analyzer.js`** — pptx/xlsx now report a **real page/slide count** by scanning the zip (pptx → slide count, xlsx → sheet count). Previously they fell back to `pageCount: 1`, which undercharged.

parts.text:
I see the issue! The `processPDF` function has a shortcut at line 196-198:```javascript
if (isAllPages && pagesPerSheet <= 1) {
 return file.storagePath;
}
```If the print job is for all pages with 1-up (no N-up), it just returns the original file path without creating a print-ready copy. But the agent is looking for the print-ready file!

So when the job is "1-up | single" (which means pagesPerSheet=1, all pages), the function returns the original storagePath instead of creating a print-ready file.

The agent's download route looks for files in the `print-ready` directory. So it fails.

The fix should be one of:
1. Always create a print-ready file even for 1-up all pages (change the shortcut)

### Option 1: One-click (recommended)
Double-click **`start.bat`** in the project root. It will:
1. Start PostgreSQL (if not running)

3. Start the Cloudflare tunnel (gives you a public URL)

set JWT_SECRET=your-secret-key
set NODE_ENV=development
node src/server.js
```

**Terminal 3 — Agent (on the branch PC that has the printer):**
```
cd agent

- Finds **CONFIRMED** jobs → sends to printer → sets **COMPLETED**

**Fixed!** Here's the bug and the fix:

### Root cause
In `duplex.js:getFinalLayoutOrientation`, when the orientation was **explicitly set** (e.g. `portrait`), the code **forced the final orientation** and completely ignored the N-up flip. So a 2-up portrait job ended up with `flipDirection = long-edge` — wrong.

For 2-up, the output sheet is the **opposite** orientation of the source:
- 2-up **portrait source** → landscape sheet → needs **short-edge** flip
- 2-up **landscape source** → portrait sheet → needs **long-edge** flip

### The fix
`duplex.js:getFinalLayoutOrientation` now:
- **1-up:** respects the manual orientation override (unchanged)
- **N-up (≥2):** ignores the manual orientation override and derives the flip from the **actual N-up layout** (because N-up defines its own sheet orientation)

Verified end-to-end: a 2-up + duplex job with orientation forced to `portrait` now correctly stores **`flip=short-edge`**, which the agent maps to `duplexshort`.

Just restart the server (already done in this session) and the agent will print 2-up duplex jobs with the correct short-edge flip.

The `agent/` folder is self-contained (just `index.js` + `package.json` + `pdf-to-printer`). The shop PC only needs this folder, Node.js, and the printer.

## How to install on your shop PC

The **agent** is a small program that runs on the shop PC (the one with the printer). It connects to your **server** over the internet and prints jobs locally. It does NOT need the full backend.

### What the shop PC needs
1. **Windows** with the **printer installed** (printer must show up in "Devices and Printers")
2. **Node.js** (download from nodejs.org — the LTS version)
3. The **`agent/` folder** copied from this project (just that one folder)

### Steps on the shop PC

**1. Install Node.js**
- Go to https://nodejs.org → download **LTS** → install (keep all defaults)

**2. Copy the agent folder**
- Copy the `agent/` folder from this project to the shop PC (USB drive or email it to yourself)
- It only needs: `index.js`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`

**3. Install dependencies** (one-time, in a terminal inside the agent folder):
```
cd agent
npm install
```

**4. Connect it to your server**
```
node index.js --setup
```
It will ask:
- **Server URL** → paste your public server URL (the Cloudflare tunnel URL, or your permanent hosted domain like `https://print.yourshop.com`)
- **Email / Password** → the **admin login for THAT shop** (each shop has its own login, and the agent only receives that shop's print jobs)

**5. Run it**
```
node index.js
```
Keep this window open. It polls every 5 seconds and prints jobs as they're approved.

### Important notes
- The shop PC needs **internet access** to reach your server.
- The **printer must be installed on the shop PC** and its name must match what you set in the admin dashboard (e.g. `"1 no"`).
- One agent = **one shop**. If you have multiple branches, install the agent on each branch PC and log in with that branch's shop admin account.

### For permanent use (instead of the temporary tunnel)
Right now the server runs on this dev PC with a Cloudflare quick-tunnel (URL changes on restart). For a real shop:
1. Deploy the **backend + frontend** to a cloud host (Railway, Render, or a VPS) with a fixed domain.
2. Point each shop PC's agent at that fixed domain.

Now I have a clear picture. Key findings:

**Free hosting reality in 2026:**
- **Railway**: No permanent free tier — $5/mo trial only (requires card now)
- **Render**: Free tier exists — web services spin down after 15min inactivity (cold starts 30-60s), free Postgres (256MB, 90-day expiry). No credit card needed for free tier. **Best free option.**
- **Supabase**: 500MB free Postgres, may pause after 7 days inactivity
- **Fly.io**: Free tier with $5 credits, no card for trial
- **Neon / Prisma Postgres**: 500MB free
- **aiven.io**: 1GB free, shuts down after inactivity

**Project readiness issues I can see:**
1. **No git repo** (earlier: "Is directory a git repo: no") — Render needs a GitHub repo to pull from
2. **Frontend needs `npm run build`** to produce `frontend/dist` that the server serves
3. **Hardcoded dev paths** in `start.bat` (`C:\Users\mayank\...`) — won't matter for Render but the project must be pushed to GitHub
4. **`cloudflared.exe`** in project root — not needed for cloud
5. **`processAndDispatchOrder`** uses local file paths — fine, Render has disk
6. **PostgreSQL** — Render offers free Postgres, OR use Supabase/Neon free
7. **Agent** points to `http://localhost:5000` — needs to be updated to the Render URL
8. **JWT_SECRET** — needs to be set as env var on Render
9. **The agent's `pdf-to-printer` + SumatraPDF** — only works on Windows shop PCs, NOT on Render (Linux). That's fine — the agent runs on the shop PC, server runs on Render.

**The real blocker:** I cannot create a GitHub account or Render account for the user. These require THEIR credentials. So I can:
1. Prepare the project for deployment (create render.yaml, Dockerfile if needed, ensure frontend builds, write a clear env var list, fix the agent config to use a URL)
2. Give them a step-by-step guide to: create GitHub repo, push, create Render account, connect, set env vars, run prisma migrate
3. The agent on shop PC just needs the new server URL

Let me think about what's truly deployable. The server uses:
- `pdfjs-dist`, `pdf-lib`, `mammoth`, `sharp`, `pdf-to-printer` (pdf-to-printer is Windows-only but only used by agent, which won't be deployed)
- Prisma + Postgres

For Render:
- Build command: `npm install && npx prisma generate && npm run build` (need to build frontend too)
- The server serves `frontend/dist` — need to build it
- Start command: `node src/server.js` with `NODE_ENV=production`
- Needs `DATABASE_URL` env var
- Needs `JWT_SECRET` env var
- Postgres: Render free Postgres add-on

One issue: the frontend build. The server.js serves `frontend/dist`. For Render, I should build the frontend as part of deploy, OR serve from a separate static host. Simplest: build frontend in the same service's build command, and server serves it.

Actually, the frontend uses Vite and makes API calls to `/api`. When served by the same backend (same origin), that works. So building frontend + serving from backend is the simplest single-service deploy.

Let me also check: does the server need `NODE_ENV=production`? The upload limit and static serving depend on `FRONTEND_DIST` existing. In production it will.

Let me also consider: the agent on the shop PC needs the public URL. The user will get something like `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com`.

Now, the honest constraint: **I cannot create GitHub/Render accounts or push the code.** I need the user to do that part. But I can prepare everything so it's a 5-minute copy-paste job for them.

Let me also reconsider whether to use **Render** vs something even simpler. Given the agent polls every 5s and the shop needs printing to work, cold starts (15min sleep) on Render free could cause the agent's first poll to take 30-60s — that's fine, the agent retries.

Actually, there's a subtle problem: **Render free web service spins down after 15 min of inactivity.** But the agent polls every 5s, so as long as the agent is running, the service stays awake. But if ALL shop agents are off (shop closed), it sleeps — fine. When shop opens and agent starts polling, it wakes up. Good.

**Decision: Use Render** (best free tier: free web service + free Postgres, no credit card). I'll also note Supabase/Neon as free DB alternatives.

parts.text: Now create `render.yaml`:

input.content:
# Render deployment config for Patel AutoPrint
# Free tier: web service (sleeps after 15 min idle) + free PostgreSQL (256 MB)

services:
  # --- PostgreSQL database (free tier) ---
  - type: postgres
    name: patel-autoprint-db
    databaseName: patel_autoprint
    user: patel
    plan: free
    ipAllowList: [] # empty = allow all (Render sets this automatically)

  # --- Node.js backend + serves the built frontend ---
  - type: web
    name: patel-autoprint
    runtime: node
    plan: free
    region: oregon # change if closer to you (frankfurt, singapore, oregon, virginia, ohio)
    branch: main
    rootDir: backend
    buildCommand: npm install && npx prisma generate
    startCommand: npm run start
    healthCheckPath: /api/health
    envVars:
      - key: NODE_ENV
        value: production
      - key: PORT
        value: 5000
      - key: DATABASE_URL
        fromDatabase:
          name: patel-autoprint-db
          property: connectionString
      - key: JWT_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: CORS_ORIGIN
        value: "*"
      - key: FRONTEND_DIR
        value: ../frontend/dist

input.content:
# Deploy Patel AutoPrint to the Cloud (Free)

This makes the server run 24/7 in the cloud so **you never have to keep this PC on**.
The printer agents on each shop PC just connect to the cloud URL.

> **Free host used:** [Render](https://render.com) — free web service + free PostgreSQL, no credit card.
> **Note:** Render free services sleep after 15 min of no activity. Your shop agents poll every 5s, so while a shop is open the server stays awake. When all shops are closed it sleeps (fine). First request after sleep takes ~30-60s (the agent retries automatically).
> **Free Postgres expires after 90 days** — re-create it or move to Supabase/Neon (free, no expiry) when that happens.

---

## Part 1 — Push code to GitHub (do this ONCE)

You need a free GitHub account: https://github.com/signup

1. Go to https://github.com/new
2. **Repository name:** `patel-autoprint`
3. Keep it **Public** (or Private — either works)
4. **Do NOT** add a README / .gitignore / license (we already have them)
5. Click **Create repository**
6. On the next page, copy the commands under **"…or push an existing repository from the command line"**

   They look like:
   ```
   git remote add origin https://github.com/<your-user>/patel-autoprint.git
   git branch -M main
   git push -u origin main
   ```
7. Run those 3 commands in a terminal **inside this project folder**
   (`C:\Users\mayank\Documents\New OpenCode Project\patel-autoprint`)

> If you'd rather not use the terminal, install [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com),
> add the local repository (File → Add Local Repository → pick this folder), then click **Publish**.

---

## Part 2 — Deploy on Render (do this ONCE)

You need a free Render account: https://dashboard.render.com/ (sign up with your GitHub)

1. Click **New +** → **Blueprint**
2. Connect your GitHub and select the `patel-autoprint` repo
3. Render reads `render.yaml` automatically — it will create:
   - a **PostgreSQL** database (`patel-autoprint-db`, free)
   - a **Web Service** (`patel-autoprint`, free)
4. Click **Apply** / **Deploy**

Render will then automatically:
- install dependencies
- generate the Prisma client
- create the database tables (`prisma db push`)
- seed the demo shop + admin (`prisma db seed`)
- start the server

**First deploy takes 3–5 minutes.** Watch the logs in the Render dashboard.

---

## Part 3 — Your live URL

When the deploy finishes, Render gives you a URL like:

```
https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com
```

- **Admin panel:** open that URL → log in with
  `admin@patelautoprint.com` / `admin123`
- **Customer uploads:** same URL (the customer portal)
- **Share that URL** with customers instead of the Cloudflare tunnel link.

> To use a custom domain later (e.g. `print.yourshop.com`), go to the Web Service →
> **Settings → Custom Domain** in Render (paid add-on) or point a domain at it.

---

## Part 4 — Point each shop PC's agent at the cloud

On every shop PC that has a printer:

1. Copy the `agent/` folder there (just that folder)
2. Install deps: `cd agent` then `npm install`
3. Configure it:
   ```
   node index.js --setup
   ```
   - **Server URL** → paste your Render URL (e.g. `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com`)
   - **Email / Password** → the shop admin login
4. Run it: `node index.js` (keep the window open while the shop is open)

That's it — the agent now prints jobs from the cloud, and **this dev PC can stay off**.

---

## Changing the code later

After you edit files here:
```
git add -A
git commit -m "your change"
git push
```
Render auto-redeploys on every push.
(If you change the frontend, rebuild it first: `cd frontend && npm run build`.)

## Troubleshooting

# Render deployment config for Patel AutoPrint
# Free tier: web service (sleeps after 15 min idle) + free PostgreSQL (256 MB, 90-day expiry)

# --- PostgreSQL database (free tier) — top-level key, NOT inside services ---
databases:
  - name: patel-autoprint-db
    databaseName: patel_autoprint
    user: patel
    plan: free
    ipAllowList: [] # empty = internal connections only (Render sets this)

# --- Services (web / worker / cron / static only) ---
services:
  # Node.js backend — also serves the built frontend from ../frontend/dist
  - type: web
    name: patel-autoprint
    runtime: node
    plan: free
    region: oregon # change to frankfurt / singapore if closer to you
    branch: master
    rootDir: backend
    buildCommand: npm install && npx prisma generate
    startCommand: npm run start
    healthCheckPath: /api/health
    envVars:
      - key: NODE_ENV
        value: production
      - key: PORT
        value: 5000
      - key: DATABASE_URL
        fromDatabase:
          name: patel-autoprint-db
          property: connectionString
      - key: JWT_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: CORS_ORIGIN
        value: "*"
      - key: FRONTEND_DIR
        value: ../frontend/dist

## Objective
- Deploy the Patel AutoPrint server to a free cloud host (Render) so the user never has to keep their dev PC on. The printer agent runs on each shop PC and connects to the cloud URL.

## Important Details
- **Node v24.18.0**; PostgreSQL `patel_autoprint` on localhost:5432 (password `123` in actual runtime, `.env` shows `postgres` but server runs with `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:123@localhost:5432/patel_autoprint?schema=public`).
- **Server runs on port 5000**, started manually each session.
- **Admin**: `admin@patelautoprint.com` / `admin123` (user Mayank Patel, shopId `c8cae036-c21c-4a01-b54a-d79e37859dce`).
- **Print flow (current)**: Customer uploads → order PENDING → admin clicks "Approve & Print" or "Start Printing" → order PRINTING → `processAndDispatchOrder()` creates print jobs (status PRINTING) → agent polls `GET /api/agent/jobs` (PRINTING only) → downloads file → prints via `pdf-to-printer` → marks COMPLETED. No extra confirmation step (user wanted admin click = permission, not auto-print of PENDING).
- **Agent**: `agent/index.js`, config `agent/config.json` (created via `node index.js --setup`). Polls every 5s. Uses `pdf-to-printer` (SumatraPDF, Windows-only). Maps `job.flipDirection === 'short-edge' ? 'duplexshort' : 'duplex'`.
- **Flip-direction bug FIXED**: `duplex.js:getFinalLayoutOrientation()` — when `pagesPerSheet>1`, the N-up layout orientation is derived from source + N-up flip and the manual orientation override is IGNORED. So 2-up portrait → landscape output → `short-edge` (was wrongly forced to `long-edge` when `settings.orientation='portrait'`). Verified: 2-up + orientation forced portrait → `flip=short-edge`.
- **Cloudflare Tunnel**: `cloudflared.exe` in project root, quick tunnel (URL changes on restart). Being replaced by Render permanent URL.
- **Deployment target**: Render free tier — free web service (sleeps after 15 min idle, agent 5s polling keeps awake) + free PostgreSQL (256MB, 90-day expiry). No credit card.
- **Render Blueprint error**: `unknown type "postgres"` — cause identified: `type: postgres` was placed INSIDE `services:` list. Render only allows `web`/`worker`/`cron`/`pserv`/`private-service` under `services:`. Postgres must be under a separate top-level `databases:` key. FIX NOT YET APPLIED.

## Work State
### Completed
- Flip-direction N-up fix in `duplex.js` (verified end-to-end with 2-up + forced portrait orientation → `short-edge`).
- Agent simplified back to direct print on admin "Start Printing" (removed intermediate READY/CONFIRMED steps that broke printing).
- Agent API reverted to return only PRINTING jobs; admin READY/CONFIRMED endpoints removed.
- Schema status comment reverted to `PENDING, PROCESSING, PRINTING, COMPLETED, FAILED`.
- Git repo initialized at project root; committed 49 clean files (excluded node_modules, uploads, agent config.json, print-agent/, shared/, cloudflared.exe, test files).
- `.gitignore` updated: force-include `!frontend/dist/`, ignore `agent/config.json`, `agent/print-cache/`, `*.exe`.
- `render.yaml` created (web service rootDir=backend, free Postgres, env vars DATABASE_URL fromDatabase, JWT_SECRET generateValue, CORS_ORIGIN=*, FRONTEND_DIR=../frontend/dist, healthCheckPath /api/health).
- `backend/package.json` `start` script: `npx prisma generate && npx prisma db push && node prisma/seed.js && node src/server.js`; `build`: `npx prisma generate`.
- `backend/.gitignore` created (node_modules, .env, uploads, prisma/generated).
- `DEPLOY.md` written with full GitHub + Render step-by-step.
- Branch is `master` (NOT `main`) — `render.yaml` already corrected to `branch: master`.

### Active
- Fixing `render.yaml` Blueprint syntax error (`unknown type "postgres"`). Need to move Postgres definition from `services:` to top-level `databases:` key.

### Blocked
- User must create GitHub account + Render account and push repo / connect Blueprint (cannot be done without their credentials). Code is commit-ready locally.

## Next Move
1. Fix `render.yaml`: replace `services:` list containing `type: postgres` with a top-level `databases:` key for the Postgres resource, keeping the web service under `services:`.
2. Re-commit the fixed `render.yaml` and tell user to retry Render Blueprint deploy.
3. After deploy, user points shop-PC agents at the new `.onrender.com` URL via `node index.js --setup`.

## Relevant Files
- `render.yaml` (project root): Render Blueprint — currently has Postgres wrongly nested under `services:`; needs `databases:` top-level key.
- `backend/src/services/duplex.js`: `getFinalLayoutOrientation()` (line 17, N-up ignores orientation override), `determineFlipDirection()`.
- `agent/index.js`: poll loop (PRINTING only), `processJob()` → download + print, `pdf-to-printer` mapping.
- `backend/src/server.js`: agent routes (~line 1240 `GET /api/agent/jobs` returns PRINTING), `processAndDispatchOrder()` (~line 394, sets PRINTING), upload route (594), status route (~929), `/api/health` (1198).

- `backend/prisma/schema.prisma`: Postgres, no migrations dir (uses `db push`).
- `DEPLOY.md`: user-facing GitHub + Render instructions.
- `frontend/dist/`: pre-built, force-committed so Render serves without build step.

I see a likely problem. The `start` script runs `npx prisma db push` and `node prisma/seed.js` — but on Render's free tier, **`prisma db push` can hang or fail** if the DB isn't ready, and more importantly, the dependency on `sharp` (native binaries) and `pdf-to-printer` (Windows-only) can break the **build** on Linux.

But I can't fix blindly — I need the actual error. Please do this:

1. Go to your Render dashboard → the **`patel-autoprint` web service** → **Logs** tab.
2. Scroll to the red error lines and **copy/paste them here**.

In the meantime, two things are almost certainly going to bite you on Linux/Render:

**Problem A — `pdf-to-printer` is Windows-only.** It won't install/run on Render's Linux. The `start` script doesn't use it, but it's in `dependencies`, so `npm install` may fail or warn.

**Problem B — `sharp`** needs native build; usually fine but can be slow on free tier.

Let me check where `pdf-to-printer` and `sharp` are imported in the backend — if the server imports them at startup, it'll crash on Linux:

parts.text:
Good news — both are handled defensively:
- `printProcessor.js:8` wraps `pdf-to-printer` in try/catch and **simulates** if missing → won't crash on Linux. ✅
- `analyzer.js:182` and `printProcessor.js:90` use `require('sharp')` **lazily** (inside functions, not at top). If `sharp` fails to install it'll error only when that code runs, not at startup. ✅

So the server *should* start. That means the failure is most likely in the **build/install** step or the **db push/seed** step. I really need the log text.

1. `prisma db push` can fail if `DATABASE_URL` isn't ready at first build — but Render injects it, so usually OK.
2. The bigger risk: **`npm install` failing on `sharp` or native deps on Render's build image.**

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// CORE MODELS
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  name      String
  settings  Json?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  users         User[]
  customers     Customer[]
  orders        Order[]
  printers      Printer[]
  pricingRules  PricingRule[]
  orderFiles    OrderFile[]
  printJobs     PrintJob[]

  @@map("shops")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId       String
  email        String
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("OPERATOR") // OWNER, MANAGER, OPERATOR, CUSTOMER
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@unique([shopId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId    String
  name      String
  phone     String?
  email     String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  shop   Shop    @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  orders Order[]

  @@map("customers")
}

model Order {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  token         Int?
  customerId    String?
  shopId        String
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, APPROVED, PRINTING, COMPLETED, REJECTED
  paymentStatus String   @default("UNPAID")  // UNPAID, PAID, REFUNDED
  paymentMethod String?
  totalPrice    Float    @default(0)
  discount      Float    @default(0)
  tax           Float    @default(0)
  notes         String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt    DateTime?
  printedAt     DateTime?

  shop      Shop        @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  customer  Customer?   @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])
  files     OrderFile[]
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@unique([shopId, token])
  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@index([shopId, token])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderFile {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId       String
  originalName  String
  storagePath   String
  fileType      String
  size          Int
  pageCount     Int      @default(0)
  colorPageCount Int     @default(0)
  orientation   String   @default("portrait")
  settings      Json?
  shopId        String

  order    Order      @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  shop     Shop       @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@map("order_files")
}

model PrintJob {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId        String
  fileId         String
  sectionIndex   Int      @default(0)
  pages          String   // JSON array of page numbers
  colorMode      String   @default("auto")   // auto, bw, color
  printStyle     String   @default("single") // single, duplex
  paperSize      String   @default("A4")
  pagesPerSheet  Int      @default(1)
  flipDirection  String   @default("long-edge")
  copies         Int      @default(1)
  status         String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, PROCESSING, PRINTING, COMPLETED, FAILED
  assignedPrinter String?
  shopId         String

  order     Order     @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  file      OrderFile @relation(fields: [fileId], references: [id])
  shop      Shop      @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("print_jobs")
}

model Printer {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  ip             String?
  paperSizes     Json     @default("[\"A4\"]")
  colorSupport   Boolean  @default(false)
  duplexSupport  Boolean  @default(false)
  status         String   @default("ONLINE") // ONLINE, OFFLINE, PRINTING, ERROR
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("printers")
}

model PricingRule {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  name            String
  bwPerPage       Float    @default(1)   // ₹ per B&W page
  colorPerPage    Float    @default(5)   // ₹ per color page (single)
  colorDuplexPerPage Float @default(10)  // ₹ per color page (duplex)
  taxRate         Float    @default(18)
  shopId          String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("pricing_rules")

display.text:
# Patel AutoPrint v2.0

Cloud-Based Multi-Tenant Print Shop Management & Automatic Printing Platform (SaaS)

## Tech Stack

### Backend
- Node.js + Express.js
- PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM
- JWT Authentication
- WebSocket (Real-time updates)
- PDF-Lib (PDF processing)
- Sharp (Image processing)

### Frontend
- React 18
- Material UI
- React Router
- React Query (TanStack Query)
- React Hook Form
- PDF.js (Preview)
- Tailwind CSS

### Print Agent
- Node.js (Windows)
- PowerShell (Printer discovery)
- Auto-update support

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+
- PostgreSQL 14+
- Redis (for job queues)

### Installation

1. Clone the repository
```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd patel-autoprint
```

2. Install dependencies
```bash
npm install
```

3. Set up environment
```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
# Edit backend/.env with your database credentials
```

4. Initialize database
```bash
cd backend
npx prisma migrate dev
npm run db:seed
```

5. Start development servers
```bash
# From root directory
npm run dev
```

This starts both backend (port 5000) and frontend (port 5173).

### Demo Credentials

After seeding:
- **Shop Owner:** admin@patelxerox.com / admin123
- **Manager:** manager@patelxerox.com / manager123
- **Operator:** operator@patelxerox.com / operator123

## Project Structure

```
patel-autoprint/
├── backend/           # Express.js API server
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── controllers/
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── middleware/
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   ├── utils/
│   │   └── server.js
│   └── prisma/
│       ├── schema.prisma
│       └── seed.js
├── frontend/          # React application
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── pages/
│   │   ├── components/
│   │   ├── layouts/
│   │   ├── contexts/
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   └── utils/
│   └── index.html
├── print-agent/       # Windows Print Agent
│   └── src/
│       └── index.js
└── shared/            # Shared types & constants
    ├── types/
    └── constants/
```

## API Endpoints

### Authentication
- `POST /api/v1/auth/register` - Register new shop
- `POST /api/v1/auth/login` - Login
- `GET /api/v1/auth/profile` - Get profile

### Orders
- `POST /api/v1/orders` - Create order
- `GET /api/v1/orders/queue` - Get order queue
- `GET /api/v1/orders/search` - Search orders
- `POST /api/v1/orders/:id/approve` - Approve order
- `POST /api/v1/orders/:id/hold` - Hold order
- `POST /api/v1/orders/:id/reject` - Reject order

### Files
- `POST /api/v1/files/upload/:orderId` - Upload files
- `GET /api/v1/files/order/:orderId` - Get order files
- `GET /api/v1/files/:fileId/analyze` - Analyze file

### Printers
- `GET /api/v1/printers` - List printers
- `POST /api/v1/printers` - Add printer
- `PUT /api/v1/printers/:id` - Update printer
- `DELETE /api/v1/printers/:id` - Delete printer

### Pricing
- `GET /api/v1/pricing` - List pricing rules
- `POST /api/v1/pricing` - Create pricing rule
- `POST /api/v1/pricing/calculate` - Calculate price

## Features

### Customer Portal
- Drag & drop file upload
- Multi-file support
- Independent print settings per file
- Mixed print rules
- Live preview
- Real-time pricing
- Multiple payment methods
- Order tracking
- Print again feature

### Admin Dashboard
- Real-time order queue
- Search by Order ID, Mobile, Name
- One-click approve/hold/reject
- Printer recommendation
- Revenue reports
- Customer management
- User management
- Pricing configuration

### Print Processing Engine
- Automatic file analysis
- Office document conversion
- N-up printing
- Image layouts
- PowerPoint layouts
- Duplex auto-detection
- Binding margins
- Watermarks
- Print-ready PDF generation

### Windows Print Agent
- Automatic printer discovery
- Silent printing
- Job queue management
- Retry logic
- Status monitoring
- Auto-update

## License

Proprietary - Patel AutoPrint

## Quick Start Windows Agent

```bash
cd patel-autoprint\agent

### 2. Configure on first run
```bash
node index.js --setup

node index.js

- Report status back to cloud

### Agent behavior (patel-autoprint/agent/index.js)

- Poll `/api/agent/jobs` every 5s (GET only PRINTING jobs)
- Download job file → print via `pdf-to-printer` (SumatraPDF)

- Map `job.flipDirection === 'short-edge' ? 'duplexshort' : 'duplex'` to SumatraPDF duplex

The login (`findFirst` by email only) returned the newest user → attached to the **empty shop** → no printers, no orders.

## What I fixed

The seed script now checks `if (existingShops > 0) return` — it only seeds once, ever. Future restarts/wake-ups won't create duplicates.

## What you need to do

Since the damage is already done (your Render DB has orphaned duplicate shops), the simplest path is a **fresh start**:

1. **Push this fix:**
```bash
cd "C:\Users\mayank\Documents\New OpenCode Project\patel-autoprint"
git add backend/prisma/seed.js
git commit -m "fix: make seed idempotent — skip if data exists"
git push origin main
```

2. **On Render dashboard:**
   - Go to your **PostgreSQL database** (`patel-autoprint-db`) → **Actions** → **Reset** (this wipes all data)
   - Go to your **Web Service** (`patel-autoprint`) → **Manual Deploy** → **Deploy latest commit**

3. After deploy completes, login with `admin@patelautoprint.com / admin123` and re-add your printers.

651: export default function CustomerPortal() {
652:   const [activeStep, setActiveStep] = useState(0);
653:   const [files, setFiles] = useState([]);
654:   const [customerInfo, setCustomerInfo] = useState({ name: '', phone: '', email: '' });
655:   const [fileSettings, setFileSettings] = useState({});
656:   const [uploadedOrder, setUploadedOrder] = useState(null);
657:   const [paymentMethod, setPaymentMethod] = useState('cash');
658:   const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
659:   const [priceData, setPriceData] = useState(null);
660:   const [loadingPrice, setLoadingPrice] = useState(false);
661:   const [upiQrUrl, setUpiQrUrl] = useState('');
662:   const theme = useTheme();
663:   const isMobile = useMediaQuery(theme.breakpoints.down('sm'));
664: 
665:   const handleUpload = async () => {
666:     if (files.length === 0) { toast.error('Please select files'); return; }
667:     if (!customerInfo.name || !customerInfo.phone) { toast.error('Please fill name and phone'); return; }
668:     setLoading(true);
669:     try {
670:       const formData = new FormData();
671:       files.forEach((f) => formData.append('files', f));
672:       formData.append('customerName', customerInfo.name);
673:       formData.append('customerPhone', customerInfo.phone);
674:       formData.append('customerEmail', customerInfo.email);
675: 
676:       const result = await api.post('/guest/upload', formData);
677:       if (result.success) {
678:         setUploadedOrder(result.data);
679:         toast.success(`${result.data.files?.length || 0} file(s) analyzed!`);
680:         setActiveStep(1);
681:       }
682:     } catch (err) {
683:       toast.error(err.message || 'Upload failed');
684:     } finally {
685:       setLoading(false);
686:     }
687:   };
688: 
689:   const handleSaveSettings = async () => {
690:     if (!uploadedOrder) return;
691:     setLoading(true);
692:     try {
693:       for (const [fileIndex, settings] of Object.entries(fileSettings)) {
694:         const fileId = uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.id;
695:         if (fileId) {
696:           await api.put(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/settings`, {
697:             fileId,
698:             settings: { ...uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.settings, ...settings },
699:           });
700:         }
701:       }
702:       const updated = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}`);
703:       if (updated.success) setUploadedOrder(updated.data);
704:       toast.success('Settings saved!');
705:       setActiveStep(2);
706:     } catch (err) {
707:       toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to save settings');
708:     } finally {
709:       setLoading(false);
710:     }
711:   };
712: 
713:   const fetchPrice = async () => {
714:     if (!uploadedOrder) return;
715:     setLoadingPrice(true);
716:     try {
717:       const result = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/price`);
718:       if (result.success) setPriceData(result.data);
719:     } catch (err) {
720:       toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to get price');
721:     } finally {
722:       setLoadingPrice(false);
723:     }
724:   };
725: 
726:   const fetchUpiQr = async () => {
727:     try {
728:       const result = await api.get('/settings/public/upi-qr');
729:       if (result.success && result.data.url) setUpiQrUrl(result.data.url);
730:     } catch {}
731:   };
732: 
733:   useEffect(() => {
734:     if (activeStep === 2) fetchUpiQr();
735:   }, [activeStep]);
736: 
737:   useEffect(() => {
738:     if (activeStep === 2 && uploadedOrder) fetchPrice();
739:   }, [activeStep, uploadedOrder?.id]);
740: 
741:   const handlePlaceOrder = async () => {
742:     if (!uploadedOrder || !paymentMethod) { toast.error('Select payment method'); return; }
743:     setLoading(true);
744:     try {
745:       const result = await api.post(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/confirm`, { paymentMethod });
746:       if (result.success) {
747:         setUploadedOrder(result.data);
748:         toast.success('Order placed!');
749:         setActiveStep(3);
750:       }
751:     } catch (err) {
752:       toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to place order');
753:     } finally {
754:       setLoading(false);
755:     }
756:   };
757: 
758:   const handleNext = async () => {
759:     if (activeStep === 0) await handleUpload();
760:     else if (activeStep === 1) await handleSaveSettings();
761:     else if (activeStep === 2) await handlePlaceOrder();
762:   };
763: 
764:   const handleBack = () => setActiveStep((prev) => prev - 1);
765: 
766:   const handleNewOrder = () => {
767:     setActiveStep(0);
768:     setFiles([]);
769:     setCustomerInfo({ name: '', phone: '', email: '' });
770:     setFileSettings({});
771:     setUploadedOrder(null);
772:     setPaymentMethod('cash');
773:     setPriceData(null);
774:   };
775: 
776:   return (
777:     <Container maxWidth="sm" sx={{ py: { xs: 2, sm: 4 }, px: { xs: 1.5, sm: 3 } }}>
778:       <Typography variant="h5" align="center" gutterBottom sx={{ fontWeight: 700, fontSize: { xs: '1.4rem', sm: '1.8rem' } }}>
779:         Patel AutoPrint
780:       </Typography>
781:       <Typography variant="body2" align="center" color="text.secondary" sx={{ mb: 2 }}>
782:         Print Shop - Self Service
783:       </Typography>
784: 
785:       <Stepper activeStep={activeStep} alternativeLabel sx={{ mb: 3 }}>
786:         {steps.map((label) => (
787:           <Step key={label}>
788:             <StepLabel><Typography variant="caption" sx={{ display: { xs: 'none', sm: 'block' } }}>{label}</Typography></StepLabel>
789:           </Step>
790:         ))}
791:       </Stepper>
792: 
793:       <Paper sx={{ p: { xs: 1.5, sm: 3 }, minHeight: 300 }}>
794:         {activeStep === 0 && (
795:           <Step1Upload files={files} setFiles={setFiles} customerInfo={customerInfo} setCustomerInfo={setCustomerInfo} />
796:         )}
