generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// CORE MODELS
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  name      String
  settings  Json?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  users         User[]
  customers     Customer[]
  orders        Order[]
  printers      Printer[]
  pricingRules  PricingRule[]
  orderFiles    OrderFile[]
  printJobs     PrintJob[]

  @@map("shops")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId       String
  email        String
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("OPERATOR") // OWNER, MANAGER, OPERATOR, CUSTOMER
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@unique([shopId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId    String
  name      String
  phone     String?
  email     String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  shop   Shop    @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  orders Order[]

  @@map("customers")
}

model Order {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  token         Int?
  customerId    String?
  shopId        String
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, APPROVED, PRINTING, COMPLETED, REJECTED
  paymentStatus String   @default("UNPAID")  // UNPAID, PAID, REFUNDED
  paymentMethod String?
  totalPrice    Float    @default(0)
  discount      Float    @default(0)
  tax           Float    @default(0)
  notes         String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt    DateTime?
  printedAt     DateTime?

  shop      Shop        @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  customer  Customer?   @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])
  files     OrderFile[]
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@unique([shopId, token])
  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@index([shopId, token])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderFile {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId       String
  originalName  String
  storagePath   String
  fileType      String
  size          Int
  pageCount     Int      @default(0)
  colorPageCount Int     @default(0)
  orientation   String   @default("portrait")
  settings      Json?
  shopId        String

  order    Order      @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  shop     Shop       @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@map("order_files")
}

model PrintJob {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId        String
  fileId         String
  sectionIndex   Int      @default(0)
  pages          String   // JSON array of page numbers
  colorMode      String   @default("auto")   // auto, bw, color
  printStyle     String   @default("single") // single, duplex
  paperSize      String   @default("A4")
  pagesPerSheet  Int      @default(1)
  flipDirection  String   @default("long-edge")
  copies         Int      @default(1)
  status         String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, PROCESSING, PRINTING, COMPLETED, FAILED
  assignedPrinter String?
  shopId         String

  order     Order     @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  file      OrderFile @relation(fields: [fileId], references: [id])
  shop      Shop      @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("print_jobs")
}

model Printer {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  ip             String?
  paperSizes     Json     @default("[\"A4\"]")
  colorSupport   Boolean  @default(false)
  duplexSupport  Boolean  @default(false)
  status         String   @default("ONLINE") // ONLINE, OFFLINE, PRINTING, ERROR
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("printers")
}

model PricingRule {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  name            String
  bwPerPage       Float    @default(1)   // ₹ per B&W page
  colorPerPage    Float    @default(5)   // ₹ per color page (single)
  colorDuplexPerPage Float @default(10)  // ₹ per color page (duplex)
  taxRate         Float    @default(18)
  shopId          String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@map("pricing_rules")
}

The user wants me to transform their existing Patel AutoPrint into a professional SaaS platform quickly. They don't have 10 weeks. I need to work with what they have and make targeted improvements.

Let me look at what they currently have:
1. Backend: Express + Prisma + PostgreSQL (port 5000)
2. Agent: Node.js polling agent (agent/index.js)
3. Customer Portal: React (frontend/dist)
4. Admin Dashboard: React

Key things to add quickly:
1. Shop activation key system (generate key, validate key on agent install)
2. Enhanced agent API (heartbeat, job fetch with auth)
3. Better token display for customers
4. Real-time features (WebSocket or improve polling)
5. Multi-tenant isolation improvements

Let me focus on the most impactful changes that can be done quickly:

1. **Prisma schema extensions** - Add Agent, Subscription, Notification models
2. **Shop activation endpoints** - Generate keys, validate, activate
3. **Agent API endpoints** - Authenticated job fetch, heartbeat, status
4. **Enhanced customer portal** - Better token display, copy button, WhatsApp sharing
5. **WebSocket for real-time** - Push jobs to agents immediately

Let me start implementing these one by one. I'll begin with the Prisma schema since everything depends on it.

Let me start transforming your existing Patel AutoPrint into a professional SaaS platform. I'll work with your current codebase and add the critical features.

Let me start with the **database schema extensions**:

input.newString:
model Shop {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  name            String
  ownerName       String   @default("")
  mobile          String   @default("")
  email           String?
  address         String?
  city            String?
  state           String?
  gstNumber       String?
  
  // Activation
  activationKey   String   @unique @default("")
  isActivated     Boolean  @default(false)
  activatedAt     DateTime?
  
  // Branding
  primaryColor    String   @default("#1976d2")
  
  // Subscription
  planId          String?
  plan            Plan?    @relation(fields: [planId], references: [id])
  subscriptionStatus String @default("TRIAL") // TRIAL, ACTIVE, EXPIRED, SUSPENDED
  trialEndsAt     DateTime?
  subscriptionEndsAt DateTime?
  
  // Settings (stored as JSON for flexibility)
  settings        Json?
  
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  users           User[]
  customers       Customer[]
  orders          Order[]
  printers        Printer[]
  pricingRules    PricingRule[]
  orderFiles      OrderFile[]
  printJobs       PrintJob[]
  agents          Agent[]
  notifications   Notification[]
  whatsappSession WhatsAppSession?

  @@map("shops")
  @@index([activationKey])
  @@index([subscriptionStatus])
}

model Plan {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  name            String   @unique // "Basic", "Pro", "Enterprise"
  priceMonthly   Int      @default(0) // in paise (₹999 = 99900)
  priceYearly    Int      @default(0)
  maxOrders      Int      @default(100) // per month
  maxPrinters    Int      @default(2)
  maxStaff       Int      @default(3)
  features       Json     @default("{}") // { whatsapp: true, analytics: true, api: false }
  isActive       Boolean  @default(true)
  createdAt      DateTime @default(now())
  
  shops          Shop[]
}

model Agent {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  shopId          String
  machineName     String   @default("COUNTER-1")
  machineId       String   @unique // UUID generated on install
  apiKey          String   @unique @default("")
  version         String   @default("1.0.0")
  isActive        Boolean  @default(true)
  lastHeartbeatAt DateTime?
  ipAddress       String?
  osInfo          String?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  
  shop            Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  
  @@index([shopId])
  @@index([machineId])
  @@index([apiKey])
}

model Notification {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  shopId          String
  type            String   // order.new, printer.offline, payment.received, agent.disconnected
  title           String
  message         String
  data            Json?
  isRead          Boolean  @default(false)
  readAt          DateTime?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  
  shop            Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  
  @@index([shopId, isRead])
}

model WhatsAppSession {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  shopId          String   @unique
  phoneNumber     String?
  isConnected     Boolean  @default(false)
  sessionData     Json?
  lastConnectedAt DateTime?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  
  shop            Shop     @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
}

I see the issue now. The structure around lines 234-237 is:
```
                    </Box>
235:               )}
236:             </Grid>
237:             </Grid>
```

The issue is:
- Line 234: `</Box>` - closes the input box
- Line 235: `)}` - closes the `selectedConversation ? (...)` ternary
- Line 236: `</Grid>` - closes the Grid item (md={8})
- Line 237: `</Grid>` - this is extra! There's only one Grid container above

Let me look at the structure more carefully. The chat window section starts at line 135:
```jsx
<Grid item xs={12} md={8} sx={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', minWidth: 0 }}>
  {selectedConversation ? (
    <Box sx={{ flex: 1, display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column' }}>
      ... header ...
      <Box sx={{ flex: 1, p: 2, overflow: 'auto', display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 1 }}>
        {mockMessages.map(...)}
        {/* Typing indicator */}
        <Box sx={{ height: 20 }} />
      </Box>
      {/* Input */}
      <Box sx={{ p: 1.5, borderTop: 1, borderColor: 'divider' }}>
        ...
      </Box>
    </Box>
  ) : (
    <Box sx={{ flex: 1, display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center', color: 'text.secondary' }}>
      <Typography variant="h6">Select a conversation to start chatting</Typography>
    </Box>
  )}
</Grid>
```

So the structure is:
- Grid item (md={8})
  - Ternary: selectedConversation ? (Box) : (Box)
  - The ternary closes with `)}`
- Then `</Grid>` closes the Grid item

But the current code has:
```
235:               )}
236:             </Grid>
237:             </Grid>
```

There's an extra `</Grid>` at line 237. Let me fix this by removing the extra `</Grid>`.

Also, looking at the error message more carefully:
- Line 235: `)}` - "The character "}" is not valid inside a JSX element"
- Line 236: `</Grid>` - "Unexpected closing "Grid" tag does not match opening "Box" tag"
- Line 237: `</Grid>` - "Unterminated regular expression"

The issue is that the `)}` at line 235 is closing the ternary, but the parser thinks it's still inside JSX. This might be because the ternary is not properly structured.

Let me look at the structure more carefully. The chat window is:
```jsx
<Grid item xs={12} md={8} sx={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', minWidth: 0 }}>
  {selectedConversation ? (
    <Box>...</Box>
  ) : (
    <Box>...</Box>
  )}
</Grid>
```

              )}

The asar DOES contain `dist\main\main.js` and `dist\main\preload.js`. But the `main` field in package.json is `dist/main/index.js` — there is NO `index.js` in the asar! The compiled main is `main.js`, not `index.js`. 

So the fix: either rename the main field to `dist/main/main.js` or compile to index.js. The tsc `rootDir: src/main` includes `main.ts` and `preload.ts` → outputs `main.js` and `preload.js`. The package.json main says `dist/main/index.js`. Mismatch.

Fix: change package.json `main` to `dist/main/main.js`.

Also, note node_modules is fully packed including devDependencies — huge. But let's get it working first. Actually the packaging of all node_modules including electron's own modules (electron isn't in deps anymore, but dev deps like vite, typescript, electron-builder are in node_modules) — those get packed into asar making it huge. We should exclude dev deps. electron-builder has `"files"` and also by default excludes devDependencies? No — electron-builder's smart behavior: it copies dependencies (production deps) from node_modules. But when you explicitly list `node_modules/**/*` in files, it copies ALL of node_modules.

Better approach: remove `node_modules/**/*` from files. electron-builder automatically includes production dependencies. But then we need `npm install --production` or it uses the package-lock to determine. Actually electron-builder packs the installed node_modules that match production deps by default. Since node_modules is already installed with dev deps mixed in, electron-builder with default file handling (production only) handles it: it walks node_modules and includes only production dependency packages.

So the right config:
```
"files": [
  "dist/**/*",
  "build/icon.png",
  "package.json"
]
```
And electron-builder will auto-include production node_modules.

Let me fix both: main entry and files.
Found it: the asar has `dist\main\main.js`, but `main` field points to `dist/main/index.js`. Also `node_modules` is being packed wholesale. Fixing both:

parts.text:
The winCodeSign extraction fails because it tries to create symbolic links on Windows without admin privileges (the darwin symlinks in the winCodeSign package). This is a known electron-builder issue. Solutions:

1. Disable code signing entirely. Since we don't have a cert, set `"sign": null` or use `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false` env var. electron-builder still downloads winCodeSign to sign... but without a cert, it uses signTool for editing? Actually the winCodeSign package contains rcedit etc. that ARE needed to set the icon and metadata.

Actually, the winCodeSign archive is needed for rcedit (to set the exe icon and version info). But the failure is on symlink extraction of darwin libs, which 7zip reports as an error and exits with status 2, causing retry loop.

The workaround: since the files fail only due to symlinks, we can manually extract the 7z ignoring errors, or set the env var `ELECTRON_BUILDER_CACHE` ... no.

Known fixes:
1. Run terminal as Administrator — the symlink creation requires privilege. But we can't easily do that.
2. Manually extract the archive. electron-builder will then find the extracted folder and not re-download. But electron-builder checks for existence of the dir... it uses the folder path `winCodeSign-2.6.0` in cache. If we extract the 7z manually with 7za ignoring symlink errors, the needed binaries (rcedit, etc.) would exist.

Actually, let me check what winCodeSign contains. The darwin symlinks are only for mac. The needed files for Windows are `windows/` dir with rcedit etc.

Approach: Manually extract the downloaded 7z into the expected cache dir. The expected dir from logs: `C:\Users\mayank\AppData\Local\electron-builder\Cache\winCodeSign\283480167` (that's a temp dir). Hmm, the extraction target has a random numeric name then electron-builder renames to `winCodeSign-2.6.0`. 

Alternatively, the cleanest fix: set env `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false` to skip signing, AND the winCodeSign is still needed for rcedit. Hmm.

Actually wait — the winCodeSign download/extraction happens during the `pack` phase regardless because electron-builder uses `rcedit` from winCodeSign to set the exe icon. 

Alternative approach: Many people solve this by running the build in a terminal with admin rights, OR by pre-extracting winCodeSign manually.

Let me think about the simplest path: Manually extract the winCodeSign 7z to the cache location where electron-builder expects it, with errors tolerated. electron-builder checks `C:\Users\mayank\AppData\Local\electron-builder\Cache\winCodeSign\winCodeSign-2.6.0` (folder name = `winCodeSign-2.6.0`). If that dir exists with the `windows/` subfolder, it will skip download.

Let me do that. First find where the 7z was downloaded. The retry loop downloads to `winCodeSign\283480167.7z` etc (random names) and extracts to `winCodeSign\283480167`. Let me check the cache dir.

parts.text:
The `.gitignore` has:
- `dist/` (matches any dist dir) → ignores `desktop/dist/`
- `build/` → ignores `desktop/build/` — wait, but we WANT `desktop/build/icon.png` committed so it's available for future builds! Hmm. Actually, the icon is needed for building the installer. If build/ is gitignored, then a fresh clone won't have the icon and electron-builder will use the default electron icon. That's a minor issue but better to commit the icon. Actually `build/` matches any directory named build at any level. This would ignore `desktop/build/icon.png`.
- `*.exe` → ignores `desktop/dist-electron/*.exe` installer.

But `dist-electron/` is NOT ignored — it contains `Patel AutoPrint Setup 1.0.0.exe` (ignored by *.exe), `latest.yml`, `builder-debug.yml`, `.blockmap`, and `win-unpacked/` (which contains the unpacked app ~200MB+). `win-unpacked` would be committed! That's bad.

I should add `desktop/dist-electron/` to .gitignore. Also consider committing `desktop/build/icon.png` (need negation). And `dist/` is already ignored globally.

Let me update .gitignore:
- Add `desktop/dist-electron/`
- Add `!desktop/build/icon.png` so the icon is committed (needed to rebuild installer)

Actually, `build/` ignores everything under desktop/build. Let me add negations:
```
desktop/build/icon.png
```
after `build/`.

Wait the rule `build/` means any dir named build. To unignore a specific file: `!desktop/build/icon.png` — but gitignore negation requires the parent dir not be excluded entirely. Since `build/` excludes the directory, `!desktop/build/icon.png` won't work unless we also unignore the dir. Actually, gitignore rules: "It is not possible to re-include a file if a parent directory of that file is excluded." So `build/` excludes `desktop/build/`, and we can't re-include `icon.png`. 

Option: change the ignore rule to `**/build/` and add negation, still same problem.

Simplest: move the icon to a non-ignored location, e.g. `desktop/icon.png`, and update references (main.ts ICON_PATH prod, electron-builder files). Or change the gitignore to ignore `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `dist-electron/` more precisely.

Actually the cleanest: change the global `build/` rule. It's used to ignore... what else uses `build/`? The frontend/backend probably don't have a build dir. The comment `# Build` with `dist/` and `build/`. Let me just add explicit exceptions won't work.

Alternative: keep icon in `desktop/build/icon.png` (ignored by git) but regenerate it before each package — I can re-run the generation script when needed. But better to commit it.

Better approach: Put the icon in `desktop/icon.png` instead (not ignored), and reference that. Let me do that:
- Copy icon.png from build/ to desktop/icon.png
- Update main.ts ICON_PATH prod → `process.resourcesPath/icon.png` stays the same (resourcesPath gets files from `files` list). electron-builder `files` currently includes `build/icon.png`. Change to `icon.png`.
- The dev ICON_PATH `../../build/icon.png` → change to `../../icon.png`? In dev, `__dirname` is `desktop/dist/main`, so `../../build/icon.png` = `desktop/build/icon.png`. Change to `../icon.png`? `__dirname` = desktop/dist/main. `../../icon.png` = desktop/icon.png. Let me set dev path to `path.join(__dirname, '../../icon.png')`.

Hmm wait, in dev, does the tray even work from `dist/main`? Yes dev runs compiled tsc output in dist/main. So `../../icon.png` from `desktop/dist/main` = `desktop/icon.png`. Good.

Also add `dist-electron/` ignore.

Let me also double check the `desktop/dist` isn't tracked (dist/ rule covers it). And `desktop/dist-electron` — need to add.

Let me make these changes:
1. Copy build/icon.png → desktop/icon.png
2. Update package.json files: "icon.png" instead of "build/icon.png"
3. Update main.ts ICON_PATH
4. Add `desktop/dist-electron/` to .gitignore
5. Can delete desktop/build dir (or leave it, it's ignored)

Let me do it.

The `.gitignore` ignores `build/` (so the icon won't be committed) and doesn't ignore `dist-electron/` (would commit the unpacked app). Let me fix: move the icon out of `build/`, and ignore `dist-electron/`.

# Render deployment config for Patel AutoPrint

databases:
  - name: patel-autoprint-db

          property: connectionString

        value: "*"

parts.text:
The local DB has old data and can't add required `updatedAt` columns without defaults. The local DB is dev data — safe to reset. Let me use `--force-reset` to drop and recreate. This is local dev, so data loss is fine.

Actually — the `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` field doesn't have `@default(now())`. In Prisma, `@updatedAt` fields are managed by Prisma Client, but when db push needs to add the column, it's "required without default". The standard approach: add `@default(now())` to updatedAt fields? Many Prisma schemas use `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` without default and `prisma db push` handles it by... actually it does complain. Common solution is `@default(now())`. But since the production deploy ALSO runs `prisma db push` against a DB with existing rows, this could fail on Render too!

Wait — but production DB: did it already have these tables? The production DB is `patel_autoprint` on Render. The schema evolution there... if the PrintJob table already exists with updatedAt column (from a previous successful push), fine. But if it doesn't have it, push fails. Given deploys have been failing since f6e66ea, the production DB is at the OLD schema (pre-f6e66ea), which likely DID have `updatedAt` on print_jobs/printers (those models existed before). The f6e66ea changes added: Shop columns, Plan, Agent, Notification, WhatsAppSession tables, Order renamed fields, PrintJob new columns (downloadedAt, printedAt, agentMachineId, printerId, shopId), etc.

Adding NEW columns to existing tables: `downloadedAt`, `printedAt`, `agentMachineId` are nullable (DateTime?, String?) → OK. `shopId String` required on print_jobs — if there are existing rows, adding a required column without default FAILS on production too!

Hmm, wait — was `shopId` newly added to PrintJob in f6e66ea? Let me check git. Actually the PrintJob model previously had `shopId`? The broken index referenced shopId, and the relation existed at line 300, but the field was missing — suggesting a merge error where the field declaration got lost. It's possible `shopId` existed before. 

For LOCAL testing, simplest: `--force-reset`. The local DB is throwaway dev data. Let me do that.

For PRODUCTION later, I'll need to be careful — but that's a separate concern (the user chose local testing). Let me first get local working.

## Objective
- Restore the Patel AutoPrint version published on Render, then fix its bugs and build a Windows desktop admin app while removing the admin panel from the customer web frontend.

## Important Details
- Repo: `contactkanix-commits/patel-autoprint`, branch `main`, in sync with `origin/main`. Live Render app: `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com` (serves old app from `frontend/dist`; backend routes only `/api/health`, `/api/auth/login`, etc. — no `/api/plans` or `/api/activate`).
- User wants the old version restored exactly as published on Render (commit `a77950e`). All newer desktop-app/SaaS work is preserved on local branch `backup/new-work`.
- New task: remove admin panel from customer web app ("customers url"), create a full admin desktop app. User approved: full admin (Dashboard, Orders, Order detail, Printers, Pricing) + delete admin code from web entirely (better security than web admin).
- Render web service (`render.yaml`): rootDir `backend`, build `npm install && npx prisma generate`, start `npm run start`, serves `frontend/dist` via `FRONTEND_DIR`. The frontend bundle is committed; Render does NOT rebuild the frontend — source fixes must be rebuilt locally and committed.
- Git commit history on `main` (newest first): `b8448b3` (Chip fix + bundle rebuild), `6214d1f` (restore old version), `65e5b33`, `790a4ad`, `73bd739`, `b4df919`, `6034a4e`, `f6e66ea`, `a77950e` (restored release point).
- Wait: the above git log is partially stale — the final summary should reflect that main now has been restored and includes the Chip fix (confirmed via git). Local untracked `desktop/` folder remains on disk (app processes were locking it; not part of repo).
- Render's last verified state: serving old bundle `assets/index-CcXazOwq.js` (with the Chip bug), health ok, login works with `admin@patelautoprint.com` / `admin123`, printers list returns 2 printers. Push `b8448b3` was made; Render had NOT yet auto-deployed it as of last poll (free-tier deploy lag). Manual deploy may be required.
- Backend API surface (old version): `/api/auth/register`, `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/profile`, `/api/upload`, `/api/orders/:id`, `/api/admin/orders`, `/api/admin/orders/:id`, `/api/admin/orders/:id/status`, `/api/admin/orders/:id/print-jobs`, `/api/admin/orders/:id/reprint`, `/api/printers` CRUD, `/api/settings/pricing` GET/PUT, `/api/settings/public/upi-qr`, plus guest endpoints (`/api/guest/*`), all JWT-authenticated via `frontend/src/services/api.js` (injects `Bearer` token).
- Old web frontend structure: `frontend/src/App.jsx` (routes incl. `/login`, `/register`, `/admin/*`), `frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx` (login/logout/register/profile), admin pages: `pages/admin/AdminLayout.jsx`, `DashboardPage.jsx`, `OrderQueuePage.jsx`, `OrderDetailPage.jsx`, `PrintersPage.jsx`, `SettingsPage.jsx`; shared `components/OrderStatusBadge.jsx`.
- Fix already committed for old-version bug: Printers crash "Chip is not defined" → added `Chip` import in `frontend/src/pages/admin/PrintersPage.jsx`, rebuilt bundle (new `frontend/dist/assets/index-CSlrMm6q.js`), committed as `b8448b3`, pushed.
- Frontend build: `npm run build` in `frontend/` regenerates `frontend/dist/` (Vite); build succeeded locally (index-CSlrMm6q.js, 554.5 KB).
- `desktop/` folder (Electron app from earlier work) still untracked on disk; not part of repo after restore.

## Work State
### Completed
- Restored `main` to exact old published state (`a77950e`): removed desktop app, SaaS/activation changes via `git rm` + `git checkout a77950e -- .`, committed `6214d1f` "Restore last published version", pushed → Render redeployed old app (health ok).
- Saved new work to local branch `backup/new-work`.
- Fixed `Chip is not defined` crash in `frontend/src/pages/admin/PrintersPage.jsx` (added `Chip` to MUI import block), rebuilt `frontend/dist`, committed `b8448b3`, pushed to origin.
- Scanned frontend JSX for missing imports (extended checker to `.jsx`); only `Chip` was missing.
- Verified live Render: still serving `assets/index-CcXazOwq.js` (old bundle), health ok, login ok, printers endpoint returns 2 printers (page crash was due to Chip rendering). Render had not yet deployed `b8448b3` at last check.

### Active
- Porting existing web admin pages to a new Electron desktop admin app (full admin: Dashboard, Orders, Order detail, Printers, Pricing).
- Removing admin code from the web frontend (routes/pages/login/register/AuthContext), then rebuild bundle and commit+push.

### Blocked
- Render auto-deploy of `b8448b3` had not completed at last poll (~15-20 min after push); may need manual "Deploy latest commit" in Render dashboard.

## Next Move
1. Finish reading/porting the existing admin pages (read `AdminLayout.jsx`, `DashboardPage.jsx`, `OrderQueuePage.jsx`, `OrderDetailPage.jsx`, `PrintersPage.jsx`, `SettingsPage.jsx`) into the new desktop app.
2. Remove admin code from web frontend (`App.jsx` admin routes + `pages/admin/`, `LoginPage`, `RegisterPage`, AuthContext admin logout usage), rebuild `frontend/dist`, commit+push.
3. Scaffold admin desktop app (Electron + React + MUI + Vite) with configurable API URL and JWT login; port admin pages as desktop screens.
4. Verify desktop app against live backend (`http://localhost:5000` local or Render), then build NSIS installer.

## Relevant Files
- `render.yaml`: Render config — rootDir `backend`, serves committed `frontend/dist`.
- `frontend/src/App.jsx`: routes incl. `/login`, `/register`, `/admin/*`; registration/home page has Admin Panel entry — admin removal target.
- `frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx`: JWT auth (localStorage keys `token`, `user`), `logout()` used by AdminLayout.
- `frontend/src/services/api.js`: axios instance with baseURL + Bearer token interceptor.
- `frontend/src/pages/admin/PrintersPage.jsx`: Chip import fixed.
- `frontend/src/pages/admin/OrderQueuePage.jsx` / `OrderDetailPage.jsx`: full order queue/detail with print dialog, filters, status actions — richest porting targets.
- `frontend/src/pages/admin/DashboardPage.jsx`, `SettingsPage.jsx`, `AdminLayout.jsx`: dashboard stats + pricing settings + sidebar layout.
- `frontend/dist/assets/index-CSlrMm6q.js`: new bundle committed in `b8448b3`.
- `backup/new-work` (local branch): preserved newer desktop app + SaaS work.
- Untracked `desktop/` dir (old Electron app, with `dist-electron/Patel AutoPrint Setup 1.0.0.exe`): leftover on disk; may be replaced by the new admin desktop app.

Note: pdf-to-printer 5.8.0 uses `printer` option. But the v1 agent used `options.side` ('duplex'/'duplexshort'/'simplex') — in pdf-to-printer the option is `side`? Let me double-check pdf-to-printer's option names. In pdf-to-printer v5, options: `{ printer, pages, copies, orientation, scale, monochrome, side, paperSize }` where `side` can be 'duplex', 'duplexshort', 'simplex'. Yes, matches. And `print(filePath, options)`.

Good. Now let me build the renderer and package. But first, let me also verify the agent module loads in plain Node (it requires 'electron' for app.getPath — that won't work outside electron). The `agent.js` requires `electron` at top, so `node -e require('./electron/agent')` would fail outside Electron. That's fine — it only runs inside Electron. 

Let me build the renderer + package. But wait — there may be an issue: `electron/main.js` now requires `./agent`, and `agent.js` requires `pdf-to-printer` at require time. In the packaged app, electron-builder includes node_modules (pdf-to-printer) and asarUnpack. The require path resolves inside asar → electron patches it. Should be fine.

Also, `main.js` requires `nativeImage` for tray — fine.

One concern: In dev mode (`npm run dev`), `electron .` runs main.js which requires `./agent` → requires `pdf-to-printer` → fine (installed). And tray icon path `path.join(__dirname, '../resources/tray.png')` → in dev, `__dirname` = `desktop/electron`, so `desktop/resources/tray.png` — exists. In packaged, `__dirname` = `resources/app.asar/electron`, so `resources/app.asar/resources/tray.png` — included via files glob `resources/**/*`. Good.

Let me now rebuild + package. I need to close the running app first (it's running from the last launch — PID 7052). Let me close it, build, package, relaunch.

Actually — one more thing. The `window-all-closed` handler: `if (process.platform !== 'darwin' && isQuitting) app.quit();`. When window is hidden (close-to-tray), the window isn't destroyed, so window-all-closed won't fire. When user chooses Quit from tray → isQuitting=true → app.quit() → window closes → window-all-closed fires → isQuitting true → quit. Good.

But there's a subtle bug: if the user logs out and the window stays open, agent is stopped — good. If user closes window → hidden → agent keeps running. Good.

Another subtlety: on `before-quit`, isQuitting=true. Fine.

Also, when app starts and creds exist, agent starts immediately even before renderer loads. Good — that's the "good to go" behavior.

Now, one issue: `agent.start()` in main on app start uses persisted token. If token expired, poll gets 401 → emits auth-expired → agent stops, clears creds, renderer gets event → logs out. Good.

Let me also handle: when renderer logs in, it calls setCredentials which calls agent.start(). If already running (started from persisted creds at app boot), start() returns early (running already true) but configure() updates the token. Good.

"The requested operation requires elevation" — that's a NEW error. Start-Process now says the exe requires elevation. That's because `requestedExecutionLevel: highestAvailable` in the manifest, and the environment changed (maybe the previous elevated session ended, or the shell now runs unelevated and UAC prompts are suppressed). Earlier launches worked because... hmm, earlier launches were the same exe with the same manifest. Actually earlier launches DID work (processes showed up). 

Wait, earlier launches succeeded and showed windows. Why would it now "require elevation"? Possibly because a UAC-related policy changed, or because there's already a pending state. Actually, the error "The requested operation requires elevation" from Start-Process typically happens when `-Verb RunAs` is implied or when the executable manifest requests admin and the current process is not elevated — in which case Start-Process normally launches it (triggering UAC) rather than erroring. But with `-RedirectStandardOutput`, elevation isn't allowed → that's why: **Start-Process with -RedirectStandardOutput requires the process to be launched without elevation**. Since the exe requires admin, you can't redirect. Hence the error.

So the exe manifest's `requestedExecutionLevel: highestAvailable` is the root of many problems:
1. It triggers UAC on every launch (annoying for the shop owner).
2. It makes processes elevated → can't be killed by normal means.
3. Launching/redirecting in scripts fails.

For a "good to go" shop owner experience, the app should NOT require admin. The `requestedExecutionLevel: highestAvailable` was inherited from the backup's build config, but our admin desktop app doesn't need admin rights (it just talks HTTP + prints via pdf-to-printer). Removing elevation makes the app launch normally without UAC, and processes can be killed normally.

But wait — why did the app crash/fail to start in the scheduled task? A scheduled task runs unelevated; launching an elevated-requiring exe from a scheduled task without a UAC prompt context... it may fail silently. That explains why the scheduled task launch didn't produce a process.

And the previous two "launch initiated" timeouts: the shell was probably waiting on the UAC prompt (which the user didn't see/approve because they're not at the machine right now?), then got killed.

So the fix: remove `requestedExecutionLevel: highestAvailable` from the win build config so the app launches without elevation. Then it'll start cleanly, no UAC, and I can kill/launch it from scripts.

Done — the agent is now merged into the desktop app, and the app is **running on your screen right now**.

## How it works now (one install, good to go)
1. Shop owner installs **Patel AutoPrint Admin** and logs in.
2. The agent **auto-starts** — same login token is used to poll the backend for print jobs every 5s.
3. Approved jobs are **downloaded and printed locally** via `pdf-to-printer` (supports printer assignment, copies, simplex/duplex, paper size), then reported back as Completed/Failed.
4. Closing the window **hides to tray** and the agent keeps printing in the background. On relaunch, it auto-reconnects (credentials persisted) — no re-login needed.
5. New **Agent tab**: Running/Stopped status, processed/completed/failed counts, last poll, current job, and a live log console. Plus an **Agent ON/OFF** chip in the header.

## Also fixed
- Removed the old `requestedExecutionLevel: highestAvailable` (that was why every launch popped a UAC prompt and apps couldn't be killed). The app now runs normally — no admin needed.
- `pdf-to-printer`'s SumatraPDF binary is unpacked so printing works from the packaged installer.

## Test it now
Log in with `admin@patelautoprint.com` / `admin123` → you'll see **Agent ON** in the header → open the **Agent** tab to watch it poll. To see a real print, place an order on the customer site and approve it — the job will flow to the agent and print to your default/assigned printer.

Installer: `desktop\dist-electron\Patel AutoPrint Admin Setup 1.0.0.exe` — committed and pushed (`64679d4`).

1. Automatically discover all printers installed on the shop PC (Windows system printers)
2. Show them in the desktop app UI where the owner can select/connect which printers to use with the tool (like XeroBot)
3. The selected printers should sync to the backend (so the backend knows about them for job assignment)

Let me think about the architecture:

Current state:
- Backend `PrintersPage` (web, now in desktop) has a manual CRUD: `/api/printers` POST/PUT/DELETE with `{ name, ip, colorSupport, duplexSupport }`.
- Backend `/api/printers` CRUD stores printers in DB with fields. Let me check the Printer model schema.
- The agent (`agent.js`) prints to `job.assignedPrinter` (printer NAME from DB) or default printer.
- Job assignment: when admin approves an order, they pick a printer by name (bwPrinterName/colorPrinterName). The backend assigns jobs with `assignedPrinter` = printer name.

Wait — the current print job flow: the web admin's PrintersPage lets you add printer with name + IP. When approving orders, you select printers by name. The backend's printer records probably store status (ONLINE/OFFLINE based on ping to IP?). Let me check the Printer model and printer service.

The user wants:
- Desktop app auto-discovers system printers (via PowerShell `Get-Printer`)
- Shows them in the app (Agent section or a "Printers" tab) with a toggle/checkbox to connect
- When connected, the app registers them with the backend (creates/updates the backend Printer records automatically)
- The owner doesn't manually type name/IP

So the new flow:
1. Desktop app discovers printers → lists them in the Printers tab as "Available / Not connected" with a Connect button/toggle.
2. On connect → calls backend `/api/printers` POST to create (or PUT to update) the printer record with the discovered name (and auto-detected color/duplex support if possible).
3. On disconnect → delete from backend.
4. The backend `Printer` records drive the dropdowns in the approve/print dialogs (they already select by printer name).

Let me look at the current backend printer routes and Printer model to understand what fields exist and how status is computed. Also check how `bwPrinterName`/`colorPrinterName`/`assignedPrinter` work.

Let me read:
- backend server.js printer routes
- backend prisma schema Printer model
- backend services/printer.js
- The desktop PrintersPage (currently manual CRUD)

Then design:

Backend changes:
- Possibly add an endpoint to list system printers? No — the desktop app discovers them locally. The backend doesn't need to know system printers. The backend just stores the connected printers.
- The auto-discovery happens in the Electron main process via PowerShell `Get-Printer`.

Desktop changes:
1. `electron/main.js` or a new `electron/printerDiscovery.js`: IPC `printer:list-system` → runs PowerShell `Get-Printer | ConvertTo-Json`, returns `[{ Name, DriverName, PrinterStatus, Type, PortName, ... }]`.
2. Renderer PrintersPage: 
   - Fetch backend printers (existing `/api/printers`).
   - Fetch system printers via IPC.
   - Show a table of system printers with "Connect"/"Disconnect" toggles (connected = exists in backend list, matched by name).
   - On connect → POST to backend `/api/printers` with `{ name, ip: (portName or ''), colorSupport, duplexSupport }`.
   - On disconnect → DELETE backend printer.
   - Keep manual add? The user wants to remove manual. I'll keep a note but the main flow is click-to-connect. Maybe remove the manual Add dialog and rely on discovery. The user explicitly said shop owner should NOT have to install printer manually — the desktop app fetches all printers and owner clicks which to connect. So replace the manual CRUD UI with the connect/disconnect UI. I can keep the edit dialog for color/duplex support toggles since auto-detection of color/duplex isn't always reliable.

   Actually, to keep it simple and aligned with the request: 
   - Show discovered system printers list.
   - Each has a toggle "Connected to Patel AutoPrint".
   - Connected ones appear with color/duplex toggles (small switches) that update the backend record (PUT).
   - Add a "Refresh" button to re-discover printers.
   - Remove the manual add dialog (or keep it hidden). I'll remove manual add entirely.

3. Determining colorSupport/duplexSupport: `Get-Printer` doesn't directly give color capability reliably. `Get-PrintDeviceCapability` or WMI can help. A simpler heuristic: try to query the printer driver for color support. Actually, there's `Get-Printer | Get-PrintDeviceCapability -Property ...` — complex. 

Alternative: `powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Printer | Select Name, PrintJobDataType, Capabilities, Default`. `Win32_Printer.Capabilities` is an array of capability values; values include 4 (Color), 6 (Duplex). Actually Win32_Printer.Capabilities: 1=other,2=unknown,3=color?,4=duplex,5=copy,6=duplex? Let me recall. The standard: PRINTER_ATTRIBUTE: `Capabilities` in Win32_Printer corresponds to flags: 4 = PRINTER_ATTRIBUTE_COLOR? Hmm not exact.

Actually simpler approach: `Get-Printer` returns `PrinterStatus` and we can get `printserver`. For color support, a common approach: use `Get-PrintDeviceCapability -PrinterName X -Property PrintColorModesSupported` but that's slow.

Another approach: Let the app auto-detect duplex via `Get-Printer -PrinterName | Get-PrintConfiguration` (gives DuplexingMode if duplex supported). And for color, use `Get-PrintDeviceCapability` for `ColorModesSupported`? 

Given complexity, I'll do a reasonable heuristic:
- Duplex: `Get-Printer -Name X | Get-PrintConfiguration` → if `DuplexingMode` != "OneSided" then duplex supported. But if the printer only supports one-sided, Get-PrintConfiguration returns OneSided — can't distinguish. Hmm.

Simplest robust approach used by many tools: try WMI `Win32_Printer` — `Capabilities` array. Per Microsoft docs, Win32_Printer Capabilities values:
- 0 = Unknown
- 1 = Other
- 2 = Unknown (again)
- 3 = Color Printing
- 4 = Duplex Printing
- 5 = Copying
- 6 = Duplex Printing (deprecated?)... 

Actually the documented PRINTER_CAPABILITIES in Win32_Printer:
Value 3 → Color Printing, Value 4 → Duplex Printing. Let me go with that heuristic: `3` = color, `4` = duplex.

Hmm, but real-world accuracy is uncertain. I'll implement:
- `Get-CimInstance Win32_Printer | Select-Object Name, DriverName, PortName, PrinterStatus, Capabilities, Default, Network`
- Parse Capabilities: includes 3 → color, includes 4 → duplex.

And also allow the owner to toggle color/duplex after connecting (editable switches) — since auto-detection may be wrong. That gives flexibility.

4. Also handle the "Assigned Printer" flow: when approving orders, the dropdowns list backend printers. Those will now be the connected ones. Good. The `assignedPrinter` used by the agent is the printer NAME — the desktop discovery uses the same Windows printer name, so `print.print({ printer: name })` matches the actual system printer. 

Also important: the old manual flow had `ip` field. When connecting discovered printers, I'll set `ip` = PortName (e.g., "USB001" or an IP for network printers) as a reference label. The backend printer.status (ONLINE/OFFLINE) — let me check how backend determines ONLINE status. If it pings the IP, USB printers would show OFFLINE. Let me check the printer service and Printer model.

Let me read the backend printer routes and model now.
Let me look at the current printer backend (model, routes, how status is computed) and the desktop PrintersPage before redesigning.

## Objective
- Merge the existing print agent into the new Patel AutoPrint desktop admin app so a shop owner can install one app that both manages the shop and prints jobs locally.
- Convert the admin left sidebar into header tabs (done before/parallel with agent merge).

## Important Details
- Repo: `contactkanix-commits/patel-autoprint`, branch `main`, live backend `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com`; backend still hosts admin APIs (owner keeps admin backend; only customer web UI removed admin).
- Backend agent protocol: `/api/agent/login` (same as admin login response shape), `GET /api/agent/jobs` (returns `PrintJob` rows where `status: 'PRINTING'` filtered by `req.user.shopId`), `GET /api/agent/jobs/:id/file` (binary print-ready PDF), `PUT /api/agent/jobs/:id/status` (`{status, message}`); all protected by `authenticate` in `backend/src/middleware/auth.js`, which requires any valid JWT — the desktop admin JWT works for agent routes without extra auth.
- `PrintJob` schema fields (passed to printer): `colorMode`, `printStyle` (`single`/`duplex`), `paperSize`, `pagesPerSheet`, `flipDirection` (`long-edge`/`short-edge`), `copies`, `assignedPrinter` (nullable → local default printer).
- Agent v1 (`agent/index.js`, polls `/api/agent/*` every 5s with stored `config.json` incl. `shopId`) matches the backend; newer `print-agent/` (v2, `/api/v1/agent/*`) does not. Agent merged here follows v1 protocol.
- Local printers (verified earlier): `1 Canon iR-ADV 6575 PCL6`, `2 Canon iR-ADV 6575 PCL6`.
- Electron main process injects permissive CORS headers via `onHeadersReceived` so packaged `file://` renderer can reach Render (webSecurity stays on).
- Admin app had `requestedExecutionLevel: "highestAvailable"` in package.json `build.win` (legacy requirement from old install) — causes UAC elevation on every launch and blocks scripted launch; was just removed, app must be repackaged and relaunched.
- Electron 28 (installed `electron@28.3.3`), `npm approve-scripts` not found (npm v11.16/Node v24), but electron/esbuild binaries already present.
- `pdf-to-printer@5.8.0` bundled SumatraPDF: `node_modules/pdf-to-printer/dist/SumatraPDF-3.4.6-32.exe` (12,644,848 bytes); `require('pdf-to-printer')` returns `{print}` and was verified loadable in plain Node.
- Agent main process runs with `sandbox: true` / `contextIsolation: true`; `pdf-to-printer` is required in the main process via `electron/agent.js` (uses `spawn`, so works under sandbox).
- Electron default icon warning remains; no custom app icon; tray icon `desktop/resources/tray.png` (32×32, generated via PowerShell System.Drawing).

## Work State
### Completed
- Header tabs: rewrote `desktop/src/renderer/pages/admin/AdminLayout.jsx` — AppBar now contains avatar + “Patel AutoPrint”, `Tabs` (Dashboard/Orders/Printers/Pricing/Agent), an Agent status Chip (`Agent ON`/`Agent OFF` green/grey), and Logout button; Drawer/sidebar removed; active tab follows route.
- Built + repackaged header-tabs version and relaunched (PID 7052) before converting to agent merge.
- Agent engine: created `desktop/electron/agent.js` — `PrintAgent extends EventEmitter`; polls `GET /api/agent/jobs` every 5s, downloads file to `app.getPath('userData')/print-cache`, prints via `pdf-to-printer` with `options.printer`, `options.copies`, `options.side` (`simplex`/`duplex`/`duplexshort` from `printStyle`/`flipDirection`), `options.paperSize`; reports `COMPLETED`/`FAILED` via `PUT /api/agent/jobs/:id/status`; simulated-print fallback when `pdf-to-printer` unavailable; emits `status` and `auth-expired` (on 401); `snapshot()` returns state → IPC/renderer.
- Main process: rewrote `desktop/electron/main.js` — persistent creds `{apiUrl,token}` in `agent-credentials.json` in userData (auto-restore/auto-start agent on app launch), IPC: `agent:set-credentials` (configure+save+start), `agent:clear-credentials`, `agent:start`, `agent:stop`, `agent:get-status`; `agent:status` → `webContents.send`; `agent:auth-expired` → clear creds + stop + notify renderer; close-to-tray (hide on close unless quitting), Tray created from `desktop/resources/tray.png` (Show/Start/Stop/Quit menu), `window-all-closed` quits only when `isQuitting`.
- Preload: `desktop/electron/preload.js` now exposes `window.patelApp.agent` (setCredentials/clearCredentials/start/stop/getStatus/onStatus/onAuthExpired) via `ipcRenderer.invoke`/`on` with unsubscribe cleanup.
- Renderer auth: `desktop/src/renderer/AuthContext.jsx` — after `/auth/profile` success or `login()` success calls `window.patelApp.agent.setCredentials(getApiUrl(), token)`; `logout()` and `agent:auth-expired` clear localStorage/token/user and send agent `clearCredentials()`.
- New Agent tab: `desktop/src/renderer/pages/admin/AgentPage.jsx` — Start/Stop buttons, live status via `useAgentStatus` hook (getStatus + onStatus), stat cards (Processed/Completed/Failed/Last Poll), Current Activity, dark monospace Agent Log (last 100 entries).
- Routes/tabs: `desktop/src/renderer/App.jsx` added `<Route path="agent" element={<AgentPage />} />`; `AdminLayout.jsx` added Agent tab and header chip.
- Package config: `desktop/package.json` added `"pdf-to-printer": "^5.8.0"` (installed), `"resources/**/*"` added to build `files`, `asarUnpack: ["node_modules/pdf-to-printer/**/*"]`, removed `requestedExecutionLevel: "highestAvailable"` from `build.win`.
- Rebuilt renderer (`vite build` OK) and ran `npx electron-builder` successfully — new installer `desktop/dist-electron/Patel AutoPrint Admin Setup 1.0.0.exe`.
- Verified asar contains `\electron\agent.js`, `\electron\main.js`, `\electron\preload.js`, `\resources\tray.png`; SumatraPDF present in `resources/app.asar.unpacked/node_modules/pdf-to-printer/dist/SumatraPDF-3.4.6-32.exe`.

### Active
- Repackaging/relaunch: after removing `requestedExecutionLevel`, fresh launch attempts failed because previously launched instance held elevated locks (access denied) and current shell waits for the GUI pipe; need to test launch now with non-elevated build.
- Attempted launch sequence: `Start-Process` timings out on the shell pipe; `Start-ScheduledTask` trigger didn’t run/verify due to elevation; direct `Start-Process --enable-logging` failed with “requested operation requires elevation” — this confirmed the elevation manifest problem, now fixed by removing `requestedExecutionLevel`.
- Need to rebuild/repack after the manifest fix (vite build and electron-builder were run BEFORE the package.json `requestedExecutionLevel` edit — repackage needed).

### Blocked
- Even after new installer is built, GUI launch from this shell is unreliable because the shell kills the child process tree when `Start-Process` times out; scheduled task launch did not produce a running process; elevated kill was required to terminate old instances (used `Start-Process powershell -Verb RunAs` to run `taskkill /F /IM "Patel AutoPrint Admin.exe"`).
- App currently not running; non-elevated build not yet launched/tested after manifest removal.
- Default Electron icon warning (cosmetic only).

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build && npx electron-builder` in `desktop/` to repackage with removed `requestedExecutionLevel`.
2. Launch fresh: prefer plain `Start-Process ...\Patel AutoPrint Admin.exe` then immediately `Get-Process -Name "Patel AutoPrint Admin*"` in a separate call (small timeout so the shell doesn’t kill the GUI); if UAC appears, manifest was not applied — investigate.
3. Verify tray + Agent tab: login with `admin@patelautoprint.com`/`admin123` (API URL defaults to `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com`), confirm Agent starts (chip ON, log shows poll), then test real print job by approving an order in the Orders tab.
4. Commit both pending changes: header-tabs + agent merge (electron/main.js, electron/agent.js, electron/preload.js, renderer files, package.json changes, resources/tray.png) and push to `origin/main`.

## Relevant Files
- `desktop/electron/agent.js`: new PrintAgent (poll/download/print/report/status-log/auth-expired).
- `desktop/electron/main.js`: main process — CORS injection, IPC handlers, tray, credential persistence, close-to-tray, auto-start agent:
  - app.whenReady → `session.defaultSession.webRequest.onHeadersReceived` injects `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` etc.
  - IPC names: `agent:set-credentials`, `agent:clear-credentials`, `agent:start`, `agent:stop`, `agent:get-status`; main→renderer: `agent:status`, `agent:auth-expired`.
  - Creds file: `app.getPath('userData')/agent-credentials.json`.
- `desktop/electron/preload.js`: `window.patelApp.agent` exposure.
- `desktop/src/renderer/AuthContext.jsx`: auto-start agent after login/profile restore; logout + auth-expired cleanup.

parts.text:
`Win32_Printer.Capabilities` works and contains capability codes. Per Microsoft WMI docs for `Win32_Printer.Capabilities`:

- 0 = Unknown
- 1 = Other
- 2 = Unknown (duplex? no...)
- 3 = Color Printing
- 4 = Duplex Printing
- 5 = Copying
- 6 = Collation
- 7 = ... 

Wait, let me map using real data:
- "3 no parul" (Canon, color A3 machine): Capabilities [4,3,5] → contains 3 (color) ✓, contains 4 (duplex) ✓, 5 = copying.
- "Xerox EXi 570" (a print server / likely color): [4,2,5] → 4 (duplex) ✓, 2 = ?, 5 = copying. No 3 → color? Hmm, the Xerox EXi 570 is a Fiery print server for a Xerox color machine usually. But Capabilities says no color (no 3). Maybe the Fiery server's color isn't exposed. Or it IS a B/W machine. Uncertain.
- "Fax": [2,3] → 3 = color? A Fax device showing "color"? Hmm, 3 = "Color Printing" per docs... A fax can't print color. So maybe the code table is different.

Let me look up the actual documented Win32_Printer.Capabilities values:
Per Microsoft docs (Win32_Printer class Capabilities property):
| Value | Meaning |
| 0 | Unknown |
| 1 | Other |
| 2 | Unknown |
| 3 | Color Printing |
| 4 | Duplex Printing |
| 5 | Copying |
| 6 | Collation |
| 7 | Scanning |
| 8 | ... |

Hmm, so 3 = Color Printing and 4 = Duplex Printing. The Fax showing [2,3]... 2 = Unknown and 3 = Color Printing — that seems like a false positive for fax, but it doesn't matter much because we can just not display "soft" printers (Adobe PDF, Microsoft Print to PDF, XPS, OneNote, Fax) in the list. Actually that's a good idea: filter out non-physical printers (Type 0 includes all; but we can filter by name/port to exclude virtual printers like "Microsoft Print to PDF", "Adobe PDF", "OneNote", "Fax", "Microsoft XPS Document Writer", "PDF").

Actually, a better filter: Win32_Printer has `Network` and `Local` flags via Attributes bitmask: 0x1 = PRINTER_ATTRIBUTE_QUEUED (local), 0x4 = PRINTER_ATTRIBUTE_NETWORK. All printers here are "Local" in Type (Type=0 for Get-Printer). Hmm.

Simplest robust approach: Let the user see ALL printers but that's noisy (Microsoft Print to PDF, OneNote, Fax, Adobe PDF). The user wants to connect their shop printers. Showing virtual ones is confusing. I'll filter to "physical" printers by excluding well-known virtual driver names, and keep everything else. But that could accidentally filter a legit printer. 

Better: filter out printers whose DriverName/PortName match known virtual patterns:
- PortName: `PORTPROMPT:`, `SHRFAX:`, `nul:`, `Documents\*.pdf`, or contains `oneNote` / `onenoteim`, `Microsoft.Office.OneNote`
- Name contains: "Fax", "OneNote", "Print to PDF", "Adobe PDF", "XPS Document Writer", "Microsoft Print"

I'll implement a `isVirtualPrinter` helper.

For color/duplex detection, `Capabilities`:
- color = includes 3
- duplex = includes 4

But the Xerox EXi 570 (the actual likely shop printer) shows [4,2,5] — no color (3). The EXi 570 could be monochrome. But it might be a color Fiery. Uncertain. Since the owner can toggle color support after connecting, a wrong auto-detect is fixable. That's the designed safety valve. Good.

Also `PrinterStatus` for Win32_Printer: 1 = Other, 2 = Unknown, 3 = Idle, 4 = Printing, 5 = Warming Up, 6 = Stopped, 7 = Offline, 8 = ... Actually per docs: 1=Other, 2=Unknown, 3=Idle, 4=Printing, 5=Warmup, 6=Stopped, 7=Offline, 8=NoError?, ... 0 = ? Hmm. The data shows: Canon WSD (unreachable) = 1, working printers (Xerox, OneNote, PDF) = 3 (Idle). So `PrinterStatus === 3` → ONLINE (idle), `PrinterStatus === 4` → Printing. Everything else → treat as available if 3 or 4, else show as-is. Actually for the UI, I'll compute `status`: 3 → ONLINE, 4 → PRINTING, 7 → OFFLINE, else UNKNOWN. The "3 no parul" shows status 1 (Other) even though it's the default printer — the WSD device may be sleeping. I'll map: idle/printing → ONLINE/PRINTING, 7 → OFFLINE, everything else → UNKNOWN. But maybe simpler: display based on 3/4/7 else UNKNOWN.

Now, where to run discovery: in the Electron main process via `spawn('powershell.exe', ...)`. Main process is sandboxed but spawn works (pdf-to-printer uses spawn). Good.

First, `desktop/electron/printers.js`:

```js
const { execFile } = require('child_process');

function listSystemPrinters() {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const script = `Get-CimInstance Win32_Printer | Select-Object Name, DriverName, PortName, PrinterStatus, Capabilities, Default | ConvertTo-Json -Compress`;
    execFile(
      'powershell.exe',
      ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command', script],
      { windowsHide: true, timeout: 20000, maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024 },
      (error, stdout) => {
        if (error || !stdout) {
          resolve([]);
          return;
        }
        try {
          const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout.trim());
          const list = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : [parsed];
          resolve(
            list
              .map((p) => normalizePrinter(p))
              .filter((p) => p && !p.virtual)
          );
        } catch {
          resolve([]);
        }
      }
    );
  });
}
```

Wait: with one printer, ConvertTo-Json returns a single object not array — handled.

Capabilities parsing: `p.Capabilities` is an array of ints. Convert. In JSON it will be array.

normalizePrinter:
```js
function normalizePrinter(p) {
  const caps = Array.isArray(p.Capabilities) ? p.Capabilities : [];
  const capsInts = caps.map((c) => Number(c));
  const color = capsInts.includes(3);
  const duplex = capsInts.includes(4);
  const name = (p.Name || '').toString();
  const driver = (p.DriverName || '').toString();
  const port = (p.PortName || '').toString();
  const statusRaw = Number(p.PrinterStatus);
  let status = 'UNKNOWN';
  if (statusRaw === 3) status = 'ONLINE';
  else if (statusRaw === 4) status = 'PRINTING';
  else if (statusRaw === 7) status = 'OFFLINE';
  return {
    name,
    driverName: driver,
    portName: port,
    status,
    color,
    duplex,
    isDefault: !!p.Default,
    virtual: isVirtualPrinter(name, driver, port),
  };
}

function isVirtualPrinter(name, driver, port) {
  const n = `${name} ${driver} ${port}`.toLowerCase();
  if (n.includes('onenote')) return true;
  if (n.includes('fax')) return true;
  if (n.includes('adobe pdf')) return true;
  if (n.includes('print to pdf')) return true;
  if (n.includes('xps document writer')) return true;
  if (port === 'PORTPROMPT:'.toLowerCase()) return true;
  if (port === 'SHRFAX:'.toLowerCase()) return true;
  if (port.includes('nul:')) return true;
  return false;
}
```

## New Printers tab flow
- On open, the desktop app scans the shop PC's installed printers (via `Win32_Printer`) and lists them — **no name/IP typing**.
- Each detected printer has a **"Connected / Not connected" switch**. Flipping it on registers the printer with the backend in one click; flipping it off removes it.
- **Color and duplex are auto-detected** from the printer driver (Capabilities: 3=color, 4=duplex) and shown per row — owner can override them with the switches while connected.
- Virtual printers (Adobe PDF, Print to PDF, Fax, OneNote, XPS) are filtered out automatically.
- Only connected printers appear in the order approval dialogs, and jobs print to them by name.

## What changed
- **No more auto color/duplex detection.** The app only detects the printer name, driver, port and status. Color and duplex are now manual switches the owner sets.
- **Paper size tick marks.** Every printer row now has chip toggles for **A4, A3, A5, A2, Letter, Legal, Tabloid** — the owner ticks which sizes that printer supports.
- Owner can tick color/duplex/paper sizes **before connecting** (they're remembered per printer) or **after** connecting (saves instantly to the backend).
- **Routing now respects paper size**: when a customer orders e.g. A3, the job goes to a printer ticked for A3 (falls back to any online printer if none match). Color/BW routing still uses the owner's color tick — so your "1 no" printer set to B/W-only will only receive B/W jobs.

So for `1 no`: leave Color **off**, tick **A4 + A3** (or whatever it loads), connect it, and it'll only get B/W jobs in those sizes.

The user wants to change the authentication flow. Currently the desktop admin app requires login with email/password (admin@patelautoprint.com / admin123). They want:

- A one-time "agent key" provided by us (Patel AutoPrint / the vendor)
- During installation, shop owner enters the agent key once
- After that, the shop owner just opens the app and it works — no login every time

So instead of email/password login, they want a per-shop license/agent key that is entered once during setup/installation, and the app authenticates with that key automatically on every launch.

Let me think about how to architect this:

**Backend:**
1. Add an "agent key" concept. Each shop gets an `agentKey` (a unique, long, secure token) that we generate and give to the shop owner (e.g., in onboarding). Store it on the Shop model.
2. Add an endpoint `POST /api/agent/key-login` (or `/api/auth/agent-key`) that accepts `{ agentKey, apiUrl }`, validates it against the Shop, and returns a JWT (same shape as admin login — token + user). The desktop app stores this token + uses it for all API calls (admin + agent).
3. The token returned should be a JWT for that shop's admin user. So agent key login finds the shop by agentKey, then finds the shop's admin user, and issues a token for them (same as email/password login would).

**Desktop app:**
1. Replace the login screen with an "Activation" screen: "Enter your Agent Key" (a one-time setup). 
2. On first launch: no credentials → show activation screen asking for the agent key. On submit → POST to backend `/api/agent/key-login` → get token → save `{ apiUrl, token }` to `agent-credentials.json` (already exists) → auto-start agent → enter main app.
3. On subsequent launches: credentials exist → auto-login (verify with `/auth/profile`), skip the login screen entirely → straight into the dashboard.
4. Keep the current session-persistence (localStorage token) OR move entirely to main-process credential store. Currently AuthContext uses localStorage + agent-credentials.json. Let me review the current auth flow.

Currently:
- `AuthContext.jsx` — login() calls `api.post('/auth/login', {email,password})`, stores token+user in localStorage, then calls `window.patelApp.agent.setCredentials(getApiUrl(), token)`.
- On mount, it restores from localStorage: if token, calls `/auth/profile` to validate, and re-registers agent credentials.
- The agent auto-starts from main process using `agent-credentials.json` regardless of renderer state.

The plan:
- New setup flow: AgentKey screen. On submit: `POST /auth/agent-key` with `{ agentKey }`. Response: `{ success, data: { token, user } }`. Save token+user to localStorage (for renderer), and call `agent.setCredentials(apiUrl, token)` (for main process persistence + auto-start). Then navigate to dashboard.
- On app open (main process): if `agent-credentials.json` exists, auto-start agent (already done). Renderer: currently it restores from localStorage. generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// CORE MODELS
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  name      String
  settings  Json?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  users         User[]
  customers     Customer[]
  orders        Order[]
  printers      Printer[]
  pricingRules  PricingRule[]
  orderFiles    OrderFile[]
  printJobs     PrintJob[]

  @@map("shops")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId       String
  email        String
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("OPERATOR") // OWNER, MANAGER, OPERATOR, CUSTOMER
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])

  @@unique([shopId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId    String
  name      String
  phone     String?
  email     String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  shop   Shop    @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  orders Order[]

  @@map("customers")
}

model Order {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  token         Int?
  customerId    String?
  shopId        String
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, APPROVED, PRINTING, COMPLETED, REJECTED
  paymentStatus String   @default("UNPAID")  // UNPAID, PAID, REFUNDED
  paymentMethod String?
  totalPrice    Float    @default(0)
  discount      Float    @default(0)
  tax           Float    @default(0)
  notes         String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt    DateTime?
  printedAt     DateTime?

  shop      Shop        @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id])
  customer  Customer?   @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])
  files     OrderFile[]
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@unique([shopId, token])
  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@index([shopId, token])

display.text:
# Render deployment config for Patel AutoPrint
# Free tier: web service (sleeps after 15 min idle) + free PostgreSQL (256 MB, 90-day expiry)

# --- PostgreSQL database (free tier) — top-level key, NOT inside services ---
databases:
  - name: patel-autoprint-db
    databaseName: patel_autoprint
    user: patel
    plan: free
    ipAllowList: [] # empty = internal connections only (Render sets this)

# --- Services (web / worker / cron / static only) ---
services:
  # Node.js backend — also serves the built frontend from ../frontend/dist
  - type: web
    name: patel-autoprint
    runtime: node
    plan: free
    region: oregon # change to frankfurt / singapore if closer to you
    branch: main
    rootDir: backend
    buildCommand: npm install && npx prisma generate
    startCommand: npm run start
    healthCheckPath: /api/health
    envVars:
      - key: NODE_ENV
        value: production
      - key: PORT
        value: 5000
      - key: DATABASE_URL
        fromDatabase:
          name: patel-autoprint-db
          property: connectionString
      - key: JWT_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: CORS_ORIGIN
        value: "*"
      - key: FRONTEND_DIR
        value: ../frontend/dist

# Deploy Patel AutoPrint to the Cloud (Free)

This makes the server run 24/7 in the cloud so **you never have to keep this PC on**.
The printer agents on each shop PC just connect to the cloud URL.

> **Free Postgres expires after 90 days** — re-create it or move to Supabase/Neon (free, no expiry) when that happens.

---

## Part 1 — Push code to GitHub (do this ONCE)

You need a free GitHub account: https://github.com/signup

1. Go to https://github.com/new
2. **Repository name:** `patel-autoprint`
3. Keep it **Public** (or Private — either works)
4. **Do NOT** add a README / .gitignore / license (we already have them)
5. Click **Create repository**
6. On the next page, copy the commands under **"…or push an existing repository from the command line"**

   They look like:
   ```
   git remote add origin https://github.com/<your-user>/patel-autoprint.git
   git branch -M main
   git push -u origin main
   ```
7. Run those 3 commands in a terminal **inside this project folder**
   (`C:\Users\mayank\Documents\New OpenCode Project\patel-autoprint`)

> If you'd rather not use the terminal, install [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com),
> add the local repository (File → Add Local Repository → pick this folder), then click **Publish**.

---

## Part 2 — Deploy on Render (do this ONCE)

You need a free Render account: https://dashboard.render.com/ (sign up with your GitHub)

1. Click **New +** → **Blueprint**
2. Connect your GitHub and select the `patel-autoprint` repo
3. Render reads `render.yaml` automatically — it will create:
   - a **PostgreSQL** database (`patel-autoprint-db`, free)
   - a **Web Service** (`patel-autoprint`, free)
4. Click **Apply** / **Deploy**

Render will then automatically:
- install dependencies
- generate the Prisma client
- create the database tables (`prisma db push`)
- seed the demo shop + admin (`prisma db seed`)
- start the server

**First deploy takes 3–5 minutes.** Watch the logs in the Render dashboard.

---

## Part 3 — Your live URL

When the deploy finishes, Render gives you a URL like:

```
https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com
```

- **Admin panel:** open that URL → log in with
  `admin@patelautoprint.com` / `admin123`
- **Customer uploads:** same URL (the customer portal)
- **Share that URL** with customers instead of the Cloudflare tunnel link.

> To use a custom domain later (e.g. `print.yourshop.com`), go to the Web Service →
> **Settings → Custom Domain** in Render (paid add-on) or point a domain at it.

---

## Part 4 — Point each shop PC's agent at the cloud

On every shop PC that has a printer:

1. Copy the `agent/` folder there (just that folder)
2. Install deps: `cd agent` then `npm install`
3. Configure it:
   ```
   node index.js --setup
   ```
   - **Server URL** → paste your Render URL (e.g. `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com`)
   - **Email / Password** → the shop admin login
4. Run it: `node index.js` (keep the window open while the shop is open)

That's it — the agent now prints jobs from the cloud, and **this dev PC can stay off**.

---

## Changing the code later

After you edit files here:
```
git add -A
git commit -m "your change"
git push
```
Render auto-redeploys on every push.
(If you change the frontend, rebuild it first: `cd frontend && npm run build`.)

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|----------|-----|
| Deploy fails on DB step | In Render → Web Service → **Manual Deploy** after the DB is created |
| Admin login fails | The seed creates `admin@patelautoprint.com`/`admin123`. Re-run seed from Render shell: `npx prisma db seed` |
| Agent says "connection refused" | Check the Server URL in `agent/config.json` matches your Render URL exactly (https://…) |
| Free Postgres expired (90 days) | Create a new Postgres in Render, copy its Internal URL into the Web Service `DATABASE_URL`, redeploy |
| Server sleeps / slow first print | Normal on free tier; the agent retries. Upgrade to a paid instance for always-on |

Let me design the subscription check helper:
```js
async function getSubscriptionStatus(shopId) {
  const sub = await prisma.subscription.findUnique({ where: { shopId } });
  if (!sub) return { active: true, status: 'ACTIVE', plan: 'FREE' }; // no sub = default free
  const end = sub.endDate ? new Date(sub.endDate) : null;
  const now = new Date();
  if (sub.status === 'SUSPENDED' || sub.status === 'CANCELLED') {
    return { active: false, status: sub.status, plan: sub.plan, endDate: end ? end.toISOString() : null, daysLeft: 0 };
  }
  if (end && end < now) {
    return { active: false, status: 'EXPIRED', plan: sub.plan, endDate: end.toISOString(), daysLeft: 0 };
  }
  let daysLeft = null;
  if (end) {
    daysLeft = Math.ceil((end - now) / (1000*60*60*24));
    if (daysLeft < 0) daysLeft = 0;
  }
  return { active: true, status: 'ACTIVE', plan: sub.plan, endDate: end ? end.toISOString() : null, daysLeft };
}
```
