parts.text:
## Objective
- Evolve Patel AutoPrint into a subscription product: add a **super admin panel** (`/superadmin`) for the tool vendor to monitor shops, add/delete shops, and generate/rotate agent keys, with manual subscription billing.
- Expired/suspended subscriptions must block printing. Desktop app must show a 5-day countdown notice before expiry and suspend after.

## Important Details
- Repo `contactkanix-commits/patel-autoprint`, branch `main`. Live backend `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com`. **Render auto-deploy is NOT triggering on push** (verified: new `/api/agent/key-login` endpoint was pushed/on-remote yet still returns 404 after ~45+ min of polling; uptime kept growing → no restart). User must do **Manual Deploy** on Render after the next push.
- Super admin credentials planned: `superadmin@patelautoprint.com` / `superadmin123` (seeded; idempotent, runs every start; overridable via `SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD` env).
- Shop owner legacy login (`admin@patelautoprint.com`/`admin123`) kept as fallback; settings page has an Agent Key card.
- Agent key format `PAP-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`; `Shop.agentKey` unique; backfilled for existing shops at startup (`ensureAgentKeys`).
- `POST /api/agent/key-login` returns 365-day JWT (`expiresIn: '365d'`), attaches `subscription`, blocks with 403 `SUBSCRIPTION_SUSPENDED` when inactive.
- Subscription model: `plan` (FREE/STARTER/PROFESSIONAL/ENTERPRISE), `status` (ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/CANCELLED), `price`, `endDate`, `maxPrinters`; helper `getSubscriptionStatus(shopId)` derives `{active, status, plan, price, endDate, daysLeft, maxPrinters}` — ACTIVE until endDate; `daysLeft` computed via `Math.ceil(msLeft/day)`, floors at 1; EXPIRED/SUSPENDED/CANCELLED → `active:false`.
- Desktop must pass override token into `getSubscriptionStatus` to get raw `status` (LOCAL flags) independent of date-derived EXPIRED (date is overridden → `end.getTime() < now.getTime()` false when endDate overridden far-future; also date `endDate` from DB may have TZ issues — `new Date(string)` caveat).
- Key-login activation already wired in desktop: `ActivationPage.jsx` (route `/activate`), `AuthContext.activate(agentKey)` → `POST /api/agent/key-login`, stores token; `agentSetCredentials` runs. `api.js` interceptor redirects 401 → `/login` (kept for legacy fallback; not yet redirected to `/activate`).
- `User.shopId` now optional (`shop Shop?`, `onDelete: Cascade`); `Subscription` model added with all `Shop.*` child relations + `Shop.subscription`; `serialize` route sets `subscription` when `user.shopId`; `Printer`/`PricingRule` relations use `onDelete: Cascade`. `Printer` has `paperSizes Json @default("[\"A4\"]")`; `routeJob`/`routeJobForMode(mode, printers, paperSize)` (job.paperSize) prefers paperSizes-matched ONLINE printers else falls back to any ONLINE then all.
- Local printer discovery (WIN32 `Get-CimInstance Win32_Printer`, filter virtual printers): `1 no`, `3 no parul` (Canon WSD, status UNKNOWN, default), `iR-ADV 6575 III`, `Xerox EXi 570 Print Server` (IP 192.168.31.175, ONLINE). Manual capability/paper-size toggles ONLY (no driver auto-detect).
- Local Postgres at `localhost:5432` reachable (port open test passed; ODBC driver missing is ignorable); schema pushed with `--accept-data-loss` (remove stale `Agent`/`Plan` tables). Node v24, `@prisma/client` 5.22.0. Working dir suffix `node_modules` (`C:\...\patel-autoprint\node_modules`).
- Render v1: `render.yaml` — web service `patel-autoprint`, start `npm run start` (prisma generate + db push + seed + node), health `/api/health`. Static frontend `frontend/dist`; `backend/package.json` `"build": "npx prisma generate"`. frontend removal of admin happened earlier; app now serves at `frontend/dist` with `SUPERADMIN_DIST` too.
- Superadmin routes live in `backend/src/server.js` (before SPA catch-all); use `authenticate` + new `requireSuperAdmin` (middleware in `auth.js`).
- Superadmin SPA (to build) expected at `superadmin/` (path `path.join(__dirname,'..','..','superadmin','dist')`), served under `/superadmin` with `app.get('/superadmin/*')` fallback; watch `app.use('/superadmin', express.static(SUPERADMIN_DIST))`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backend schema changed (opt-in superadmin): `Shop.agentKey`, `Subscription`, optional `User.shopId` cascades applied locally. `ensureSubscriptions()` creates default FREE ACTIVE subscriptions; register route generates `agentKey`.
- `requireSuperAdmin` added to `backend/src/middleware/auth.js`; backend syntax check OK.
- Superadmin API routes added with manual billing + key generate/rotate/delete: stats, shops list (q filter, `_count` order/printer/user), shop detail (+lastOrder/recentJobs/completed), POST create shop+owner+subscription, PUT update, DELETE cascade, POST regenerate-key, change-password.
- `seed.js` refactored to idempotent superadmin ensure + subscription for demo shop; `localPostgres` db push `--accept-data-loss` succeeded (removed stale Agent/Plan, added columns); `prisma generate` available.
- `getSubscriptionStatus` + `requireActiveSubscription` added to `server.js`; applied to `/api/agent/jobs`, `/api/agent/jobs/:id/file`, `PUT /api/agent/jobs/:id/status`; agent jobs response now `{success,data,subscription}`.
- Superadmin SPA dist serving wired in backend (`SUPERADMIN_DIST`, `/superadmin` static + `/superadmin/*` history fallback).
- Desktop `ActivationPage.jsx` created + routed (`/activate`), `AuthContext` has `activate()`, fallback session restore reads `agent.getCredentials()` store; 401 interceptor still → `/login`.
- Existing `PrintersPage` fully rewritten: manual color/duplex paper-size toggle flow.
- Agent key settings card added to `SettingsPage.jsx` (copy/regenerate via new endpoints).

### Active
- `node -e` Prisma list-table check failed (PowerShell `$` interpolation in quoted `-e` — must escape `$queryRaw` as `` `$queryRaw `` or use single-quoted Python-style here-string; not yet re-run).
- Local seed failing at `prisma.shop.deleteMany` — FK violation `Agent_shopId_fkey` from leftover `Agent` table on old local DB (needs `--accept-data-loss` push again or `DROP TABLE "Agent","Plan"` + `prisma db push`).
- Need to apply remaining backend schema changes for subscription model against local DB and re-seed after cleanup.

### Blocked
- Render auto-deploy not running after push (as above). Render manual deploy needed by user.
- Local verification pending until `Agent`/`Plan` tables removed properly and seed runs.
- No `gh` CLI; no `RENDER_API_KEY` env; no API key to trigger deploy programmatically.

## Next Move
1. Drop leftover local `Agent`/`Plan` tables (or `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` again) and re-run `node prisma/seed.js` until it succeeds.
2. Start backend locally (`npm run dev` in `backend/`) and verify both flows:
   - superadmin login + shops CRUD + key generate/regenerate + subscription update,
   - shop key-login activation with `subscription` payload; expired/suspended rejection.
3. Build superadmin React SPA (`superadmin/` — login, dashboard with stats/status counts, shops table, create/edit/delete, key copy/regenerate, subscription form, change password), pointing API at Render URL; wire Vite build to `superadmin/dist`.
4. Update `Desktop `kz` files`: add subscription countdown banner + expired/suspended blocking in `AuthContext`/`App`/`AgentPage`; pass override token to `getSubscriptionStatus`.
5. Commit+push, then tell user to **Manual Deploy** on Render dashboard; verify `key-login` 401/403 and superadmin endpoints live.

## Relevant Files
- `backend/prisma/schema.prisma`: Shop.agentKey, Subscription, User.shopId? cascades, Printer paperSizes.
- `backend/prisma/seed.js`: superadmin ensure + shop/subs idempotent seed.
- `backend/src/server.js`: all auth/superadmin/subscription/agent routes + `ensureAgentKeys`/`ensureSubscriptions`/`getSubscriptionStatus`/`requireActiveSubscription`.
- `backend/src/middleware/auth.js`: `authenticate` sets `req.user`; `requireRole`; new `requireSuperAdmin`.
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/ActivationPage.jsx`: new key-entry activation screen.
- `desktop/src/renderer/AuthContext.jsx`: `activate()` + session restore via agent credential store.
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/admin/SettingsPage.jsx`: agent key copy/regenerate card.
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/admin/PrintersPage.jsx`: manual capability/paper-size chip toggles + connect/disconnect.
- `desktop/electron/main.js` / `preload.js` / `printers.js`: IPC + printer discovery.
- `superadmin/`: SPA to build for vendor (not created yet).
- `render.yaml` / `DEPLOY.md`: Render config; automatic deploy expected but not working reliably.
- `backend/.env`: local Postgres URL + local JWT/port.

Results analysis:
1. Superadmin login works. ✓
2. `/api/superadmin/stats` → 500 error with empty body. Bug!
3. `/api/superadmin/shops` → returns `data` as an ARRAY (not `{ shops: [...] }` as my smoke script assumed). So the route returns `res.json({success, data: <array>})`. That's fine, but my smoke assumed `data.shops`. Not a bug in the API, just my script. BUT the 500 on stats is a real bug.
4. Shop detail `/api/superadmin/shops/:id` with correct id worked. ✓
5. Create shop → 400 with empty body. The response body was empty because my Call function reads the error stream... Actually 400 with empty body — the route probably responds with JSON but reading failed? The BODY is empty. Hmm, Invoke-RestMethod on 400 throws, and my handler reads the response stream. It got empty. Could be the response wasn't JSON or the body wasn't read properly. Actually — the issue: `Invoke-RestMethod` with a 400: `$_.Exception.Response.GetResponseStream()` — sometimes with Invoke-RestMethod the response body is already consumed. But that would give empty body for ALL errors, and stats 500 also gave empty body. So my error-reading is unreliable. The HTTP codes are what matter: stats=500, create=400.

So real bugs:
- `/api/superadmin/stats` → 500.

This is getting complex; the current approach (server blocks + UI banners + disabled start) satisfies the requirement.

Wait — if I stop polling on 403, when the subscription is reactivated, the agent won't resume until user restarts it. The current behavior retries every 5s and would recover automatically on reactivation. Better to keep retrying (server auto-recovers). Leave as is.

## Objective
- Add a **super admin panel** (`/superadmin`) for the tool vendor to create/manage shops, generate/rotate agent keys, and perform manual subscription billing (plan, price, status, endDate, maxPrinters).
- Enforce paid subscriptions: expired/suspended blocks desktop printing; desktop shows 5-day expiry countdown. Deployable on Render with a live DB that still holds legacy tables.

## Important Details
- Repo `contactkanix-commits/patel-autoprint`, branch `main`. Push `0bc5a2a..bbf1c35` then `bbf1c35..4dac937` succeeded.
- **Render auto-deploy is NOT triggering on push** — live server at `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com` still runs the `b8448b3` build (`/api/agent/key-login` → 404, only legacy `/api/agent/login` exists). User has been doing **Manual Deploy → Deploy latest commit**, and it is **currently failing** (see Blocked).
- Superadmin credentials: `superadmin@patelautoprint.com` / `superadmin123` (seeded idempotently every start; override via `SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD` env).
- Local Postgres `localhost:5432` (usr/pass `postgres`); local DB `patel_autoprint` fully migrated/seeded and verified.
- **npm workspaces hoists deps to root `C:\...\patel-autoprint\node_modules`**; local `.bin` shims are broken (PowerShell error 800705af). Workaround used: `node node_modules/prisma/build/index.js <args>` run from workspace root, with `cwd` set to the app dir and `DATABASE_URL` in env; monorepo normally runs commands via `cmd /c "cd backend && npm run ..."` from root.
- Agent key format `PAP-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`, unique on `Shop.agentKey`; backfilled via `ensureAgentKeys`. `POST /api/agent/key-login` returns 365-day JWT plus `subscription`; blocks inactive subs with 403 `SUBSCRIPTION_SUSPENDED`. `getSubscriptionStatus(shopId)` derives `{active,status,plan,price,endDate,daysLeft,maxPrinters}` — `daysLeft` via `Math.ceil`, floors at 1; ACTIVE until endDate; EXPIRED/SUSPENDED/CANCELLED → `active:false`.
- Seed runs every production start and contains a multi-shop **merge path** (`Found N shops. Merging into one...`, keeps admin's shop, `deleteMany` of duplicate shops with legacy relation cleanup) plus `ensureAgentKeys`/`ensureSubscriptions`.
- `backend/package.json` start script was changed to `npx prisma generate && npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss && node prisma/seed.js && node src/server.js` (commit `4dac937`) because the Render DB still has legacy tables.
- Live probes confirmed which build is serving: old build owns `/api/auth/agent-key`, `/api/agent/key-login`; current build owns `/api/superadmin/*`, React admin SPA, `/superadmin` history fallback.
- Old builds that contained the SaaS `Agent`/`Plan`/`Notification`/`WhatsAppSession` models: `f6e66ea`, `73bd739`, `6214d1f`; current-era render.yaml tests hit `/api/agent/key-login` (404 on live = old build still running).
- `render.yaml`: web service `patel-autoprint`, runtime node, `rootDir: backend`, `build: npm install && npx prisma generate`, `start: npm run start`, health `/api/health`, free Postgres `patel-autoprint-db`; generated `JWT_SECRET`; `CORS_ORIGIN=*`.
- Local smoke test verified: superadmin login, stats, shops CRUD, agent key rotate (old key fails, new works), suspend→key-login 403, reactivate with endDate, password-change guard, non-superadmin blocked with 403.
- Desktop app (Electron + React in `desktop/`): primary flow is **agent key activation on first use** (`/activate` via `ActivationPage.jsx`), email/password login kept as fallback link (user was asked but left the question unanswered: "Agent key only vs Keep both" — **keep both**).
- Desktop renderer builds count: 11584 modules, chunk 565.38 kB → `dist/`. Superadmin SPA builds: 11578 modules, 503 kB → `superadmin/dist/`, detected by git (3 files: `dist/index.html`, asset JS, `dist/assets/`).
- `superadmin/vite.config.js` sets `base: '/superadmin/'` and dev port 5174; served by prod Express from `SUPERADMIN_DIST` at `/superadmin` with `app.get('/superadmin/*')` fallback (already in `backend/src/server.js`).
- `GET /api/auth/profile` includes `subscription` via `getSubscriptionStatus` — desktop `AuthContext.initAuth` fetches it after activation/login.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backend schema: `Shop.agentKey` unique, `Subscription`, optional `User.shopId` with cascade; `ensureAgentKeys`/`ensureSubscriptions`; `getSubscriptionStatus`; `requireActiveSubscription`; seed idempotent.
- Superadmin routes in `backend/src/server.js`: stats, shops CRUD, detail (+recentJobs/completedOrders), regenerate-key, change-password. `requireSuperAdmin` in `auth.js`.
- Fixed production bugs found in smoke tests: stats route had Prisma `include`+`select` crash (removed `include`); shop detail selected nonexistent `PrintJob.updatedAt` (removed it); PUT create-subscription path passed duplicate keys (simplified to `{shopId, ...subData}`).
- Local DB migrated (`--accept-data-loss`) → tables: customers, order_files, orders, pricing_rules, print_jobs, printers, shops, subscriptions, users. Seed ran: merged 3 shops into 1, `superadmin@patelautoprint.com` created; smoke test passed end-to-end.

- Desktop changes: `AuthContext` stores subscription in state + localStorage, polls every 5 min and on window focus via `/auth/profile`; `clearSession` also clears `subscription`; `api.js` 401 → `#/activate`; `AdminLayout` shows expiring banner (≤5 days) and blocked banner for SUSPENDED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED with `pt: '64px'` + removed double margin; `AgentPage` Start button disabled + red alert when `subscription.active === false`; AppBar chip shows "Agent BLOCKED".

- Live server still on old `b8448b3` build; `/api/agent/key-login` 404, `/superadmin` likely not served.
- Live probe of auth endpoints only: `/api/agent/login` 400, `/api/auth/agent-key` 404, `/api/agent/jobs` 404, `/api/auth/login` 400, `/api/settings/pricing` 404; health OK.

Reproduce the Render failure against the exact legacy DB state: write `b8448b3` schema via node (no BOM), reset/push to `patel_autoprint_legacy`, then run the full chain (prisma generate + db push --accept-data-loss + seed + server start) and capture the exact error; inspect seed merge path for a failing FK/token-uniqueness query.

3. Have the user run Manual Deploy; verify live via `POST /api/agent/key-login` and `GET /superadmin` once updated.

input.content:
# Desktop App Auto-Update Files

This folder is served by the backend at `/updates/` and is where the desktop
app looks for new versions (feed URL is configured in
`desktop/package.json` → `build.publish`).

To ship a new desktop app version:

1. Bump `version` in `desktop/package.json` (e.g. `1.0.1`).
2. Build and publish the installer:

   ```
   cd desktop
   npm run publish:win
   ```

3. Copy the generated files from `desktop/dist-electron/` into this folder:

   - `latest.yml`
   - `Patel AutoPrint Admin Setup <version>.exe`
   - `Patel AutoPrint Admin Setup <version>.exe.blockmap`

4. Commit and push. Render deploys, and every shop's desktop app auto-updates
   within ~15 seconds of launch (or within 4 hours while running).

NOTE: Files here are committed to the repo so they persist on Render. If you
later switch the feed to GitHub Releases or an S3 bucket, just change the
`publish.url` in `desktop/package.json` and stop committing files here.

Done — pushed `036c589`. Auto-update is implemented for every shop's desktop app:

**What's in place**

**How you ship each new version** (also written in `backend/updates/README.md`)
1. Bump `version` in `desktop/package.json` (e.g. `1.0.1`).
2. `cd desktop` then `npm run publish:win` (builds installer + publishes metadata).
3. Copy `latest.yml`, `Patel AutoPrint Admin Setup X.exe`, and `.exe.blockmap` from `desktop/dist-electron\` into `backend/updates\`.
4. Commit + push → Render deploys → every shop auto-updates.

- **Deploy the backend commit on Render** so `/updates/` exists on prod.
- **Clients must install via the Setup `.exe`** (auto-update only works on installer-based installs, not dev builds). Installers still show the SmartScreen "unknown publisher" warning until you add a code-signing cert.
CAN ITS WORK LIKE WHEAT EVER UPDATES WE DO ITS AUTOMATICALLY DONE IN SHOP ADMIN PANEL ?

The user asks: "CAN IT WORK LIKE WHENEVER UPDATES WE DO ITS AUTOMATICALLY DONE IN SHOP ADMIN PANEL?" — i.e., can updates be fully automatic so shop owners don't need to do anything.

The answer: Yes — that's exactly how it's configured. `autoDownload = true` and `autoInstallOnAppQuit = true` means:
- Update downloads automatically in the background.
- On app quit, it installs automatically.
- If the shop owner clicks "Update & Restart", it installs immediately.
- Otherwise, the next time the app closes/reopens, the new version is installed.

The only "manual" action on the vendor side: bump version, build, copy 3 files, push. The shop owner does nothing.

One consideration: if the shop owner never quits the app (it runs in tray/background for the agent), the update installs on next quit. To make it even more automatic, could force-install on quit regardless — that's already the case. If the app literally never closes, the update waits. Could add auto-restart after install after a delay, but that would interrupt the running agent (bad for a print shop that's actively printing). So install-on-quit is the right design.

So answer: Yes, fully automatic. Explain the flow briefly and the one edge case (if app stays open forever, update installs on close). Keep concise. No need to change code.

I should confirm the current config already achieves this. Yes: autoDownload=true, autoInstallOnAppQuit=true, check on launch + every 4h. So whenever vendor pushes a new version, all shops automatically update within 15s of app open (or within 4h while running), and install on next quit.

Keep it short.

Yes — that's exactly how it's set up. The shop owner does **nothing**:

1. You update `backend/updates/` with the new installer files (that's the only manual step, on your side).
2. Each shop app auto-checks: **15s after launch** and **every 4 hours** while running.
3. New version **downloads silently** in the background — no popup needed.
4. It **installs automatically when the app closes** (or when they click the "Update & Restart" button).

One honest caveat: the app runs in the background for printing, so if a shop never closes it, the update installs the next time it does close. Forcing an install mid-printing could break a live job, so install-on-close is the safe behavior — but the download is always already done in the background, so the switchover is instant.

The only thing you must remember per release: **bump the version** in `desktop/package.json` (if the version stays the same, the app thinks it's already up to date).

    if (files.length === 0) { toast.error('Please select files'); return; }
    if (!customerInfo.name || !customerInfo.phone) { toast.error('Please fill name and phone'); return; }
    setLoading(true);
    try {
      const formData = new FormData();
      files.forEach((f) => formData.append('files', f));
      formData.append('customerName', customerInfo.name);
      formData.append('customerPhone', customerInfo.phone);
      formData.append('customerEmail', customerInfo.email);

      const result = await api.post('/guest/upload', formData);

        setUploadedOrder(result.data);
        toast.success(`${result.data.files?.length || 0} file(s) analyzed!`);
        setActiveStep(1);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Upload failed');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

Flow design (as user described):
1. Customer messages the shop's WhatsApp number with files.
2. Meta sends a webhook (message event with media) to our backend.
3. Backend downloads the media files via Graph API, stores them in an uploads temp area, creates a WhatsApp session keyed by the customer's phone number (from the webhook).
4. Backend sends a WhatsApp reply with a link like `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/s/<shopSlug>?wa=<sessionToken>` (needs the shop context — the WhatsApp number belongs to a shop; need a mapping from WhatsApp phone number → shopId).
5. Customer opens the link → CustomerPortal loads with `?wa=<token>` → fetches pending WhatsApp files for that token → shows them pre-loaded in the flow (upload step shows the files already, or jumps to configure step), user configures per-file settings and places order.

Files are binary — we'd store them on disk under `backend/uploads/whatsapp/<sessionId>/` and a DB record `WhatsAppMessage`/`WhatsAppSession` with id, token, customerNumber, files metadata, createdAt, expiresAt, claimedAt.
- Webhook endpoints:
  - `GET /api/whatsapp/webhook` — hub.challenge verification (echo challenge + hub.verify_token).
  - `POST /api/whatsapp/webhook` — receive message events.
- On media message: download media via `GET https://graph.facebook.com/v19.0/{media_id}` with Bearer token → returns URL → download binary → store file.
- Also handle text messages (e.g., customer sends "hi") → reply with instructions + link (once they've sent files, reply with the link). Better: whenever we receive media, reply with link. If they send no files yet and just text, reply with a "send files" instruction. To reply, need `POST https://graph.facebook.com/v19.0/{phone_number_id}/messages` with a text message.

  slug      String?  @unique
  agentKey  String?  @unique

Now I understand the pipeline. Let me plan the implementation.

Key design:
- **WhatsAppSession model** (new): stores inbound WhatsApp files for a customer before they claim them in the portal.
  - id, token (unique, the ?wa= value), shopId, customerPhone, customerName (from profile name?), files Json (array of {originalName, storagePath, fileType, size, mediaId}), status (NEW/CLAIMED/EXPIRED), expiresAt, createdAt, claimedAt.
- **Shop.whatsappNumber** String? (unique) — maps the shop's WhatsApp number to the shop. On inbound webhook, look up shop by whatsappNumber.
- Webhook routes:
  - `GET /api/whatsapp/webhook` — verify: echo `hub.challenge` if `hub.verify_token` matches `WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN`.
  - `POST /api/whatsapp/webhook` — parse `entry[].changes[].value.messages[]`. For each message with `type === 'image'` (or document) → download media, save, add to session (create if not exists), then reply with the portal link. For text/others → reply with instructions.
- WhatsApp service (`backend/src/services/whatsapp.js`):
  - `downloadMedia(mediaId)` → Graph API → returns { path, size, mimeType, filename? }
  - `sendText(phoneNumberId, to, body)` → POST Graph API.
  - Use `node-fetch` or built-in `fetch` (Node 18+). Check node version / package. backend package.json? Let me check if `axios` is available in backend. Likely yes. I'll use `fetch` global (Node 18+) to avoid new deps. Let me check node version available and backend package.json.
- Claim endpoint: `POST /api/guest/whatsapp/:token/claim`:
  - find session by token, not claimed, not expired.
  - create customer (by phone), create order with token, for each session file: analyze (analyzeFile with fileType), create OrderFile (storagePath = session file path), settings default like upload.
  - mark session CLAIMED (or delete).
  - return order (same shape as guest upload → frontend reuses everything).
- Frontend:
  - Read `useSearchParams` for `wa` token.
  - On mount if token: call claim; on success set uploadedOrder, customerInfo.phone from session (return it), setActiveStep(1). Show a banner "Files received from WhatsApp — configure print settings". On failure (expired/claimed) show message.
  - Reset should clear wa? On new order, keep wa cleared so they don't re-claim. Actually handleNewOrder resets; if we keep wa in URL, a re-claim would 400. We can set step 0 and clear token state; but the URL still has ?wa=. Better: after claim, `history.replaceState` to strip the token, or use `setSearchParams({})`. I'll strip it after claim.
  - Also, the upload step: when claimed, we skip straight to step 1 (Configure). Good.
- Superadmin: add `whatsappNumber` field to Shop. Update create/update handlers and ShopDetail form. Also show in shops list? Optional. I'll add to create/update handler (schema validation) and ShopDetail an editable text field.

Actually, to limit scope creep, maybe just allow setting whatsappNumber via superadmin shop edit. Let me check superadmin create/update handlers and ShopDetail to integrate.

Also `.env.example` update + setup doc.

Also need to consider: Media download from Meta requires the access token and returns a URL that's valid temporarily; we download binary to `backend/uploads/whatsapp/<sessionToken>/<filename>`.

Filename: Meta media endpoint returns `filename` only for documents? For images it may not include filename; we can generate a name from mime/extension.

Document messages: WhatsApp "document" type includes filename. Images: no filename — we create `image_<timestamp>.<ext>`.

WhatsApp file receiving is built and tested. Here's what's in place:

**Flow:** Customer sends files to the shop's WhatsApp → webhook downloads them → WhatsApp auto-replies a link like `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/s/patel-autoprint?wa=TOKEN` → opening it pre-loads their files into the Configure step → they set print options, pay, done. No access code.

**Backend**
- `services/whatsapp.js` — Meta Cloud API: media download + text replies (uses global `fetch`)
- `GET /api/whatsapp/webhook` — Meta verification (echoes challenge on correct token, 403 otherwise)
- `POST /api/whatsapp/webhook` — receives messages; accepts image/document, rejects unsupported types with a WhatsApp reply, dedupes by message id, replies the portal link (supports `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` signature check)
- `POST /api/guest/whatsapp/:token/claim` — turns a session into a real order reusing the same analyzer pipeline (60-page sample verified: order token 2, pages/color counted, correct shop + customer). Re-claim → 409, expired → 410
- New `Shop.whatsappNumber` (unique) + `WhatsAppSession` model; superadmin create/edit sets the number
- `.env.example` updated with `WHATSAPP_*` + `PUBLIC_URL` vars

**Frontend**
- `CustomerPortal` reads `?wa=`, claims the job, jumps to Configure with a "Files received via WhatsApp" banner, strips the token from the URL; invalid/used links show a clear error

**Tested locally:** webhook verify (403/200), webhook POST (200), claim end-to-end, superadmin set/reset `whatsappNumber`. Both `frontend/dist` and `superadmin/dist` rebuilt.

**To go live you'll need to (Meta setup — free):**
1. Register the shop's number in the **WhatsApp Business app**
2. `developers.facebook.com` → create a **Business app** → add the **WhatsApp** product → add the number
3. Note the **Phone Number ID** and generate an access token (dashboard token is temporary; create a **System User** for a permanent long-lived one)
4. On Render add env vars: `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`, `WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN` (pick a secret), `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` (optional), `PUBLIC_URL=https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com`
5. In Meta webhook settings: callback URL `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/whatsapp/webhook` + your verify token, subscribe to **messages**
6. In superadmin → edit your shop, set **WhatsApp number** (digits only with country code, e.g. `919876543210`) — must match the Meta number exactly

Now I'll create WhatsAppPage.jsx following the same conventions:
- Header with WhatsApp icon, title, status chip
- If state === 'waiting-for-qr': show QR image + instructions + logout/unlink button
- If state === 'connected': green card with linked number + "Unlink" button + explanation that files are being received
- If state === 'connecting': spinner + "Connecting..."
- If state === 'idle'/'closed'/'error': show a "Start WhatsApp" button (if error shows message). Note: state idle after logout or on launch without session (QR comes when connecting). Actually when not paired and no session, `start()` → connecting → QR. When paired with saved session, connecting → connected. So idle means not started. The page should auto-start on mount (call window.patelApp.whatsapp.start()) if state is idle and not connected and not waiting-for-qr. But auto-start could fail if not logged in. Let me auto-start once on mount, and show a retry button if it errors.

Let me design states clearly:
- `state` values: 'idle', 'connecting', 'waiting-for-qr', 'connected', 'closed'
- Error text in `error`.

UI:
- Header: WhatsApp icon, "WhatsApp File Receiving", chip with current state.
- Card 1: Status area.
  - connected: green check "Receiving files as +<phone>" + note "Files sent to this number are saved and a portal link is auto-replied."
  - waiting-for-qr: QR image centered + steps.
  - connecting: spinner + "Connecting to WhatsApp..."
  - idle/closed: info + Start button (or "Retry"). If error, show Alert.
- Card 2: How it works (3 steps: customers send files, app replies link, they tap to configure+pay).
- Card 3: Activity log (same style as agent).

Also "Unlink / Disconnect" button with confirm. When unlinked, state → idle, and page shows Start button.

On mount: subscribe to onStatus, getStatus initial. Then if state is idle and not already started, auto-call start. Track "userUnlinked" to avoid auto-restart loop after logout — if user clicks unlink, don't auto-start again. I'll set a ref `autoStartedRef` — only auto-start once. After logout, state idle; user can click "Link again".

Actually on first mount, if not paired, auto-start will trigger QR — good. If paired, it'll connect automatically — good (client already started at app launch via main.js, so state would be connecting/connected already). The start() call in page handles "already running" gracefully ({ success: false, message: 'already running' }).

Let me handle: on mount, get status. If status.state === 'idle' (not started), call start() once. If it's 'connecting'/'waiting-for-qr'/'connected', do nothing.

However, there's one more concern: `jsqr`? `open`? Those are transitive deps. Also `qrcode` needs canvas? No — `qrcode` core (QRCode.toDataURL) uses `pngjs`, pure JS. Good.

Now, electron-builder will include production dependencies automatically. The `files` array lists app files; node_modules are added by electron-builder automatically (production deps). But baileys has a LOT of deps and could trigger rebuild scripts. Should be fine.

Actually, there IS a subtle issue: electron-builder needs to NOT bundle devDependencies. electron (the devDep) is automatically excluded. Good.

Electron 28 = Node 18.18. `fetch` (undici) global: added in Node 18.0 (experimental, stable 21; available in 18 with experimental warning but functional). pdfjs-dist is hoisted to the repo root `node_modules` (npm workspaces/hoisting). The build dir has `pdf.min.js` and `pdf.worker.min.js` (v3 style, not `.mjs`). This is pdfjs-dist v3.11.174, which is a CommonJS build (UMD). It also has a `legacy/build` dir.

For pdfjs-dist v3:
- Import: `import * as pdfjsLib from 'pdfjs-dist';` — but in a Vite ESM app, importing 'pdfjs-dist' resolves to the CJS `build/pdf.js`? pdfjs-dist v3 has `main: build/pdf.js` in package.json. Vite can handle CJS→ESM via commonjs plugin (esbuild). It works.
- Worker: `pdfjsLib.GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc = new URL('pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.js', import.meta.url).toString();` — with Vite, `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` bundles the asset. The worker is a plain script (not a module) for v3 — needs `new Worker(workerSrc, { type: 'classic' })`. pdfjs v3 by default uses classic worker? GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc + default creates `new Worker(workerSrc)`. In v3, the worker file is `pdf.worker.min.js` (classic). Should work.

However, there's a known Vite issue: importing pdfjs-dist v3 in ESM. Many projects use:
```
import { getDocument, GlobalWorkerOptions } from 'pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs';
GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc = 'pdf.worker.mjs';
```
But v3.11 doesn't have `.mjs` files (that's v4). v3.11 has CJS `pdf.js`/`pdf.worker.js` in `build` and `legacy/build`.

function Step2Configure({ files, fileSettings, setFileSettings }) {
  const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState(0);

  const getSettings = (fileIndex) => {
    const dbSettings = files[fileIndex]?.settings || {};
    const localSettings = fileSettings[fileIndex] || {};
    const merged = { ...dbSettings, ...localSettings };
    if (merged.colorMode === 'auto') merged.colorMode = 'bw';
    if (!merged.colorMode && isImageFile(files[fileIndex])) merged.colorMode = 'color';
    return merged;
  };

  const allImages = files.length > 0 && files.every((f) => isImageFile(f));
  const totalImages = files.filter((f) => isImageFile(f)).length;
  const imageUrls = files.map((f) => fileUrl(f));

  // Apply a setting to every image file at once (contact-sheet mode)
  const updateAllImageSettings = (key, value) => {
    setFileSettings((prev) => {
      const next = { ...prev };
      files.forEach((f, i) => {
        if (isImageFile(f)) next[i] = { ...next[i], [key]: value };
      });
      return next;
    });
  };

  const updateSetting = (fileIndex, key, value) => {
    setFileSettings((prev) => ({
      ...prev,
      [fileIndex]: { ...prev[fileIndex], [key]: value },
    }));
  };

  const addSection = (fileIndex) => {
    const current = getSettings(fileIndex);
    const sections = current.sections || [];
    const totalPages = files[fileIndex]?.pageCount || 1;
    const lastSection = sections[sections.length - 1];
    const startPage = lastSection ? lastSection.endPage + 1 : 1;
    if (startPage > totalPages) {
      toast.error('No more pages available');
      return;
    }
    updateSetting(fileIndex, 'sections', [...sections, {
      id: Date.now(),
      startPage,
      endPage: startPage,
      paperSize: current.paperSize || 'A4',
      colorMode: current.colorMode || 'bw',
      printStyle: current.printStyle || 'single',
      copies: current.copies || 1,
      pagesPerSheet: current.pagesPerSheet || 1,
    }]);
  };

  const updateSection = (fileIndex, sectionIndex, key, value) => {
    const current = getSettings(fileIndex);
    const sections = [...(current.sections || [])];
    sections[sectionIndex] = { ...sections[sectionIndex], [key]: value };
    updateSetting(fileIndex, 'sections', sections);
  };

  const removeSection = (fileIndex, sectionIndex) => {
    const current = getSettings(fileIndex);
    updateSetting(fileIndex, 'sections', (current.sections || []).filter((_, i) => i !== sectionIndex));
  };

  const s = getSettings(activeTab);
  const currentFile = files[activeTab];

      {files.length > 1 && (

            <Chip

              label={file.originalName?.substring(0, 20) || file.name?.substring(0, 20)}
              onClick={() => setActiveTab(index)}
              color={activeTab === index ? 'primary' : 'default'}
              variant={activeTab === index ? 'filled' : 'outlined'}
              size="small"
            />
          ))}
        </Box>
      )}

      {allImages && (
        <Box sx={{ mb: 1.5 }}>
          <Typography
            variant="caption"
            fontWeight={700}
            color="text.secondary"
            sx={{ display: 'block', mb: 0.5, textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: 0.6 }}
          >
            Photos per page
          </Typography>
          <Box sx={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(6, minmax(0, 1fr))', gap: 0.75 }}>
            {pagesPerSheetOptions.filter((n) => n > 1).map((n) => {
              const selected = (s.pagesPerSheet || 1) === n;
              return (
                <ButtonBase
                  key={n}
                  onClick={() => updateAllImageSettings('pagesPerSheet', n)}
                  sx={{
                    py: 1,
                    borderRadius: 1.5,
                    border: '1.5px solid',
                    borderColor: selected ? 'primary.main' : 'divider',
                    bgcolor: selected ? 'primary.main' : 'background.paper',
                    color: selected ? 'primary.contrastText' : 'text.primary',
                    fontWeight: 800,
                    fontSize: '0.9rem',
                    transition: 'all 0.15s',
                    '&:hover': { borderColor: 'primary.main' },
                  }}
                >
                  {n}
                </ButtonBase>
              );
            })}
          </Box>
        </Box>
      )}

      {currentFile && (
        <Card variant="outlined">
          <CardContent sx={{ p: { xs: 1.5, sm: 2 }, '&:last-child': { pb: 1.5 } }}>
            <Typography variant="caption" color="text.secondary" display="block" sx={{ mb: 1.5 }}>
              {currentFile.originalName || currentFile.name} — {currentFile.pageCount || '?'} page{currentFile.pageCount === 1 ? '' : 's'}
            </Typography>

            <Grid container spacing={2}>
              <Grid item xs={12} sm={5}>
                <PrintPreview
                  file={currentFile}
                  settings={s}
                  allImages={allImages}
                  totalImages={totalImages}
                  imageUrls={allImages ? imageUrls : [fileUrl(currentFile)]}
                />

                <OptionGroup
                  label="Paper Size"

                  value={s.paperSize || 'A4'}

                  options={paperSizes.map((ps) => ({ value: ps, label: ps }))}

                <Box sx={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: '1fr 1fr', gap: 2 }}>

Now I have a good understanding of the current portal. Let me also quickly check Step1Upload and the bottom action bar for completeness. Actually I have enough. Let me formulate my opinion.

Current issues (what makes it hard for a customer):
1. **Too many settings up front** — Paper size, Color, Sides, Orientation, Copies, Pages/Sheet, Page range, AND "Print Sections (advanced)" with add/remove section rows. Most customers just want: how many copies, color or B/W, and for photos "how many per page".
2. **Two competing ways to set photos-per-page** — a big "Photos per page" quick row (2,4,6,9,16) AND a "Pages/Sheet" dropdown in the card AND per-section N-up. Confusing duplication.
3. **Print Sections (advanced)** visible on the same screen — very confusing for normal customers. Should be hidden behind "Advanced options" toggle or removed for the customer.
4. **Per-file tabs when multiple files** — reasonable, but combined with per-file section editing it's a lot.
5. Terminology: "Pages/Sheet", "Sides → Single-sided/Double-sided", "Simplex/Duplex", "N-up" — shop jargon. Customers understand "Print on both sides", "photos per page", "color / black & white".
6. The page range text field with "e.g. 1-5, 8, 10-12" is technical.
7. Multiple option groups stacked (paper size, color, sides, orientation) with a preview — decent but the preview is on the left, options right; on mobile it stacks and everything is long.

# Desktop App Auto-Update Files

This folder is served by the backend at `/updates/` and is where the desktop
app looks for new versions (feed URL is configured in
`desktop/package.json` → `build.publish`).

To ship a new desktop app version:

1. Bump `version` in `desktop/package.json` (e.g. `1.0.1`).
2. Build and publish the installer:

   ```
   cd desktop
   npm run publish:win
   ```

3. Copy the generated files from `desktop/dist-electron/` into this folder:

   - `latest.yml`
   - `Patel AutoPrint Admin Setup <version>.exe`
   - `Patel AutoPrint Admin Setup <version>.exe.blockmap`

4. Commit and push. Render deploys, and every shop's desktop app auto-updates
   within ~15 seconds of launch (or within 4 hours while running).

NOTE: Files here are committed to the repo so they persist on Render. If you
later switch the feed to GitHub Releases or an S3 bucket, just change the
`publish.url` in `desktop/package.json` and stop committing files here.

Better idea: **two-stage**: First reduce payload size so normal compression gets under 100MB. OR use a lighter compression that's still better than "normal". NSIS supports `differentialPackage` (already), and compression options: "store", "normal", "maximum". 

Hmm, what about excluding the WhatsApp audio codecs that are wasm-heavy? @wasm-audio-decoders (8.4MB) + ogg-opus-decoder (9.7MB) + node-wav (7.2MB) — these are for processing voice notes in WhatsApp. Do we need all? Risky to remove.

Hmm wait, is it? Earlier I said 107MB. 107689432 bytes / 1e6 = 107.7 MB. GitHub uses 100 MiB = 104,857,600 bytes. So cut ~2.8MB.

This is a classic electron-updater NSIS error. It happens because when the installer (NSIS) runs at quit-time, it tries to kill the running app process, but the app doesn't close fully / the process is still running / is being held open.

Common causes and fixes:
1. The app has background processes that keep running (e.g., a child process, hidden window, tray icon, or a second instance).
2. The main process has a window/handler blocking quit — e.g., `before-quit` not firing, or the window is still open when the update installer launches.
3. electron-updater's default `quitAndInstall` behavior: it calls `app.quit()` then launches installer. But if the app takes too long to close (or doesn't), the NSIS installer complains.
4. A known issue: **when there's a browserWindow that isn't destroyed, or when `app.exit()` isn't called**, the NSIS `!exec` wait for process exit times out.

# Receiving Updates

After getting the initial "history" messages, let's get real-time messages and updates.

Baileys exposes these updates via the event emitter as well.

## Message events ​

### messages.upsert ​

This event provides you with messages that you get either on offline sync or in real time.

The type of upsert is provided as either `notify` or `append` .
Notify messages are usually the new messages, meanwhile append messages are everything else.

This event provides an array of `proto.IMessage` s, so make sure to handle every item in the array.

Look into the Handling Messages page to handle the IMessage properly.

As an example:

```
sock . ev . on ( 'messages.upsert' , ( { type ,  messages } ) => {  
 if ( type  == "notify" ) { // new messages  
 for ( const  message  of  messages ) {  
 // messages is an array, do not just handle the first message, you will miss messages  
 }
} else { // old already seen / handled messages  
 // handle them however you want to  
 }  
 } )
```

### messages.update ​

Whether the message got edited, deleted or something else happened (change of receipt /ack state), a message update will be fired.

### messages.delete ​

This event exists to declare the deletion of messages.

### messages.reaction ​

Whether a reaction was added or removed to a message

### message-receipt.update ​

This runs in groups and other contexts, where it tells you updates on who received/viewed/played messages.

## Chat events ​

### chats.upsert ​

This is triggered whenever a new chat is opened with you.

### chats.update ​

This is triggered on every message (to change the unread count), and to put the latest message / latest message timestamp in the chat object.

### chats.delete ​

This is triggered when the chat is deleted only.

### blocklist.set ​

### blocklist.update ​

Self-explanatory

### call ​
Universal event for call data (accept/decline/offer/timeout etc.)

## Contact events ​

### contacts.upsert ​

Upon the addition of a new contact to the main device's address book

### contacts.update ​

Upon the change of a saved contact's details

## Group events ​

### groups.upsert ​

When you are joined in a new group.

### groups.update ​

When metadata about the group changes.

### group-participants.update ​

When the participants of group change or their ranks change

There are known baileys issues with `messages.upsert` not triggering. The most relevant is issue #1936 (baileys 6.7.20) where messages aren't received if both sender/receiver official WhatsApp apps are offline — the server doesn't push the message (CB:receipt not received). This is a baileys v6 regression.

Our version is 6.6.0. This suggests baileys v6 has delivery problems. The well-known STABLE approach is baileys 6.7.x with `markOnlineOnConnect: true`... but the issue says that doesn't help for #1936.

Let me reconsider the whole approach. The user asks "can it work like whatsapp npm?" — they want the bot to reliably receive and reply.

Key considerations:
1. **The known-good approach** for this exact use case (receiving customer files, replying with links) is the older, battle-tested baileys 6.5.x/6.6.x... but v6 has these reported issues.

2. Actually — the MOST important realization: **the message delivery problem might be due to the baileys version being too new (6.6.0) with known regressions.** Downgrading to a widely-used stable version like `6.7.x` or `6.5.x`... hmm. Issue #1936 is on 6.7.20. So 6.7.20 has the issue too.

Let me think about what's actually happening with our connection. The bot is "Connected" but receives nothing. This matches issue #1936: messages are only pushed to the server if a device is "online" — WhatsApp's server routes messages to devices that are actively connected. If the bot's connection isn't fully registering as a recipient...

Actually — here's a KEY detail from the docs I found: "Emulating the Desktop app instead of the web: use `browser: Browsers.macOS('Desktop')` and `syncFullHistory: true`" — a Desktop-type connection "receive[s] more message history". Also, the docs mention `fireInitQueries` (default true).

Hmm. Let me reconsider. Actually the REAL question is why messages.upsert never fires. Given our log shows "Connected" and no message events, either:
(a) The server isn't pushing messages to this device.
(b) baileys isn't processing them.

Let me look at the ACTUAL delivery mechanism. In baileys, when a message arrives, the WS receives a node with tag 'message' or via 'action' with add/notify, and baileys emits messages.upsert. If the connection is healthy, it works. The known v6 issue #1936 is specifically about messages NOT being pushed when BOTH the sender and the number's official apps are offline — meaning the message sits on the server until someone's online.

In the user's test: the shop's primary phone (which scanned QR) — is it online? The user said "i linked the whatsapp and test it" — if the primary phone was offline when the customer sent the PDF, and if the baileys connection isn't receiving pushes (v6 regression), the message wouldn't arrive.

Hmm, but actually in multi-device mode, linked devices should receive pushes independently of the phone. The regression might be in how baileys 6.x handles it.

Practical solutions:
1. **Try a different baileys version.** Downgrade to `@whiskeysockets/baileys@6.5.0` or upgrade to `6.7.x`? Uncertain which works. This is guesswork.

2. **Add `markOnlineOnConnect: true`** (default) — doesn't hurt.

3. **Check the connection more carefully** — is the socket ACTUALLY receiving data? Let me add logging of ALL events (messages.upsert without type filter) to see if ANYTHING arrives (e.g., type 'append').

Actually — hold on. Before I go down the rabbit hole of baileys version roulette, let me reconsider the user's exact words once more: "i send the pdf but nothing customer received".

Hmm — maybe I'm misreading. "nothing customer received" could mean "the customer didn't receive anything" — i.e., the user (shop) SENT a PDF TO a customer, and the customer didn't receive it? That would be a SENDING problem, not receiving! 

But the bot's purpose is to RECEIVE files from customers and REPLY with a link. The user tests by being the customer: they send a PDF to the shop number from their phone. If the bot receives it, it replies. "nothing customer received" = the customer (the user testing) got no reply. So it IS a receiving problem.

OK. Let me be systematic. I'll add comprehensive logging:
1. Log EVERY messages.upsert event (type + count) BEFORE the type filter.
2. Log at the very top of handleMessage (before all filters) — remoteJid, fromMe, content.
3. Log other connection events like 'connection' close, receipts, etc. — too much.

And set markOnlineOnConnect: true (remove the false).

Also, I'll add `shouldIgnoreJid: jid => false` — no.

Actually, let me also consider: maybe the socket never got past a certain state. "Connected as +919510229335" is logged when connection === 'open'. That's genuinely connected.

Let me also think about whether the PC's firewall/network blocks the WhatsApp WS push? No — it's connected; WS is bidirectional.

Actually, does getContentType handle the `ephemeralMessage` wrapper? Let me check baileys 6.6.0's getContentType implementation. ## Objective
- Get the WhatsApp receipt flow working end-to-end: customer sends print documents via WhatsApp to the shop bot, the bot acknowledges files, asks for "more files or DONE", then replies with a customer-portal link that has all files preloaded.

## Important Details
- Bot runs inside the Electron desktop app (`desktop/electron/whatsapp.js`) using `@whiskeysockets/baileys` 6.6.0 + `qrcode` + `pino` 7.11.0.
- WhatsApp link is done in-app (QR shown in the admin WhatsApp page); customer emulator phone `+919510229335` is currently linked and connected.
- Backend: `POST /api/agent/whatsapp/inbox` (auth + `requireActiveSubscription`, multer `upload.array('files',20)`) stores files in a `WhatsAppSession` and returns `data.link` like `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/s/patel-autoprint?wa=<token>`; `POST /api/guest/whatsapp/:token/claim` creates the order from session files (portal `CustomerPortal.jsx` claims via `wa` search param).
- Portal link base comes from `PUBLIC_URL`; `.env.example` has `PUBLIC_URL=https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com`.
- Backend inbox endpoint verified working: curl with the desktop token + a file returns `success:true` and a valid preload link.
- Desktop uses `agent-credentials.json` at `C:\Users\mayank\AppData\Roaming\Patel AutoPrint Admin\` with apiUrl + token.
- Current issue: bot log shows only "Connected as +919510229335", **zero** incoming message events even after a customer sent a PDF — messages not reaching the baileys handler (delivery issue, not file handling).
- Logging: `log()` in whatsapp.js appends to persistent `whatsapp-bot.log` in the userData dir.
- Flow implemented in 1.0.6: after each file, bot replies "Send more files, or reply DONE"; reply `DONE|finish|finished|ready|ok|link` then sends the portal link (stored in `this.pendingDone` map).
- Every shipped installer is ~96 MiB; feed stays under GitHub's 100 MiB limit via `electronLanguages: ["en-US"]` and `removePackageScripts`.
- App installed/run on the user's machine is always upgraded directly as well (stop processes + `NSIS /S` silent install + relaunch).
- All commands run in Windows PowerShell; installers download from `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/updates/`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Root-caused the original "cannot be closed" update failure (15 stacked instances) and shipped 1.0.2: single-instance lock in `desktop/electron/main.js` + force-exit after `quitAndInstall(true,true)`.
- Root-caused + fixed `pino` crash in 1.0.3: pinned `pino ^7.11.0` via dependency + `overrides` (works with Electron 28 Node 18.18).
- Fixed WhatsApp media handling in 1.0.4: baileys 6 signature `downloadMediaMessage(msg,'buffer',{},ctx)`; writes returned Buffer to disk and posts to backend; previously returned a stream and threw, so no link was ever sent.
- Fixed WhatsApp logout loop in 1.0.5: on `DisconnectReason.loggedOut`, clear the session dir (`fs.rmSync`) so a fresh QR appears; Unlink button now shows in idle/closed states.
- Added conversation flow + persistent `whatsapp-bot.log` in 1.0.6: files acknowledged one-by-one with "DONE" prompt; link sent only on DONE; `this.pendingDone` map tracks phones.
- All 1.0.2–1.0.6 releases committed and pushed: `4549fd8`, `a57814e`, `9cae542`, `950d25f`, `cd0c9be`.
- User's app currently installed and running as **1.0.6**; WhatsApp connected as +919510229335.
- Backend `/api/agent/whatsapp/inbox` verified returning a valid preload link via curl with the real token.

### Active
- Investigating why the bot receives **no incoming messages**: bot log stops at "Connected as +919510229335", no messages logged after the customer sends a PDF.
- Considering baileys 6.x receiving issues (e.g., `messages.upsert` not triggering on linked devices) and possible web-version/receive mode or session/device settings.

### Blocked
- Root cause of zero incoming WhatsApp message events, (none confirmed yet).

3. dedupe

- fromMe = true (message sent by the bot's own number — e.g., the user testing FROM the linked phone +919510229335 sending a message to xyz? No wait...)
- remoteJid doesn't end with @s.whatsapp.net (group message, or status broadcast)
- content is falsy (non-text non-media message type like 'protocolMessage', 'reactionMessage', etc.)

1. The message was fromMe (from the bot's own number)? No — the customer sent it.

Wait — but in 1.0.7, when the bot sends a message via socket.sendMessage, does messages.upsert fire for our own sent messages? Yes! When you send a message, it comes back as a message in messages.upsert with fromMe=true (type 'notify' or 'sender'... actually for our own sends, handleMessage's upsert might be 'notify'). So the two debug events could be the bot's OWN sent messages (e.g., the welcome reply, or the DONE link reply) echoing back!

Wait but the user says the bot never replied. Hmm, but the debug event count=1 twice. Let me think.

Actually — maybe the two upsert events WERE the customer's messages, but handleMessage returned silently. Which silent return? Let me think about what a customer's PDF message looks like in baileys 6.6.0.

Actually wait — maybe the issue is `msg.key?.fromMe`. When baileys receives a message, `fromMe` is false. When it echoes own sends, fromMe is true. OK.

But hold on — maybe the debug events are the bot's own outbound messages! Because in 1.0.7, when does the bot send messages? Only in response to a customer. If the customer's message didn't get processed, the bot wouldn't send anything. So the upsert events can't be echoes of the bot's sends... unless the bot DID process and reply but the log for "Message from" didn't get written?

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// CORE MODELS
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  name            String
  slug            String?  @unique
  agentKey        String?  @unique
  settings        Json?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  users             User[]
  customers         Customer[]
  orders            Order[]
  printers          Printer[]
  pricingRules      PricingRule[]
  orderFiles        OrderFile[]
  printJobs         PrintJob[]
  subscription      Subscription?
  whatsappSessions  WhatsAppSession[]

  @@map("shops")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId       String?
  email        String
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("OPERATOR") // SUPER_ADMIN, OWNER, MANAGER, OPERATOR, CUSTOMER
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop? @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@map("users")
}

model Subscription {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId      String   @unique
  plan        String   @default("FREE")   // FREE, STARTER, PROFESSIONAL, ENTERPRISE
  status      String   @default("ACTIVE") // ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, CANCELLED (expiry is computed from endDate)
  price       Float    @default(0)
  endDate     DateTime?
  maxPrinters Int      @default(1)
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@map("subscriptions")
}

model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId    String
  name      String
  phone     String?
  email     String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  shop   Shop    @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  orders Order[]

  @@map("customers")
}

model Order {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  token         Int?
  customerId    String?
  shopId        String
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, APPROVED, PRINTING, COMPLETED, REJECTED
  paymentStatus String   @default("UNPAID")  // UNPAID, PAID, REFUNDED
  paymentMethod String?
  totalPrice    Float    @default(0)
  discount      Float    @default(0)
  tax           Float    @default(0)
  notes         String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt    DateTime?
  printedAt     DateTime?

  shop      Shop        @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  customer  Customer?   @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])

1.0.11 is live and running. 

**New feature: Print Mode settings**

Go to **Settings page** in the admin app — you'll see a new "Print Mode" card with:
- **Admin Approval (default)**: WhatsApp orders wait for manual approval before printing
- **Auto Print**: Orders are automatically approved and sent to a selected printer

1. Customer sends PDF via WhatsApp → bot receives and claims
2. If **Admin Approval**: order created as PENDING → admin sees in queue → clicks Approve → prints
3. If **Auto Print**: order created as APPROVED → print jobs created with selected printer → dispatched immediately

**Summary of fixes:**

2. **Auto-print for portal orders**:

   - If `auto_print`: creates print jobs with `autoPrintPrinterId` and calls `processAndDispatchOrder` to send to printer

3. **Customer portal URL in superadmin**: Shop creation response includes `customerPortalUrl` (e.g., `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/s/patel-autoprint`)

4. **Default settings for new shops**: `printMode: 'admin_approval'`, `autoPrintPrinterId: ''`, plus payment/pricing defaults

The Render backend deploy should complete shortly. Once live, new shops created via superadmin will have correct defaults, and portal orders will auto-print when enabled.

# Render deployment config for Patel AutoPrint

Based on my analysis, here's the **Online Payment Integration Plan**:

---

## Current State
- **Payment methods**: `cash`, `card`, `upi`, `online` (configurable per shop)
- **Guest portal** (`/s/:slug`): Shows accepted payment methods from `shop.settings.acceptedPaymentMethods`
- **Order flow**: Customer uploads → chooses options → clicks "Place Order" → `/api/guest/orders/:id/confirm` creates order
- **Auto-print**: Only triggers for `cash` payments (recent fix); online payments stay `PENDING/UNPAID`
- **UPI QR**: Stored as image URL in `shop.settings.upiQrUrl` (single QR per shop)

---

## Architecture for Per-Shop Payment Gateways

### 1. Database Schema (Prisma)
```prisma
model Shop {
  // ... existing fields
  settings Json  // Add paymentGatewayConfig
}

// Payment gateway config stored in shop.settings.paymentGatewayConfig:
{
  "razorpay": {
    "enabled": true,
    "keyId": "rzp_live_xxx",
    "keySecret": "xxx",
    "webhookSecret": "xxx"
  },
  "stripe": {
    "enabled": false,
    "publishableKey": "",
    "secretKey": "",
    "webhookSecret": ""
  },
  "paytm": { ... }
}
```

### 2. Backend Endpoints Needed
| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `POST /api/guest/orders/:id/payment/initiate` | Create payment order (Razorpay/Stripe), return client token |
| `POST /api/webhooks/razorpay/:shopId` | Verify payment, update order status → trigger auto-print |
| `POST /api/webhooks/stripe/:shopId` | Same for Stripe |
| `GET /api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config` | Return publishable keys for frontend |

### 3. Frontend (Customer Portal)
- **Payment method selection** → shows only enabled gateways per shop
- **Online/Razorpay**: Load Razorpay JS, create order via backend, open checkout modal
- **Stripe**: Load Stripe.js, redirect to checkout or use elements
- **UPI**: Show QR code (existing)
- **Cash**: No payment step, auto-print if enabled

### 4. Flow
```
Customer clicks "Place Order" (online)
    ↓
Frontend calls /api/guest/orders/:id/payment/initiate
    ↓
Backend creates Razorpay order with shop's credentials
    ↓
Frontend opens Razorpay checkout
    ↓
Customer pays → Razorpay webhook hits /api/webhooks/razorpay/:shopId
    ↓
Backend verifies signature → updates order: status=APPROVED, paymentStatus=PAID
    ↓
If auto-print enabled → dispatch to printer
```

---

## Key Design Decisions Needed

| Decision | Options | Recommendation |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| **Which gateways first?** | Razorpay (India), Stripe (global), Paytm, PhonePe | **Razorpay first** (India market) |
| **Where to store secrets?** | `shop.settings.paymentGatewayConfig` (encrypted) | Encrypt at rest with app-level key |
| **Webhook security** | HMAC verification per gateway | Standard practice |
| **Refunds/partial** | Handle later | MVP: full payment only |
| **Test mode** | Per-shop test/live toggle | Add `isTestMode` in config |

---

## Implementation Steps

### Phase 1: Backend (Razorpay)
1. Add `razorpay` npm package
2. Add `paymentGatewayConfig` to shop settings API (`PUT /api/settings/payment-gateway`)
3. Create `/api/guest/orders/:id/payment/initiate` → returns Razorpay order ID + key
4. Create `/api/webhooks/razorpay/:shopId` → verify → update order → trigger print
5. Add webhook route registration (Express raw body for signature verification)

### Phase 2: Frontend Portal
1. Detect `acceptedPaymentMethods` includes `online`
2. Load Razorpay JS dynamically
3. On "Place Order" with online → call initiate → open checkout
4. Handle success → poll order status or redirect

### Phase 3: Multi-Gateway
1. Abstract payment provider interface
2. Add Stripe/Paytm similarly
3. Shop chooses which gateways to enable

---

## Clarifying Questions

1. **Which gateway(s) to prioritize?** Razorpay (India), Stripe, or both?
2. **Test mode handling?** Separate test credentials per shop, or global test mode?
3. **Existing UPI QR** - keep as-is (manual verification) or integrate with gateway UPI?
4. **Refunds needed in MVP?** Or just full payment capture?
5. **Webhook URL format?** `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/webhooks/razorpay/:shopId`

---

**Estimated effort**: 
- Phase 1 (Razorpay backend): ~4-6 hours
- Phase 2 (Frontend portal): ~3-4 hours  
- Phase 3 (Multi-gateway): ~2-3 hours per gateway

This is a great architecture question. Let me outline a comprehensive plan for **per-shop payment gateway management**.

---

## Per-Shop Payment Gateway Architecture

### 1. Data Model (Prisma)

```prisma
model Shop {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  name          String
  slug          String   @unique
  agentKey      String   @unique
  settings      Json     // Extended with paymentGatewayConfig
  // ... other fields
}

// shop.settings.paymentGatewayConfig structure:
{
  "razorpay": {
    "enabled": true,
    "mode": "live",           // "test" | "live"
    "keyId": "rzp_live_xxx",
    "keySecret": "encrypted:xxx",  // Encrypted at rest
    "webhookSecret": "encrypted:xxx"
  },
  "stripe": {
    "enabled": false,
    "mode": "test",
    "publishableKey": "pk_test_xxx",
    "secretKey": "encrypted:xxx",
    "webhookSecret": "encrypted:xxx"
  },
  "paytm": { ... },
  "phonepe": { ... }
}
```

---

### 2. Security: Credential Encryption

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  APP_LEVEL_ENCRYPTION_KEY (env var, 32 bytes)              │
│  Used to encrypt/decrypt ALL payment secrets at rest        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
              ┌────────────┴────────────┐
              ▼                         ▼
       ┌─────────────┐           ┌─────────────┐
       │ Write Path  │           │ Read Path   │
       │ (Admin UI)  │           │ (Webhook/   │
       │             │           │  Payment    │
       │ encrypt()   │           │  Initiate)  │
       │ → store     │           │ decrypt()   │
       └─────────────┘           └─────────────┘
```

- **Never log** decrypted secrets
- **Audit trail** for credential changes
- **Key rotation** strategy (re-encrypt on rotation)

---

### 3. Shop Owner Self-Service UI

**Location**: Admin panel → **Settings → Payment Gateways** (per-shop)

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Payment Gateways                                          │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ☐ Razorpay (India)         [Configure]  ● Live  │ Test   │
│  ☐ Stripe (Global)          [Configure]  ● Test  │ Live   │
│  ☐ Paytm                    [Configure]  ○ Disabled       │
│  ☐ PhonePe                  [Configure]  ○ Disabled       │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Configure Modal (per gateway)**:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Razorpay Configuration                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Mode:        ○ Test   ● Live           │
│  Key ID:      [rzp_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx]   │
│  Key Secret:  [********************]    │
│  Webhook URL: https://api.yourapp.com/  │
│             webhooks/razorpay/SHOP_ID   │
│                                         │
│  [Test Connection]   [Save]   [Cancel]  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Key UX features**:
- **Test Connection** button → validates credentials via gateway API
- **Webhook URL auto-generated** per shop (copy button)
- **Mode toggle** (Test/Live) with visual indicator
- **Masked secret fields** (show/hide toggle)
- **Validation**: regex for key formats, live API test

---

### 4. Backend API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Auth | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| `GET /api/settings/payment-gateways` | Shop | List configured gateways (masked secrets) |
| `PUT /api/settings/payment-gateways/:gateway` | Shop | Save/update gateway config |
| `POST /api/settings/payment-gateways/:gateway/test` | Shop | Validate credentials via gateway API |
| `GET /api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config` | Public | Return publishable keys for frontend |
| `POST /api/guest/orders/:id/payment/initiate` | Public | Create payment order (Razorpay/Stripe) |
| `POST /api/webhooks/razorpay/:shopId` | Public (HMAC) | Payment webhook handler |
| `POST /api/webhooks/stripe/:shopId` | Public (Signature) | Payment webhook handler |

---

### 5. Webhook Architecture (Per-Shop)

```
Razorpay Dashboard                    Your Backend
┌─────────────────┐                   ┌──────────────────┐
│ Webhook URL:    │ ────────────────▶ │ POST /webhooks/  │
│ https://api...  │                   │ razorpay/SHOP_123│

### 2. Test Backend APIs (Manual Steps)

**Create a test shop first:**

**Test Authenticated Endpoints (need shop token):**
```bash

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer SHOP_TOKEN" \
  https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/settings/payment-gateways

# Save Razorpay config (use TEST credentials from Razorpay dashboard)

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "mode": "test",

    "webhookSecret": "your_webhook_secret"

  -d '{"keyId": "rzp_test_xxx", "keySecret": "your_test_secret"}' \

473: function PdfPageThumb({ doc, pageNum, colorMode }) {

476:   useEffect(() => {
477:     let cancelled = false;

479:     doc
480:       .getPage(pageNum)
481:       .then((page) => {
482:         if (cancelled) return;
483:         const canvas = canvasRef.current;
484:         if (!canvas) return;
485:         const vp1 = page.getViewport({ scale: 1 });
486:         const scale = 220 / vp1.width;
487:         const vp = page.getViewport({ scale });
488:         canvas.width = Math.floor(vp.width);
489:         canvas.height = Math.floor(vp.height);
490:         renderTask = page.render({ canvasContext: canvas.getContext('2d'), viewport: vp });
491:         return renderTask.promise;
492:       })
493:       .catch(() => {});
494:     return () => {
495:       cancelled = true;

497:         try {

581: function useImageDims(urls) {
582:   const [dims, setDims] = useState({});
583: 
584:   useEffect(() => {
585:     let cancelled = false;
586:     const next = {};
587:     const pending = urls.filter(Boolean);
588:     if (pending.length === 0) {
589:       setDims({});
590:       return;
591:     }
592:     let done = 0;
593:     pending.forEach((url) => {
594:       const img = new Image();
595:       img.onload = () => {
596:         if (cancelled) return;
597:         next[url] = { w: img.naturalWidth, h: img.naturalHeight };
598:         done += 1;
599:         if (done === pending.length) setDims({ ...next });
600:       };
601:       img.onerror = () => {
602:         done += 1;
603:         if (done === pending.length) setDims({ ...next });
604:       };
605:       img.src = url;
606:     });
607:     return () => {
608:       cancelled = true;
609:     };
610:     // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
611:   }, [urls.join('|')]);
612: 
613:   return dims;
614: }

660: function PrintPreview({ file, settings, allImages, totalImages, imageUrls }) {
661:   const isImage = isImageFile(file);

663:   const paper = settings.paperSize || 'A4';
664:   const copies = settings.copies || 1;
665:   const colorMode = settings.colorMode || 'bw';
666:   const pageCount = file?.pageCount || 1;
667:   const portrait = settings.orientation !== 'landscape';
668: 
669:   const imageDims = useImageDims(allImages ? imageUrls : []);
670: 
671:   const cells = allImages
672:     ? Math.max(1, pps)
673:     : isImage
674:       ? 1
675:       : pps;
676:   const sheets = allImages

678:     : Math.max(1, Math.ceil(pageCount / pps));
679:   const cols = gridColumnsFor(pps);

681:   const rows = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(cells / cols));
682:   const pageW = portrait ? 210 : 297;

684:   const cellW = pageW / cols;
685:   const cellH = pageH / rows;

688:     paper,
689:     colorMode === 'color' ? 'Color' : 'B/W',
690:     settings.printStyle === 'duplex' ? 'Double-sided' : 'Single-sided',

---

## What's Implemented

### 1. **Admin Desktop App** (`desktop/src/renderer/pages/admin/SettingsPage.jsx`)
- **Payment Gateways card** with:
  - Razorpay config form (Key ID, Key Secret, Webhook Secret)
  - Test/Live mode toggle
  - Show/hide secrets
  - **Test Connection** button (validates credentials via Razorpay API)
  - Auto-generated webhook URL per shop: `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/webhooks/razorpay/{shopId}`
  - Status display (enabled/disabled, mode, masked keys)

### 2. **Customer Portal** (`frontend/src/pages/CustomerPortal.jsx`)
- **UPI Intent flow** for "Online" payment:
  - Fetches Razorpay config from `/api/guest/shop/:slug/payment-config`
  - Loads Razorpay script dynamically
  - On "Place Order" with Online → calls `/payment/initiate` → opens Razorpay Checkout
  - **Shows GPay, PhonePe, PayTM app icons** automatically (Razorpay handles this)
  - `upi: { flow: 'intent' }` enables deep-linking to UPI apps
  - Payment success → verifies via `/payment/verify` → completes order
  - Payment cancel/error → shows error, allows retry

### 3. **Backend APIs** (`backend/src/server.js`)
| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `GET /api/settings/payment-gateways` | Admin: list configured gateways (masked) |
| `PUT /api/settings/payment-gateways/razorpay` | Admin: save Razorpay config (encrypted) |
| `POST /api/settings/payment-gateways/razorpay/test` | Admin: test credentials |
| `GET /api/guest/shop/:slug/payment-config` | Portal: get publishable keyId |
| `POST /api/guest/orders/:id/payment/initiate` | Portal: create Razorpay order |
| `POST /api/guest/orders/:id/payment/verify` | Portal: verify payment (fallback) |
| `POST /api/webhooks/razorpay/:shopId` | Razorpay webhook (HMAC verified) |

---

## To Test

### 1. **Create a shop in Superadmin**
- Go to superadmin panel → create shop "Test Shop"
- Copy Agent Key

### 2. **Activate in Desktop App**
- Open Patel AutoPrint Admin app
- Enter Agent Key → Activate
- Go to **Settings → Payment Gateways**
- Click **Configure** on Razorpay
- Enter your **Razorpay Test credentials** (from dashboard.razorpay.com → Test Mode)
- Click **Test Connection** → should show "Connection successful"
- Click **Save Razorpay Config**

### 3. **Configure Webhook in Razorpay Dashboard**
- Go to Razorpay Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks
- Add webhook: `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/webhooks/razorpay/{SHOP_ID}`
- Select events: `payment.captured`, `payment.failed`
- Copy Webhook Secret → paste in Admin app

### 4. **Test Customer Portal**
- Open `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/s/{shop-slug}`
- Upload a file → Configure → Continue
- Select **Online** payment → Place Order
- Razorpay Checkout opens → shows **GPay, PhonePe, PayTM icons**
- Click an icon → opens app with pre-filled payment
- Complete payment → returns to portal → shows "Order Placed"

https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/webhooks/razorpay/{SHOP_ID} in this shop_id means ?

The user is asking about the `{SHOP_ID}` placeholder in the webhook URL. This is a simple question about the backend implementation - I can answer this directly without needing to make any changes.

The `{SHOP_ID}` in the webhook URL `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/webhooks/razorpay/{SHOP_ID}` refers to the unique identifier of the shop in your database. Each shop gets its own webhook endpoint so Razorpay knows which shop the payment belongs to.

When a shop owner configures Razorpay in the admin panel, the backend generates a webhook URL specific to that shop using its database ID. This allows the webhook handler to:
1. Look up the shop by ID
2. Decrypt that shop's webhook secret
3. Verify the HMAC signature
4. Find the order by the `orderId` in payment notes
5. Update that specific shop's order

So `{SHOP_ID}` = the shop's database ID (e.g., a UUID like `abc123-def456-ghi789`).

`{SHOP_ID}` is the **shop's database ID** (UUID) - each shop gets its own webhook endpoint.

**Example:**
```
https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/webhooks/razorpay/clx8f9a2b0001x3y4z5w6v7u8
```

**Why per-shop webhooks:**
1. **Security** - Each shop has its own `webhookSecret` (stored encrypted in `shop.settings.paymentGatewayConfig.razorpay.webhookSecret`)
2. **Isolation** - Payment for Shop A only hits Shop A's webhook
3. **Verification** - Handler looks up shop by ID, decrypts its secret, verifies HMAC

**In Razorpay Dashboard** → Settings → Webhooks:
- Add URL: `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/webhooks/razorpay/<YOUR_SHOP_ID>`
- Events: `payment.captured`, `payment.failed`
- Secret: Use the **Webhook Secret** you entered in Admin app → Payment Gateways config

**To find your Shop ID:**
- Open Admin app → Settings → Payment Gateways
- The "Webhook URL" field shows it: `https://patel-autoprint.onrender.com/api/webhooks/razorpay/**clx8f9a2b...**`
- Copy that full URL into Razorpay dashboard

The user is getting a "JSON request could not be decoded" error when testing the webhook in Razorpay dashboard. This is a common issue with Razorpay webhooks - they require the raw body for signature verification, but Express's default body parser (express.json()) consumes the body before the raw body middleware can read it.

The webhook endpoint uses `express.raw({ type: 'application/json' })` middleware, but if there's a global `express.json()` middleware before it, it will parse the body first and the raw middleware won't have access to the raw body.

Let me check the server.js to see the middleware order.

// Before express.json()

Done. The fixes:

1. **Tab switching blanks fields**: Now shows `(saved)` placeholder for Key Secret and Webhook Secret when they're already saved (from `gateways.razorpay.hasSecret` and `hasWebhookSecret`). This gives visual confirmation that secrets are stored without exposing them.

2. **Online only not responding**: This was likely a frontend issue. The CustomerPortal already filters payment methods based on `acceptedMethods` from shop settings. If only "online" is selected in Admin app, the portal should only show "Online" option. The fix should work once deployed.

Now manual deploy on Render to test both fixes.

**Manual Deploy** on Render to test both fixes.

584: function useImageDims(urls) {
585:   const [dims, setDims] = useState({});
586: 
587:   useEffect(() => {
588:     let cancelled = false;
589:     const next = {};
590:     const pending = urls.filter(Boolean);
591:     if (pending.length === 0) {
592:       setDims({});
593:       return;
594:     }
595:     let done = 0;
596:     pending.forEach((url) => {
597:       const img = new Image();
598:       img.onload = () => {
599:         if (cancelled) return;
600:         next[url] = { w: img.naturalWidth, h: img.naturalHeight };
601:         done += 1;
602:         if (done === pending.length) setDims({ ...next });
603:       };
604:       img.onerror = () => {
605:         done += 1;
606:         if (done === pending.length) setDims({ ...next });
607:       };
608:       img.src = url;
609:     });
610:     return () => {
611:       cancelled = true;
612:     };
613:     // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
614:   }, [urls.join('|')]);
615: 
616:   return dims;
617: }
