Git ignore rules: A negation `!pattern` can't re-include a file if a parent directory is excluded. Here, `dist/` excludes the directory `backend/frontend/dist`. The pattern `frontend/dist/` matches `backend/frontend/dist/` at the `frontend` level. Actually gitignore: "It is not possible to re-include a file if a parent directory of that file is excluded." <Chip icon={<InfoIcon />} label="PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, JPG, PNG, WebP" variant="outlined" size="small" />
      </Box>
      <Typography variant="body2" color="text.secondary" sx={{ mb: 2 }}>
        Each file has its own copies, colour, orientation, sides, paper & pages.
      </Typography>

      <Paper
        onDrop={handleDrop}
        onDragOver={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setDragActive(true); }}
        onDragLeave={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setDragActive(false); }}
        onClick={() => uploadInputRef.current?.click()}
        sx={{
          p: { xs: 3, sm: 5 },
          textAlign: 'center',
          border: dragActive ? '2px solid' : '2px dashed',
          borderColor: dragActive ? 'primary.main' : 'divider',
          cursor: 'pointer',
          mb: 2,
          bgcolor: dragActive ? 'action.hover' : 'background.paper',
          transition: 'all 0.3s ease',
          transform: dragActive ? 'scale(1.02)' : 'scale(1)',
          boxShadow: dragActive ? 4 : 1,
          '&:hover': { borderColor: 'primary.main', bgcolor: 'action.hover' },
        }}
      >
        <input
          ref={uploadInputRef}
          id="file-input"
          type="file"
          multiple
          hidden
          onChange={handleFileInput}
          accept=".pdf,.docx,.pptx,.xlsx,.jpg,.jpeg,.png,.webp"
        />

        <Box sx={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', alignItems: 'center', gap: 1.5 }}>
          <Box
            sx={{
              display: 'flex',
              alignItems: 'center',
              justifyContent: 'center',
              width: { xs: 76, sm: 92 },
              height: { xs: 76, sm: 92 },
              borderRadius: '50%',
              bgcolor: dragActive ? 'primary.light' : 'action.hover',
              transition: 'all 0.3s ease',
              position: 'relative',
              animation: `${pulseGlow} 2.5s ease-in-out infinite`,
            }}
          >
            <CloudUpload sx={{ fontSize: { xs: 36, sm: 48 }, color: dragActive ? 'primary.main' : 'text.secondary' }} />
            {dragActive && (
              <Box
                sx={{
                  position: 'absolute',
                  inset: -8,
                  borderRadius: '50%',
                  border: '2px solid',
                  borderColor: 'primary.main',
                  animation: `${pulseRing} 1.5s ease-out infinite`,
                }}
              />
            )}
          </Box>
          <Typography variant="subtitle1" fontWeight={600}>
            {dragActive ? 'Drop files here' : 'Tap to select files'}
          </Typography>
          <Typography variant="body2" color="text.secondary">
            or drag & drop · Max 25 MB each · Held only until print finishes, then deleted
          </Typography>
        </Box>
      </Paper>

      {files.length > 0 && (
        <Box sx={{ mb: 2 }}>
          <Typography variant="subtitle2" fontWeight={700} gutterBottom sx={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 1 }}>
            <DocIcon fontSize="small" color="primary" />
            Selected Files ({files.length})
          </Typography>
          <Grid container spacing={1}>
            {files.map((file, index) => (
              <Grid item xs={12} sm={6} md={4} key={index}>
                <Paper
                  elevation={1}
                  sx={{
                    p: 1.5,
                    display: 'flex',
                    flexDirection: 'column',
                    gap: 1,
                    borderRadius: 2,
                    '&:hover': { transform: 'translateY(-2px)', boxShadow: 3, transition: 'all 0.2s' },
                  }}
                >
                  <Box sx={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between', alignItems: 'flex-start' }}>
                    <Typography variant="body2" fontWeight={500} sx={{ flex: 1, mr: 1, overflow: 'hidden', textOverflow: 'ellipsis' }}>
                      {file.name}
                    </Typography>
                    <IconButton size="small" color="error" onClick={() => removeFile(index)} sx={{ opacity: 0.7, '&:hover': { opacity: 1 } }}>
                      <Delete fontSize="small" />
                    </IconButton>
                  </Box>
                  <Box sx={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
                    <Typography variant="caption" color="text.secondary">
                      {(file.size / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(2)} MB
                    </Typography>
                    <Chip
                      size="small"
                      label={isImageFile(file) ? 'Image' : file.name.split('.').pop()?.toUpperCase()}
                      color={isImageFile(file) ? 'success' : 'default'}
                      variant="filled"
                      sx={{ fontSize: '0.7rem' }}
                    />
                  </Box>
                </Paper>
              </Grid>
            ))}
          </Grid>
        </Box>
      )}

      <Divider sx={{ my: 2 }} />

      <Typography variant="subtitle1" fontWeight={700} gutterBottom sx={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 1 }}>
        <AccountCircleIcon fontSize="small" color="primary" />
        Your Name & Phone
      </Typography>
      <Grid container spacing={1.5}>
        <Grid item xs={12} sm={6}>
          <TextField
            fullWidth
            size="small"
            label="Your Name"
            value={customerInfo.name}
            onChange={(e) => setCustomerInfo({ ...customerInfo, name: e.target.value })}
            required
            InputProps={{ startAdornment: <InputAdornment position="start"><AccountCircleIcon fontSize="small" sx={{ color: 'text.secondary' }} /></InputAdornment> }}
            placeholder="e.g., John Doe"
          />
        </Grid>
        <Grid item xs={12} sm={6}>
          <TextField
            fullWidth
            size="small"
            label="Phone Number"
            value={customerInfo.phone}
            onChange={(e) => setCustomerInfo({ ...customerInfo, phone: e.target.value })}
            required
            InputProps={{ startAdornment: <InputAdornment position="start"><PhoneIcon fontSize="small" sx={{ color: 'text.secondary' }} /></InputAdornment> }}
            placeholder="e.g., +1234567890"
          />
        </Grid>
        <Grid item xs={12}>
          <TextField
            fullWidth
            size="small"
            label="Email (optional)"
            value={customerInfo.email}
            onChange={(e) => setCustomerInfo({ ...customerInfo, email: e.target.value })}
            InputProps={{ startAdornment: <InputAdornment position="start"><EmailIcon fontSize="small" sx={{ color: 'text.secondary' }} /></InputAdornment> }}
            placeholder="your@email.com"
          />
        </Grid>
      </Grid>
    </Box>
  );
};

function fileUrl(file) {
  if (!file?.storagePath) return null;
  return `/uploads/${file.storagePath.split(/[\\/]/).pop()}`;
}

function gridColumnsFor(pps) {
  if (pps >= 16) return 4;
  if (pps >= 9) return 3;
  if (pps >= 4) return 2;
  return 1;
}

But building the EXE requires Windows + electron-builder. This machine is Windows. But the build takes a while (electron download etc). And the user needs the update to reach their installed app. Also, the autoUpdater needs to be wired (electron-updater is in deps; main.js has autoUpdater code).

export default function CustomerPortal() {
  const { slug: shopSlug } = useParams() || {};
  const [searchParams, setSearchParams] = useSearchParams();
  const { mode, toggleMode } = useThemeMode();
  const [activeStep, setActiveStep] = useState(0);
  const [files, setFiles] = useState([]);
  const [customerInfo, setCustomerInfo] = useState({ name: '', phone: '', email: '' });
  const [fileSettings, setFileSettings] = useState({});
  const [uploadedOrder, setUploadedOrder] = useState(null);
  const [paymentMethod, setPaymentMethod] = useState('cash');
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [priceData, setPriceData] = useState(null);
  const [loadingPrice, setLoadingPrice] = useState(false);
  const [upiQrUrl, setUpiQrUrl] = useState('');
  const [shop, setShop] = useState(null);
  const [shopError, setShopError] = useState('');
  const [waSource, setWaSource] = useState(false);
  const [waError, setWaError] = useState('');
  
  // Razorpay payment state
  const [razorpayConfig, setRazorpayConfig] = useState(null);
  const [processingPayment, setProcessingPayment] = useState(false);
  const [paymentError, setPaymentError] = useState('');
  
  const waToken = searchParams.get('wa');
  const waClaimedRef = useRef(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!waToken || waClaimedRef.current) return;
    waClaimedRef.current = true;
    let cancelled = false;
    setLoading(true);
    api.post(`/guest/whatsapp/${waToken}/claim`)
      .then((result) => {
        if (cancelled || !result.success) return;
        setUploadedOrder(result.data.order);
        setCustomerInfo((prev) => ({
          ...prev,
          phone: result.data.customerPhone || '',
          name: result.data.customerName || '',
        }));
        setWaSource(true);
        setActiveStep(1);
        toast.success('WhatsApp files received!');
      })
      .catch((err) => {
        if (!cancelled) setWaError(err?.message || 'This WhatsApp link is invalid or already used.');
      })
      .finally(() => {
        if (!cancelled) setLoading(false);
        setSearchParams({}, { replace: true });
      });
    return () => { cancelled = true; };
  }, [waToken]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!shopSlug) return;
    let cancelled = false;
    api.get(`/guest/shop/${shopSlug}`)
      .then((result) => {
        if (!cancelled && result.success) setShop(result.data);
      })
      .catch((err) => {
        if (!cancelled) setShopError(err?.message || 'Shop not found');
      });
    return () => { cancelled = true; };
  }, [shopSlug]);

  const handleUpload = async () => {
    if (files.length === 0) { toast.error('Please select files'); return; }
    setLoading(true);
    try {
      const formData = new FormData();
      files.forEach((f) => formData.append('files', f));
      formData.append('customerName', customerInfo.name);
      formData.append('customerPhone', customerInfo.phone);
      formData.append('customerEmail', customerInfo.email);
      if (shop?.id) formData.append('shopId', shop.id);
      else if (shopSlug) formData.append('shopRef', shopSlug);

      const result = await api.post('/guest/upload', formData);
      if (result.success) {
        setUploadedOrder(result.data);
        toast.success(`${result.data.files?.length || 0} file(s) analyzed!`);
        setActiveStep(1);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Upload failed');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const handleSaveSettings = async () => {
    if (!uploadedOrder) return;
    setLoading(true);
    try {
      for (const [fileIndex, settings] of Object.entries(fileSettings)) {
        const fileId = uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.id;
        if (fileId) {
          await api.put(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/settings`, {
            fileId,
            settings: { ...uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.settings, ...settings },
          });
        }
      }
      const updated = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}`);
      if (updated.success) setUploadedOrder(updated.data);
      toast.success('Settings saved!');
      setActiveStep(2);
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to save settings');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const fetchPrice = async () => {
    if (!uploadedOrder) return;
    setLoadingPrice(true);
    try {
      const result = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/price`);
      if (result.success) setPriceData(result.data);
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to get price');
    } finally {
      setLoadingPrice(false);
    }
  };

  const fetchUpiQr = async () => {
    try {
      const params = new URLSearchParams();
      if (shop?.slug) params.append('shop', shop.slug);
      else if (shopSlug) params.append('shop', shopSlug);
      const result = await api.get(`/settings/public/upi-qr?${params.toString()}`);
      if (result.success && result.data.url) setUpiQrUrl(result.data.url);
    } catch {}

parts.text:
The search confirms:
1. Razorpay **Payment Links** support `upi_link: true` (or `type: 'upi'`), and there's a "UPI PL Response". Payment links can be UPI-only.
2. UPI Intent flow: "After customers select the UPI payment app on the Checkout, the app is launched automatically" — the intent flow on mobile shows the UPI app list.

Note: The docs say "UPI Collect Flow Deprecated effective 28 February 2026" — customers can no longer pay by entering VPA/mobile (that's the "enter your mobile number" thing the user saw). So the enter-mobile-number collect flow is being deprecated — meaning the user's experience of "ask for mobile number" was the Collect flow.

Upi Intent

# UPI Intent

Accept payments from your customers via UPI app on your mobile that supports the Intent flow using Razorpay.

Copy for AI

View as Markdown

---

You can make UPI payments easier for your customers by enabling UPI Intent on your application Checkout.

### 

[

Benefits

](/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/upi-intent#benefits)

Enjoy the benefits such as higher conversion rates, decrease in abandoned carts and a decrease in time to complete the payment. Your customers are also benefited in the following ways:

-   No need to handle push or SMS notifications.
-   No need to switch between applications to complete a payment (merchant, SMS and app).
-   No need to remember their VPAs.

## 

[

Understand Intent flow

](/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/upi-intent#understand-intent-flow)

The payment flow for UPI Intent payments is given below.

![Payment Flow for UPI Intent Payments](build/browser/assets/images/payment-flow-upi_intent.jpg)

1.  In the UPI Intent flow, the customer selects UPI as the payment method on your website or app. A list of UPI apps supporting the intent flow is displayed.
    
    **Watch Out!**
    
    By default, the top PSP (Payment Service Provider) apps appear on the customer's mobile irrespective of the installation status of the UPI apps.
    
2.  The customers select their preferred app. The UPI app opens with pre-populated payment details.
    
3.  The customers enter their UPI PIN to complete their transactions.
    
4.  After the payment is successful, the customers are redirected to your app or website.
    

#### 

Supported Platforms

[](/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/upi-intent#supported-platforms)

UPI Intent is supported on **mWeb (Android and iOS)** and **Mobile App (WebView)**. On **Desktop Web**, UPI Intent is not supported, a QR code is automatically displayed instead.

## 

[

Integrate on Android, iOS and Mobile Web

](/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/upi-intent#integrate-on-android-ios-and-mobile-web)

Android

iOS

Mobile Web

Use the Android SDK to support UPI Intent payments when a payment is processed through Razorpay in a WebView inside an app.

![UPI Checkout with Intent Flow](build/browser/assets/images/pay-pm-upi-intent-android.gif)

#### 

[

Installation

](/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/upi-intent#installation)

[

Download the JAR file

](https://rzp-1415-prod-mobile.s3.amazonaws.com/android/googlepay-sdk/tez-client-api-0.9.4.aar)

and include it in the `libs` folder.

#### 

[

Initialisation

](/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/upi-intent#initialisation)

To initiate the SDK, call the Razorpay class constructor in your project and pass `key` as Razorpay API key and `webView` as the object that handles the payment flow.

JavaKotlin

copy

import com.razorpay.Razorpay

Razorpay razorpay \= new Razorpay(key, webView, activity);

#### 

[

Passing Result to Razorpay

](/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/upi-intent#passing-result-to-razorpay)

After UPI is selected as the payment method, Razorpay invokes the **Intent Flow** page that lists all the available intent flows for the user to select and make the payment. Upon payment completion, the UPI app returns the result back to your `activity` in `onActivityResult` method. This should be passed to Razorpay as shown below:

JavaKotlin

copy

@Override

protected void onActivityResult(int requestCode, int resultCode, Intent data) {

    super.onActivityResult(requestCode, resultCode, data);

    if (requestCode \== Razorpay.UPI\_INTENT\_REQUEST\_CODE) {

        razorpay.onActivityResult(requestCode, resultCode, data);

    }

}

Refer to the

[

list of supported UPI intent apps for Android SDK

](/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/supported-apps/)

.

## 

[

Best Practices

](/docs/payments/payment-methods/upi/upi-intent#best-practices)

Following are the best practices to be followed to accept online payments using UPI intent flow. You must show the list of UPI apps in 2 sections:

-   Top performing apps (GPAY > PhonePe > Paytm > BHIM)
-   Other apps

Now I have the full picture of all three issues. Let me plan the fixes.

**Issue 1 — Back goes to root after order:**
Root cause: browser history — the customer's history stack is `[root, /s/abc]` (they visited root first). After order, Back → root (HomePage). Fix: push a fresh history entry when the order is completed (activeStep → 3), so pressing Back returns to /s/abc instead of root. Implement in both `handlePlaceOrder` success and `verifyRazorpayPayment` success:

```js
window.history.pushState({}, '', window.location.href);
```

Wait, pushing the same URL creates a duplicate entry. Then Back from that → previous entry (/s/abc). Good. But if the flow started AT /s/abc (direct link), stack is [/s/abc], push → [/s/abc, /s/abc], Back → /s/abc (still shop). 

Alternatively, a cleaner approach many apps use: replace the history when the shop mounts so back leaves the site entirely. But that doesn't fix "lands on root". The pushState approach is best.

Hmm, actually wait. Let me reconsider what the user wants. "customer go back than its redirect in patel-autoprint.onrender.com" — they don't want the customer landing at the homepage after back. With pushState after order completion, Back → /s/abc (the shop). That directly solves it.

But actually — there's a subtlety with `setSearchParams({}, { replace: true })` in the WA claim: it replaces /s/abc?wa=X with /s/abc. If the customer then completes the order, pushState /s/abc → [/s/abc(replaced), /s/abc]. Back → /s/abc. Still fine.

Additionally, I should ALSO make the initial shop load replace history so the root isn't in the stack when they navigated from root... can't remove entries. The pushState fix is sufficient.

Actually, there's an even more robust option: listen for the app going to step 3 and use `history.replaceState` to replace the CURRENT entry (which is /s/abc) — that doesn't help either. The push is the right approach. Let me also consider: after they press back to /s/abc, the component remounts fresh (full page load) showing step 0 (upload). That's acceptable ("back to the shop").

Let me implement: a helper `pushShopHistory` that pushes the current location. Call it when order is placed (both cash and razorpay success paths).

**Issue 2 — Blank pages in auto-print for image uploads:**
Root cause: In the `/confirm` auto-print path (line 1325-1327), print jobs are created per-file via `createPrintJobsForFile` WITHOUT grouping image files into contact sheets. So image files create a print job whose `pages` are numeric indices; `processAndDispatchOrder` → `processFile` returns the ORIGINAL image file → agent downloads it as `.pdf` → prints blank.

Fix: In the auto-print dispatch (confirm path), group image files via `createContactSheetPrintJob` like the other flows do (lines 1562-1566, 1619-1623). Also check the WhatsApp claim auto-print path (line ~1977) and apply the same fix.

Let me look at lines 1550-1640 and 1960-2000 to see how they're structured and replicate.

**Issue 3 — Online payment UX:**
Strengthen the Razorpay checkout:
- Add `prefill: { name, contact }` from customerInfo to skip the mobile-number prompt.
- Add `upi.intents` to explicitly show GPay/PhonePe/Paytm/BHIM as the app buttons (with flow intent).
- Keep `method: { upi: {} }` + hide.
- Add `intent_flow_timeout`.
- Pass customer contact to the initiate endpoint so the order notes carry it (optional; not needed).
- Also handle desktop: intent not supported on desktop — Razorpay shows QR automatically. Fine.

Also I realize the `paymentMethod === 'online'` requires `razorpayConfig`. Good.

Also `handleRazorpayPayment(uploadedOrder.id)` is called with just orderId; it gets keyId etc from the response. I'll add prefill using `customerInfo` state (available in component scope) — but customerInfo's phone/name are what the customer entered. If empty, skip.

Let me also double check: does the current checkout's `hide` include `emi`? Cards hidden anyway. Add `emi: true` too for safety.

Also — I should verify the `intents` option format. Let me search the web quickly for the exact format to avoid a broken option.

## What is UPI intent?

The UPI intent flow is a checkout experience that allows users to make payments from any UPI PSP app.

By enabling the UPI Intent as the payment method, businesses can simplify the [UPI payments](https://razorpay.com/upi/) process for their customers.
_Understanding The UPI Intent Flow_ :

Step 1: A customer selects UPI as the [payment mode](https://razorpay.com/blog/different-types-of-payment-methods/) in any app or website

Step 2: The list of UPI apps (that supports intent flow) installed on their phone pops up

Step 3: Customers select their favourite app

Step 4: The application opens with filled payment details

Step 5: Customer enters the [UPI PIN](https://razorpay.com/learn/what-is-a-upi-pin/) and completes the process

Step 6: The customer is redirected to the selected app for payment confirmation

[Learn how to accept payments via UPI without glitches](https://razorpay.com/upi/) .

## How will UPI Intent flow help iOS users?

Payments in iOS are supported via ‘Collect flow’. For example, an iOS user has to enter the [VPA](https://razorpay.com/learn/what-is-virtual-payment-address-vpa/) to make a payment, whereas, an android user can get away by clicking on the installed UPI App.
With the introduction of UPI intent flow for iOS, businesses can offer flexibility to their customers.

| --- | --- |
|* Click and pay |* User needs to enter [UPI ID](https://razorpay.com/learn/what-is-upi-id/) /VPA to initiate payment.

|* Switching between shopping app, UPI PSP app and SMS is a thing of the past.
* Seamlessly switch between apps |* Involves a lengthy flow |
|* Users can choose any UPI app on their mobile |* Many background API calls and SMS notifications |
|* Ease of making payment and better user experience results in higher conversion rate |* Delay in SMS/ app notification can lead to an unsatisfactory user experience |

End result: A higher conversion rate, decrease in abandoned carts and time to complete the payment. And finally, the cherry on a sundae–better user experience for your customers.

No more push/SMS notifications for customers.
No more wandering between apps to complete payment.

The overall process will become significantly smoother, which will also increase the adoption/usage of UPI as a payment option.

UPI intent flow on IOS will be available for Google Pay, Phonepe, PayTM, and BHIM. Additionally, NPCI is also working with Apple to figure out a solution to support App-to-App scanning, which means in near future UPI intent will be available for all UPI Apps on iOS.

PSP stands for Payment Service Providers.

UPI intent supports one-time payments, mandate/recurring payments and e-Rupee or digital Rupee transactions.

# Audit Report — patel-autoprint frontend flows

## CRITICAL

None found that hard-crashes the primary cash/UPI happy path. The most damaging issues below are MAJOR and each can break a real user flow.

## MAJOR

**1. Online (Razorpay) payment is permanently broken on the `/portal` route — `frontend/src/pages/CustomerPortal.jsx:1548-1555`**
`fetchRazorpayConfig()` calls `/api/guest/shop/${shopSlug}/payment-config`. On `/portal` (the homepage's main link, `App.jsx:67`) `shopSlug` is `undefined`, so the URL becomes `/api/guest/shop/undefined/payment-config`, which 404s (`backend/src/server.js:1909`), the error is swallowed, and `razorpayConfig` stays `null`. Then `handlePlaceOrder` (`CustomerPortal.jsx:1686-1693`) blocks the "Online" option with "Online payment not configured for this shop". Note `fetchUpiQr` (`:1538-1546`) *does* correctly fall back to the default shop, so UPI works but "Pay Online" never does on the main portal URL — even for the default shop with Razorpay configured.

**2. Guest 401s wrongly redirect customers to the homepage — `frontend/src/services/api.js:22-27`**
The response interceptor redirects `window.location.href = '/'` and wipes `token`/`user` on ANY 401, with no URL check (unlike the superadmin's api.js which guards `/superadmin/login`). Combined with the request interceptor (`api.js:8-17`) attaching any `localStorage` token to *all* requests — including `/api/guest/*` — a stale/expired shop-owner token can ride along on guest requests. Today no guest endpoint returns 401 (they return 404/400/409/410/402/500), so it won't fire yet, but the first 401 on any guest/protected call a customer makes will silently kick them to the homepage and wipe their session. Guest requests should be exempt from the token attachment and the 401 redirect.

**3. WhatsApp-claimed orders: pressing "Back" strands the customer and orphans the order — `CustomerPortal.jsx:1450`, `:1717`, `:1775`, `:1476-1478`**
The WhatsApp claim sets `activeStep=1` directly while the local `files` state stays empty (`:1775` passes `files` to Step1Upload, not `uploadedOrder.files`). The Back button is shown at step 1 (`:1809-1819`). Going back to step 0 shows an empty upload area, and "Upload Files" just toasts "Please select files" (`:1477`). The only way forward is uploading new files, which creates a brand-new order (`handleUpload` replaces `uploadedOrder`), permanently abandoning the WhatsApp order whose session was already marked CLAIMED.

**4. Order can be placed with a wrong/zero total if the price fetch fails — `CustomerPortal.jsx:1682-1709` + `:1836-1845`**
The "Place Order" button is disabled only while `loadingPrice`; nothing checks `priceData`. If `fetchPrice` (`:1525-1536`) errors, the customer can still confirm. The stored `totalPrice` at that point comes from the per-file settings loop (`:1505-1513`) hitting `/guest/orders/:id/settings`, whose backend recalculates the whole order using *only that one file's settings* applied to all files (`backend/src/server.js:989-995`) — or 0 for a WhatsApp order that was never priced. The `/price` endpoint later corrects `totalPrice` server-side, but if it never succeeds the customer is charged a wrong amount.

## MINOR

**5. Double error toast on guest failures — `OrderTracking.jsx:33-39`, `CustomerPortal.jsx:1453-1455`**
The interceptor already toasts the backend message (`api.js:29-30`), and the catch blocks toast "Order not found" / set the waError alert again. Duplicate user-visible errors (e.g., a 409/410 WhatsApp link shows both a toast and an Alert).

**6. `copyOrderId` throws on non-secure origins — `CustomerPortal.jsx:1320-1325`**
`navigator.clipboard.writeText(order.id)` throws a TypeError over plain HTTP (clipboard API unavailable), so the "Order ID copied!" toast never shows and the click errors.

**7. Razorpay options don't do what the comments claim — `CustomerPortal.jsx:1607-1615`**
`method: { upi: {} }` and `hide: { netbanking: true, card: true, wallet: true, ... }` are not the documented shapes. Razorpay's `method` keys expect booleans, and the `hide` object only supports `contact`/`email`. These are likely ignored, so the "UPI ONLY" checkout intent may silently show cards/netbanking/wallet instead. Also `prefill.contact` (`:1592`) passes an arbitrary user-typed phone (placeholder even shows "+1234567890"), which Razorpay's contact validation may reject. Not a crash, but the UPI-only restriction can fail.

**8. `OrderTracking.jsx:106` — `order.totalPrice?.toFixed(2)` renders "₹undefined"** when `totalPrice` is null (new orders default to 0 but any null value renders literal "undefined"). Cosmetic.

**9. Superadmin "EXPIRING" is always 0 — `superadmin/src/pages/Dashboard.jsx:215` + `backend/src/server.js:2296-2306`**
`getSubscriptionStatus` never returns `'EXPIRING'`; expiring shops are counted into `EXPIRED`. The dashboard chip is therefore always 0 and expiring-shop filtering can't work. Display/data bug, not a crash.

**10. Orders placed via `/portal` go to an arbitrary shop — `backend/src/server.js:888` + `CustomerPortal.jsx:1485-1486`**
With no slug, neither `shopId` nor `shopRef` is sent, and the backend resolves `findShopByRef(undefined)` → `prisma.shop.findFirst()` (first shop). With multiple shops, the homepage's `/portal` link routes orders to the wrong shop. Minor since `/s/:slug` links (WhatsApp, superadmin) are correct.

- **ThemeContext.jsx / theme.js / main.jsx / App.jsx**: `keyframes` and `Zoom` imports are valid MUI exports; localStorage guarded; ErrorBoundary present; routes correct.

- **Superadmin panel**: all API paths (`/superadmin/stats`, `/shops`, `/shops/:id`, `/shops/:id/regenerate-key`, `/change-password`) exist server-side; no missing imports; no crash paths found in Login/Dashboard/ShopDetail/dialogs.

export default function CustomerPortal() {
  const { slug: shopSlug } = useParams() || {};
  const [searchParams, setSearchParams] = useSearchParams();
  const { mode, toggleMode } = useThemeMode();
  const [activeStep, setActiveStep] = useState(0);
  const [files, setFiles] = useState([]);
  const [customerInfo, setCustomerInfo] = useState({ name: '', phone: '', email: '' });
  const [fileSettings, setFileSettings] = useState({});
  const [uploadedOrder, setUploadedOrder] = useState(null);
  const [paymentMethod, setPaymentMethod] = useState('cash');
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [priceData, setPriceData] = useState(null);
  const [loadingPrice, setLoadingPrice] = useState(false);
  const [upiQrUrl, setUpiQrUrl] = useState('');
  const [shop, setShop] = useState(null);
  const [shopError, setShopError] = useState('');
  const [waSource, setWaSource] = useState(false);
  const [waError, setWaError] = useState('');
  
  // Razorpay payment state
  const [razorpayConfig, setRazorpayConfig] = useState(null);
  const [processingPayment, setProcessingPayment] = useState(false);
  const [paymentError, setPaymentError] = useState('');
  
  const waToken = searchParams.get('wa');
  const waClaimedRef = useRef(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!waToken || waClaimedRef.current) return;
    waClaimedRef.current = true;
    let cancelled = false;
    setLoading(true);
    api.post(`/guest/whatsapp/${waToken}/claim`)
      .then((result) => {
        if (cancelled || !result.success) return;
        setUploadedOrder(result.data.order);
        setCustomerInfo((prev) => ({
          ...prev,
          phone: result.data.customerPhone || '',
          name: result.data.customerName || '',
        }));
        setWaSource(true);
        setActiveStep(1);
        toast.success('WhatsApp files received!');
      })
      .catch((err) => {
        if (!cancelled) setWaError(err?.message || 'This WhatsApp link is invalid or already used.');
      })
      .finally(() => {
        if (!cancelled) setLoading(false);
        setSearchParams({}, { replace: true });
      });
    return () => { cancelled = true; };
  }, [waToken]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!shopSlug) return;
    let cancelled = false;
    api.get(`/guest/shop/${shopSlug}`)
      .then((result) => {
        if (!cancelled && result.success) setShop(result.data);
      })
      .catch((err) => {
        if (!cancelled) setShopError(err?.message || 'Shop not found');
      });
    return () => { cancelled = true; };
  }, [shopSlug]);

  const handleUpload = async () => {
    if (files.length === 0) { toast.error('Please select files'); return; }
    setLoading(true);
    try {
      const formData = new FormData();
      files.forEach((f) => formData.append('files', f));
      formData.append('customerName', customerInfo.name);
      formData.append('customerPhone', customerInfo.phone);
      formData.append('customerEmail', customerInfo.email);
      if (shop?.id) formData.append('shopId', shop.id);
      else if (shopSlug) formData.append('shopRef', shopSlug);

      const result = await api.post('/guest/upload', formData);
      if (result.success) {
        setUploadedOrder(result.data);
        toast.success(`${result.data.files?.length || 0} file(s) analyzed!`);
        setActiveStep(1);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Upload failed');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const handleSaveSettings = async () => {
    if (!uploadedOrder) return;
    setLoading(true);
    try {
      for (const [fileIndex, settings] of Object.entries(fileSettings)) {
        const fileId = uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.id;
        if (fileId) {
          await api.put(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/settings`, {
            fileId,
            settings: { ...uploadedOrder.files?.[fileIndex]?.settings, ...settings },
          });
        }
      }
      const updated = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}`);
      if (updated.success) setUploadedOrder(updated.data);
      toast.success('Settings saved!');
      setActiveStep(2);
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to save settings');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const fetchPrice = async () => {
    if (!uploadedOrder) return;
    setLoadingPrice(true);
    try {
      const result = await api.get(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/price`);
      if (result.success) setPriceData(result.data);
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to get price');
    } finally {
      setLoadingPrice(false);
    }
  };

  const fetchUpiQr = async () => {
    try {
      const params = new URLSearchParams();
      if (shop?.slug) params.append('shop', shop.slug);
      else if (shopSlug) params.append('shop', shopSlug);
      const result = await api.get(`/settings/public/upi-qr?${params.toString()}`);
      if (result.success && result.data.url) setUpiQrUrl(result.data.url);
    } catch {}
  };

  const fetchRazorpayConfig = async () => {
    try {
      const result = await api.get(`/guest/shop/${shopSlug}/payment-config`);
      if (result.success && result.data.razorpay) {
        setRazorpayConfig(result.data.razorpay);
      }
    } catch {}
  };

  const loadRazorpayScript = () => {
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      if (window.Razorpay) return resolve(true);
      const script = document.createElement('script');
      script.src = 'https://checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js';
      script.onload = () => resolve(true);
      script.onerror = () => reject(new Error('Failed to load Razorpay script'));
      document.body.appendChild(script);
    });
  };

  const handleRazorpayPayment = async (orderId, amount, keyId, shopName, orderToken) => {
    setProcessingPayment(true);
    setPaymentError('');
    try {
      // 1. Load Razorpay script
      await loadRazorpayScript();
      
      // 2. Create Razorpay order via backend
      const result = await api.post(`/guest/orders/${orderId}/payment/initiate`, { method: 'razorpay' });
      if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.message || 'Failed to initiate payment');
      
      const { orderId: rpOrderId, amount: rpAmount, keyId: rpKeyId, shopName: rpShopName, orderToken: rpOrderToken } = result.data;
      
      // 3. Open Razorpay Checkout restricted to UPI only (GPay, PhonePe, PayTM, etc.)
      const options = {
        key: rpKeyId,
        amount: rpAmount,
        currency: 'INR',
        name: rpShopName,
        description: `Order #${rpOrderToken}`,
        order_id: rpOrderId,
        // Pre-fill the customer contact so the checkout never asks for a mobile number
        prefill: {
          name: customerInfo.name || '',
          contact: customerInfo.phone || '',
          email: customerInfo.email || '',
        },
        // UPI Intent: shows Google Pay / PhonePe / PayTM / BHIM buttons that open
        // the selected app directly - no VPA entry, no mobile number, no SMS.
        upi: {
          flow: 'intent',
          intent_flow_timeout: 5,
          intents: [
            { type: 'google_pay', flow: 'intent' },
            { type: 'phonepe', flow: 'intent' },
            { type: 'paytm', flow: 'intent' },
            { type: 'bhim_upi', flow: 'intent' },
          ],
        },
        method: { upi: {} }, // Show ONLY UPI — cards, netbanking, wallet hidden
        hide: {
          netbanking: true,
          card: true,
          wallet: true,
          bank_transfer: true,
          emi: true,
          pay_later: true,
        },
        handler: async (response) => {
          // Payment successful - verify on backend
          await verifyRazorpayPayment(orderId, response.razorpay_payment_id);
        },
        modal: {
          ondismiss: () => {
            setProcessingPayment(false);
            setPaymentError('Payment cancelled. Please try again or choose another method.');
          },
        },
        theme: { color: '#1976d2' },
      };
      
      const rzp = new window.Razorpay(options);
      rzp.on('payment.failed', (response) => {
        setProcessingPayment(false);
        setPaymentError(response.error.description || 'Payment failed. Please try again.');
      });
      rzp.open();
      
    } catch (err) {
      setProcessingPayment(false);
      setPaymentError(err.message || 'Payment initiation failed');
      toast.error(err.message || 'Payment initiation failed');
    }
  };

  const verifyRazorpayPayment = async (orderId, paymentId) => {
    try {
      const result = await api.post(`/guest/orders/${orderId}/payment/verify`, { paymentId, method: 'razorpay' });
      if (result.success) {
        setUploadedOrder(result.data);
        toast.success('Payment verified! Order confirmed.');
        setActiveStep(3);
        pushShopHistory();
      } else {
        throw new Error(result.message || 'Payment verification failed');
      }
    } catch (err) {
      setPaymentError(err.message || 'Payment verification failed');
      toast.error(err.message || 'Payment verification failed');
    } finally {
      setProcessingPayment(false);
    }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    if (activeStep === 2) {
      fetchUpiQr();
      fetchRazorpayConfig();
    }
  }, [activeStep]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (activeStep === 2 && uploadedOrder) fetchPrice();
  }, [activeStep, uploadedOrder?.id]);

  // Keep the selected payment method valid for this shop (default = first accepted)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (activeStep !== 2) return;
    const accepted = shop?.settings?.acceptedPaymentMethods;
    if (Array.isArray(accepted) && accepted.length > 0 && !accepted.includes(paymentMethod)) {
      setPaymentMethod(accepted[0]);
    }
  }, [activeStep, shop, paymentMethod]);

  const handlePlaceOrder = async () => {
    if (!uploadedOrder || !paymentMethod) { toast.error('Select payment method'); return; }
    
    // For online payment (Razorpay UPI Intent), handle differently
    if (paymentMethod === 'online') {
      if (!razorpayConfig) {
        toast.error('Online payment not configured for this shop');
        return;
      }
      await handleRazorpayPayment(uploadedOrder.id);
      return;
    }
    
    setLoading(true);
    try {
      const result = await api.post(`/guest/orders/${uploadedOrder.id}/confirm`, { paymentMethod });
      if (result.success) {
        setUploadedOrder(result.data);
        toast.success('Order placed!');
        setActiveStep(3);
        pushShopHistory();
      }
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(err.message || 'Failed to place order');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  const handleNext = async () => {
    if (activeStep === 0) await handleUpload();
    else if (activeStep === 1) await handleSaveSettings();
    else if (activeStep === 2) await handlePlaceOrder();
  };

  const handleBack = () => setActiveStep((prev) => prev - 1);

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============================================
// CORE MODELS
// ============================================

model Shop {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  name            String
  slug            String?  @unique
  agentKey        String?  @unique
  settings        Json?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  users             User[]
  customers         Customer[]
  orders            Order[]
  printers          Printer[]
  pricingRules      PricingRule[]
  orderFiles        OrderFile[]
  printJobs         PrintJob[]
  subscription      Subscription?
  whatsappSessions  WhatsAppSession[]

  @@map("shops")
}

model User {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId       String?
  email        String
  passwordHash String
  name         String
  role         String   @default("OPERATOR") // SUPER_ADMIN, OWNER, MANAGER, OPERATOR, CUSTOMER
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop? @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@map("users")
}

model Subscription {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId      String   @unique
  plan        String   @default("FREE")   // FREE, STARTER, PROFESSIONAL, ENTERPRISE
  status      String   @default("ACTIVE") // ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, CANCELLED (expiry is computed from endDate)
  price       Float    @default(0)
  endDate     DateTime?
  maxPrinters Int      @default(1)
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@map("subscriptions")
}

model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  shopId    String
  name      String
  phone     String?
  email     String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  shop   Shop    @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  orders Order[]

  @@map("customers")
}

model Order {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  token         Int?
  customerId    String?
  shopId        String
  status        String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, APPROVED, PRINTING, COMPLETED, REJECTED
  paymentStatus String   @default("UNPAID")  // UNPAID, PAID, REFUNDED, FAILED
  paymentMethod String?
  razorpayOrderId   String?
  razorpayPaymentId String?
  paymentFailureReason String?
  totalPrice    Float    @default(0)
  discount      Float    @default(0)
  tax           Float    @default(0)
  notes         String?
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  approvedAt    DateTime?
  printedAt     DateTime?

  shop      Shop        @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  customer  Customer?   @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id])
  files     OrderFile[]
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@unique([shopId, token])
  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@index([shopId, token])
  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderFile {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId       String
  originalName  String
  storagePath   String
  fileType      String
  size          Int
  pageCount     Int      @default(0)
  colorPageCount Int     @default(0)
  orientation   String   @default("portrait")
  settings      Json?
  shopId        String

  order    Order      @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  shop     Shop       @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  printJobs PrintJob[]

  @@map("order_files")
}

model PrintJob {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId        String
  fileId         String
  sectionIndex   Int      @default(0)
  pages          String   // JSON array of page numbers
  colorMode      String   @default("auto")   // auto, bw, color
  printStyle     String   @default("single") // single, duplex
  paperSize      String   @default("A4")
  pagesPerSheet  Int      @default(1)
  flipDirection  String   @default("long-edge")
  copies         Int      @default(1)
  status         String   @default("PENDING") // PENDING, PROCESSING, PRINTING, COMPLETED, FAILED
  assignedPrinter String?
  shopId         String

  order     Order     @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  file      OrderFile @relation(fields: [fileId], references: [id])
  shop      Shop      @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@map("print_jobs")
}

model Printer {
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  name           String
  ip             String?
  paperSizes     Json     @default("[\"A4\"]")
  colorSupport   Boolean  @default(false)
  duplexSupport  Boolean  @default(false)
  status         String   @default("ONLINE") // ONLINE, OFFLINE, PRINTING, ERROR
  shopId         String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@map("printers")
}

model PricingRule {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  name            String
  bwPerPage       Float    @default(1)   // ₹ per B&W page
  colorPerPage    Float    @default(5)   // ₹ per color page (single)
  colorDuplexPerPage Float @default(10)  // ₹ per color page (duplex)
  taxRate         Float    @default(18)
  shopId          String

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@map("pricing_rules")
}

model WhatsAppSession {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid())
  token         String   @unique
  shopId        String
  customerPhone String
  customerName  String?
  files         Json     @default("[]")
  status        String   @default("NEW") // NEW, CLAIMED, EXPIRED
  expiresAt     DateTime
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  claimedAt     DateTime?

  shop Shop @relation(fields: [shopId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([shopId, status])
  @@map("whatsapp_sessions")
}

# UPI Payment Integration for Indian Businesses — PhonePe, Paytm, Razorpay UPI Intent

TL;DR

UPI is India's dominant payment method — 40%+ of all digital payments. Most Indian websites should accept UPI. This guide covers the three practical integration paths: Razorpay (fastest to ship, covers all UPI apps), Paytm Business (good for Paytm-heavy audiences), and static UPI Intent links (zero-fee but manual reconciliation).
## The three UPI integration paths

|Path |Setup time |Fees |Reconciliation |Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|Razorpay |1-2 days |2% + GST |Automatic webhook |Most businesses |
|Paytm Business |2-3 days |1\.99%+ |Automatic webhook |Paytm-strong audience |
|PhonePe Business |3-5 days |Varies |Automatic |Large B2B volumes |
|Static UPI link (upi://) |5 minutes |0% |Manual (from bank statement) |Low volume, freelancers, donations |

## Path 1 — Razorpay (recommended for most)

Razorpay is the standard for Indian SaaS. Full UPI support including UPI Intent (tap the app icon), collect requests, and autopay for subscriptions.

### Step 1 — Setup

1. Sign up at razorpay.com (KYC: PAN, GST, bank statement)
2. Dashboard → Settings → API Keys → Generate Test Key (start here) and Live Key (after KYC)
3. Note: `rzp_live_XXX` and `secret_XXX`
4. Install SDK:

```bash

\# Node.js

npm install razorpay

\# PHP (Composer)

composer require razorpay/razorpay

```
### Step 2 — Create an order (server-side)

### Step 4 — Verify signature server-side

**Critical:** never trust client-provided `payment_id` . Always verify signature.

**PHP:**

php Copy

```
$attributes = [
    'razorpay_order_id'   => $_POST['razorpay_order_id'],
    'razorpay_payment_id' => $_POST['razorpay_payment_id'],
    'razorpay_signature'  => $_POST['razorpay_signature'],
];

try {
    $api->utility->verifyPaymentSignature($attributes);
    // Signature valid — mark order paid in DB
    markOrderPaid($attributes['razorpay_order_id'], $attributes['razorpay_payment_id']);
} catch (RazorpayApiErrorsSignatureVerificationError $e) {
    http_response_code(400);
    echo 'Invalid signature';
}
```

    if (expected !== sig) return res.status(400).send('Invalid');

## Path 2 — Paytm Business

Paytm has deeper penetration in Tier-2/3 cities. Their SDK is similar to Razorpay; refer to [business.paytm.com](https://business.paytm.com) docs. Fees: 1.99% on UPI, slightly cheaper than Razorpay for high volumes.

## Path 3 — Static UPI Intent link (zero-fee option)

For low-volume, personal, or donation use cases. No gateway fees, but manual reconciliation.

Create a link that opens any UPI app:

Copy

```
upi://pay?
pa=yourname@hdfcbank&pn=Your%20Name&am=500&cu=INR&tn=Invoice+1234
```

Parameters:

* `pa` = payee VPA (UPI ID)
* `pn` = payee name (URL-encoded)
* `am` = amount (optional; user can edit)
* `cu` = currency (INR)
* `tn` = note / reference

Generate QR code server-side:

python Copy

```
import qrcode

data = "upi://pay?pa=yourname@hdfcbank&pn=Your%20Name&am=500&cu=INR&tn=Invoice+1234"
img = qrcode.make(data)
img.save('upi-qr.png')
```

Mobile users tap the link, pick their UPI app, confirm. You reconcile from your bank statement — no automated webhook.

### Verifying payments (manual)

For a business where UPI reconciliation matters:

* Use ICICI/HDFC/Kotak collect-payment APIs (instant SMS → parse reference)
* Or a lightweight service like **Decentro** / **Setu** — webhook on every credit to your UPI ID

## Subscriptions (recurring billing)

Razorpay + UPI AutoPay supports mandates up to ₹15,000/day (NPCI limit).

javascript Copy

```
// Create subscription
const sub = await rzp.
subscriptions.create({
  plan_id: 'plan_XXX',
  customer_notify: 1,
  total_count: 12,    // monthly × 12
  notes: { userId: 42 },
});
```

Customer approves the UPI mandate once; subsequent charges auto-debit. Critical: handle `subscription.charged` webhook, grant/deny access based on status.

## Refunds

**Full refund:**

javascript Copy

```
await rzp.payments.refund(payment_id, {
  speed: 'normal',   // or 'optimum' for faster
});
```

**Partial refund:**

javascript Copy

```
await rzp.payments.refund(payment_id, {
  amount: 20000,    // refund ₹200 from ₹500 payment
});
```

UPI refunds hit the customer's bank in 3-5 days typically.

I have enough to finalize the audit findings and plan. Let me summarize the confirmed bugs from both agents + my own reading:

**Confirmed bugs:**

1. **MAJOR — `/portal` breaks Razorpay config**: `fetchRazorpayConfig()` uses `shopSlug` which is `undefined` on `/portal`. The route is `/api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config`. With `undefined`, URL becomes `/api/guest/shop/undefined/payment-config` → 404 → `razorpayConfig` stays null → online payment shows "not configured". Meanwhile `fetchUpiQr` falls back to default shop. Fix: In `fetchRazorpayConfig`, if no slug, use the default shop. Since the route requires `:ref`, we could use `/api/guest/shop/payment-config`? No. `findShopByRef(undefined)` → first shop. So the frontend could call `/api/guest/shop/${shopSlug || ''}` ... but the route needs a segment. Better: modify the backend route to handle missing ref OR the frontend can pass shop id. Actually the frontend has `shop?.id`. But `fetchRazorpayConfig` doesn't require shop. Simplest: change the backend route `/api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config` to also work when `ref` is not provided by adding a second route or making ref optional. 

   Actually cleanest fix: add `app.get('/api/guest/payment-config', ...)` that resolves default shop, OR modify the frontend to call `/api/guest/shop/${shopSlug || 'default'}`... but there's no default slug. Let me just add a fallback route in backend: `/api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config` already calls `findShopByRef(req.params.ref)` which returns first shop if ref falsy. But the URL path requires something. If we request `/api/guest/shop//payment-config` (double slash) express route won't match.

   Option: In the frontend, when shopSlug is undefined (i.e., on /portal), the `shop` state is also null because `useEffect` doesn't fetch shop without slug (`if (!shopSlug) return;`). So on /portal, `shop` is null. The payment-config route just needs a shop. The simplest backend fix: change route to `/api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config` AND add support for `req.query.shop`. Frontend can call `/api/guest/shop/payment-config`? No.

   Cleanest: change backend route definition so ref is optional: define `app.get('/api/guest/shop/:ref?/payment-config')`? Express 5 supports optional params but the route `/api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config` needs the segment. If `:ref?` is optional then `/api/guest/shop/payment-config` would match `:ref? = undefined`... actually with optional param `/api/guest/shop/:ref?/payment-config` then path `/api/guest/shop/payment-config` would match with ref undefined. Hmm, but Express may interpret `payment-config` as the ref and then `/payment-config` missing. Express route matching: `/api/guest/shop/:ref?/payment-config` vs `/api/guest/shop/payment-config` → ref='payment-config', then needs `/payment-config` suffix → no match. So that doesn't work directly.

   Simplest robust fix: keep backend as-is. Frontend: when shopSlug is undefined, fetch the default shop first (like the shop fetch does via a "default" endpoint) OR just use `/api/guest/shop/default/payment-config` — no.

   Actually, wait — is `/portal` even a real path used? The frontend router — `/portal` is a route in the frontend (homepage link). It degrades to the first shop. Let me check the router. But regardless, the fix: in `fetchRazorpayConfig`, fall back to a default-shop endpoint. I'll add a backend route `app.get('/api/guest/payment-config')` that uses `findShopByRef(undefined)` → first shop, and the frontend calls `/api/guest/shop/${shopSlug}/payment-config` when slug exists, else `/api/guest/payment-config`.

   Also `fetchUpiQr` uses `/api/settings/public/upi-qr` which calls `findShopByRef(req.query.shop)` (first shop when empty) — works on /portal.

   So the backend payment-config route should mirror that. I'll modify `/api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config` to also accept query param, or add `/api/guest/payment-config`. Simplest: change route path to `/api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config` AND add a route `/api/guest/payment-config`. Let me just add the second route that delegates.

2. **MAJOR — Guest 401s wrongly redirect to '/'**: api.js response interceptor redirects on any 401. Guest endpoints never 401 currently, but the request interceptor attaches token to guest requests too (harmless). The real risk: if a guest endpoint returns 401 (e.g., future auth-protected), the customer gets kicked to homepage. Fix: don't attach token for `/guest/` paths, and don't redirect on 401 for `/guest/` paths. This is low-risk hardening. Worth doing.

3. **MAJOR-ish — WhatsApp claim: reload re-claims already-claimed session → 409 WA_SESSION_USED → customer sees "already used" error**. The audit flagged: `waClaimedRef` resets on reload; if a customer reloads the page (after claiming, before order placed), the `?wa=` param is removed via `setSearchParams({}, { replace: true })` in finally, so a reload won't re-claim. Wait — the claim effect does `setSearchParams({}, { replace: true })` which removes the `wa` param. So after claim, URL no longer has `?wa`. A reload won't re-trigger. Good — but there's a subtle bug: `setSearchParams({}, { replace: true })` REMOVES ALL params. If the page has other params (none here), fine. But on `/s/:slug`, after claim, `waSource=true`, `activeStep=1`. Reload → component remounts → `waToken` is null (param removed) → no re-claim → activeStep=0, uploadedOrder=null → customer sees upload page again and their order is lost (session exists but UI shows fresh upload). That's a UX issue but not a crash. The claim 409 only happens if the param persists. Since we remove it, it's OK-ish. But if the customer uses Back button to return to the original WA link... edge. Low priority.

   Actually the more important WhatsApp issue: **Back button after WA claim**. At step 1 (configure), pressing Back → step 0 (upload) shows empty upload; if the customer uploads, it creates a NEW order, abandoning the WA order. The audit flagged this as MAJOR. Fix: when `waSource`, hide/disable the Back button at step 1 (or make Step1Upload show the WA files). Simplest: disable Back when `waSource && activeStep === 1`. Actually the Back button is `activeStep > 0 && activeStep < 3`. When waSource and activeStep===1, hide Back. That prevents stranding. Good, easy fix.

4. **Order placed with wrong total if price fetch fails**: `handlePlaceOrder` uses `priceData` only for display; the confirm route uses server totalPrice. The frontend button disables while `loadingPrice`. If price fetch failed, `priceData` stays null and the order is confirmed with server-side totalPrice (which was set by the /price route? No — the /price route sets order.totalPrice server-side; but if the fetch failed, totalPrice may be stale/default). Let me check: `fetchPrice` GET `/guest/orders/:id/price` — does it update server totalPrice or just return it? Need to check. The audit said "Order placed with wrong total if price fetch fails" — the fix: block Place Order until priceData is loaded, or re-fetch in handlePlaceOrder. Simplest: if `activeStep===2 && !priceData && !loadingPrice`, re-fetch; and disable Place Order if priceData null. Let me check the /price route to see if it persists totalPrice.

5. **MAJOR — Office files can't print on Render (Linux)**: `convertOfficeToPdf` spawns `powershell.exe` which doesn't exist on Linux. So `processFile` for docx/pptx/xlsx → `convertOfficeToPdf` → spawn error → reject → in `processAndDispatchOrder`, catch → job FAILED. So office-doc orders never reach the agent. This is THE big "no glitches" gap I identified. Fix options:
   a) Agent-side conversion: backend marks office jobs PRINTING and serves the ORIGINAL file; the agent converts locally on Windows (where the agent runs) via PowerShell COM. The file route already falls back to `job.file.storagePath` (the original). But the file route searches print-ready dir first and falls back to original — for office jobs we'd want the original served. But we also need nup/duplex etc applied — impossible for office on Linux backend anyway. So: for office files, the backend should just mark PRINTING and let the agent do conversion + print. The agent needs a conversion step (PowerShell) before printing.
   
   Let me check what the agent does with a non-PDF file. Agent downloads `${job.id}.pdf`?? The audit agent said "it always saves as .pdf". So the agent would try to print a .docx saved as .pdf. That's a bug. Fix: agent should detect office files and convert via PowerShell before printing, or use the file's real extension.

   This is the biggest fix. Scope: modify agent/index.js and desktop/electron/agent.js to (1) save file with correct extension, (2) if office, convert to PDF via powershell COM script before printing. Plus backend: for office files, don't run convertOfficeToPdf (or catch failure gracefully and still mark PRINTING so agent handles it). Actually simplest and most robust: backend, for office files in `processFile`, should return original storagePath (skip conversion) — then in processAndDispatchOrder the job is marked PRINTING (since processFile succeeded), the file route falls back to storagePath (original .docx), agent downloads it, converts locally, prints.

   But wait: the file route's fallback: `filePath = job.file.storagePath` only if the print-ready search finds nothing. For office files if we skip conversion, no print-ready file exists → fallback to original. Good.

   But hold on — does `processFile` get called for office with pagesPerSheet>1 → would need conversion to apply nup. If we skip conversion entirely, nup for office docs is lost (agent converts and prints single PDF, no nup). Trade-off: correctness of nup for office vs ability to print at all. Since backend on Linux can't convert anyway, nup for office was already broken. Agent-side conversion preserves duplex/copies/paperSize but not nup. Now I have a comprehensive picture. Let me consolidate the confirmed findings from the audits and my own reading:

**Confirmed bugs:**

1. **MAJOR: `/portal` route breaks Razorpay config.** `fetchRazorpayConfig()` uses `shopSlug` which is `undefined` on `/portal` → URL `/api/guest/shop/undefined/payment-config` → `findShopByRef('undefined')` → shop not found → 404 → razorpayConfig stays null → online payment unavailable on /portal. Meanwhile `fetchUpiQr` falls back to default shop (no shop param → findShopByRef(undefined) → first shop). Fix: in `fetchRazorpayConfig`, if `shopSlug` is undefined, fall back to a default-shop config endpoint or use the same pattern as fetchUpiQr (which sends `?shop=` param). Actually the cleanest: backend route `/api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config` — for the /portal case, frontend should request a default. I'll add support: if `shopSlug` undefined, use `/api/guest/shop/default/payment-config`? findShopByRef('default') → bySlug? no → byId? no → by name? no → returns null. Hmm. Better: modify backend to fall back to first shop when ref not found? That would mask 404s though. Actually simplest robust fix: in frontend `fetchRazorpayConfig`, if `shopSlug` is undefined, call a new/fallback path. The backend already has `/api/settings/public/upi-qr` that does `findShopByRef(req.query.shop)` → default shop if no query. I could add `/api/settings/public/payment-config` similarly. But the payment-config route is under /guest/shop/:ref. Let me add a parallel public route `/api/settings/public/payment-config` that mirrors upi-qr. Then frontend uses it when shopSlug undefined, else /guest/shop/:ref/payment-config. Actually simpler: just change the frontend to use `/api/settings/public/payment-config?shop=` for both cases (like fetchUpiQr does), and add that backend route. Consistent and minimal.

   Wait — but `/api/guest/shop/:ref` also used for shop info. On /portal, shopSlug undefined, shop stays null. The header shows "Patel AutoPrint". That's existing behavior, fine.

2. **MAJOR: Guest 401s wrongly redirect to '/'.** api.js response interceptor redirects to '/' on any 401, and clears localStorage. Guest endpoints shouldn't attach the token at all (currently request interceptor attaches ANY localStorage token to guest requests too, which is wrong but harmless since those routes are public). If a guest request ever returns 401 (e.g. some middleware), it would kick the customer to homepage. Currently no guest route returns 401, so it's latent. Fix: exempt `/guest/` paths from both token attach and 401 redirect. Low-risk hardening. Worth doing since "no glitches."

3. **MAJOR: WhatsApp claim — Back button strands customer** (from agent audit item 3, truncated). The agent said: "Step 1 after WA claim, pressing Back → step 0 shows empty upload (files state empty). Uploading creates a NEW order, abandoning the WA order." Looking at the code: after claim, `uploadedOrder` is set, `waSource=true`, `activeStep=1`. Back button at step 1 goes to step 0 which shows Step1Upload with local `files` (empty) — not the WA files. If customer uploads new files, it creates a new order. Also: the `waClaimedRef` — after claim, `setSearchParams({}, {replace:true})` removes the `wa` param. On the `/portal` route that's fine. But note: the effect deps `[waToken]` — after params cleared, effect re-runs with waToken=null, guard `if (!waToken...)` returns. Fine. 

   But there's another WhatsApp issue the agent may have flagged: if customer reloads the page after claiming, `waClaimedRef` resets (new component instance) and searchParams is now empty (wa removed), so no re-claim. OK. But if the WA link is opened twice or the claim is retried... the backend returns 409 WA_SESSION_USED on second claim. The effect only runs once per waToken. Fine.

   Fix for the back-button: when `waSource && activeStep === 1`, hide the Back button (or make it not go back). Simplest: `{activeStep > 0 && activeStep < 3 && !(waSource && activeStep === 1) && (...)}`. That prevents stranding.

4. **MAJOR: Office files can't print on Render (Linux).** `convertOfficeToPdf` spawns `powershell.exe` which doesn't exist on Linux Render → office jobs FAIL. In `processFile`, office ext → convertOfficeToPdf → spawn error → rejects → in processAndDispatchOrder catch → job FAILED. So docx/pptx/xlsx orders never reach the agent. This is the big "gap" I identified earlier. Fix options:
   a) Agent-side conversion: backend marks office jobs PRINTING and serves the ORIGINAL file (fallback path `job.file.storagePath`); the agent converts locally on Windows via PowerShell COM before printing. This matches the architecture (agents run on Windows where Office is installed).
   b) Server-side conversion on Linux: not feasible without LibreOffice installed on Render.

   Implementation for (a):
   - Backend `processFile`: for office files, DON'T convert; return `file.storagePath` (like images). Now I have a comprehensive picture. Let me consolidate findings.

## Audit summary

### Confirmed bugs (frontend — CustomerPortal.jsx)

1. **MAJOR: `/portal` route breaks Razorpay config.** `fetchRazorpayConfig()` uses `shopSlug` which is `undefined` on `/portal` → URL `/api/guest/shop/undefined/payment-config` → `findShopByRef('undefined')` → bySlug no, byId no, by name 'undefined' no → `findFirst()` → actually returns first shop! Wait — `findShopByRef` falls back to `prisma.shop.findFirst()` if no match. So `/api/guest/shop/undefined/payment-config` would return the first shop's config. So online payment might still work by accident on /portal. But the audit agent claimed 404. Hmm. The frontend agent said "fetchRazorpayConfig uses shopSlug which is undefined on /portal → 404". Let me check: route `/api/guest/shop/:ref/payment-config`, ref = 'undefined' (string). findShopByRef('undefined') → slug lookup 'undefined' → not found → id lookup 'undefined' → not found → name lookup → not found → fallback findFirst() → returns first shop. So NOT a 404. Unless there are no shops. So it actually works (returns first shop). Minor robustness issue but not a bug per se. However, on `/portal` there is no shop loaded (shopSlug undefined → `if (!shopSlug) return;` in shop fetch), so `shop` is null → `shop.settings.acceptedPaymentMethods` undefined → Step3Review acceptedMethods undefined → payment methods default. And fetchUpiQr passes no shop → default shop. So /portal works against default shop. OK so not a real bug, but fragile. I'll note it. Not critical.

   Actually wait — the audit agent said "online payment not configured for this shop" for /portal. Let me think: if paymentGatewayConfig razorpay enabled for the default shop, then `/api/guest/shop/undefined/payment-config` returns razorpay config for first shop. So online works. If the first shop isn't the intended default... eh. It's fragile but functional. Skip or low priority.

2. **MAJOR: Guest 401s wrongly redirect to '/'.** In api.js, any 401 → redirect to '/'. Guest requests should not redirect. Currently guest endpoints never return 401 (they're public), so latent. But also guest requests attach the token from localStorage (harmless since backend ignores it for guest routes, but if a shop operator is logged in and opens a guest portal... the token gets attached; guest routes don't use auth so fine). The 401 redirect for guest requests: if any guest endpoint returns 401, customer gets kicked to home. Low risk now but worth hardening: don't redirect on 401 for `/guest/` paths. Also don't attach token for guest requests (best practice). Quick fix, low risk. I'll do it.

3. **MAJOR: WhatsApp-claimed orders — Back button strands customer.** After WA claim, step 1 shows configure with `uploadedOrder.files`. Pressing Back → step 0 shows empty upload (files state empty, uploadedOrder separate). Uploading creates a NEW order, abandoning the WA order. Fix: hide/disable Back on step 1 when `waSource`. Small, safe fix. Also the claim effect re-runs? Deps `[waToken]`; after claim, `setSearchParams({}, {replace:true})` removes wa param → waToken becomes null → effect re-runs → guard `if (!waToken...) return` → fine. But note: `waClaimedRef` is set true BEFORE success. If claim fails (e.g. already claimed), `waClaimedRef` stays true, and searchParams cleared, waError shown. OK.

   Actually there's another WhatsApp issue: on step 1 the files come from uploadedOrder. The Step2Configure gets `files={uploadedOrder?.files || files}`. Good. The customer's settings saved via handleSaveSettings loops over fileSettings entries keyed by fileIndex — for WA orders fileSettings is empty ({}), so loop does nothing, then GET updated order, setActiveStep(2). Works (uses default settings). OK.

4. **MAJOR-ish: Order placed with wrong total if price fetch fails.** handlePlaceOrder doesn't re-check priceData. If fetchPrice failed (loadingPrice false, priceData null), the order confirms with server-side totalPrice computed at upload-time (/guest/upload sets totalPrice via pricing at line 675/685) — but the customer may have changed settings on step 1 after upload! Wait — settings changes on step 1 call /settings PUT which... does it recompute totalPrice? Let me check. If the customer changes copies/sections on step 1, totalPrice in DB is stale unless /price updates it. /price GET recomputes and updates totalPrice (line 1140-1143). But if price fetch fails silently (catch → toast, priceData stays null), the confirm uses stale totalPrice. For online payment, initiate uses order.totalPrice (line 1186). So there's a real risk: price could be stale when price fetch fails.

   Fix: in handlePlaceOrder (and for online), ensure price is fetched fresh before confirming, or block if priceData null. Simplest safe fix: if priceData is null and activeStep===2, re-fetch price before confirm; if still null, block. Actually the cleanest: always fetchPrice() before placing order (await it), then confirm. Let me make handlePlaceOrder fetch price first (await), and only proceed if priceData.total != null. Also for online payment, the initiate uses order.totalPrice which is set by the last /price call — so fetching price first ensures it's fresh. Good, low-risk fix.

5. **MINOR: Double error toast** on payment failure (catch does toast + setPaymentError, and Step3Review shows paymentError → user sees both toast and inline). Trivial. Skip or fix. Low value.

6. **MINOR: copyOrderId throws on HTTP** (navigator.clipboard requires secure context). Only affects localhost dev. Skip.

7. **MINOR: OrderTracking "₹undefined"** — display bug. Quick fix but low priority.

8. **MINOR: superadmin EXPIRING always 0** — display bug in superadmin panel. Low priority.

### Confirmed bugs (backend — office conversion on Render/Linux)

9. **CRITICAL: Office files (docx/pptx/xlsx) can't print on Render.** `convertOfficeToPdf` spawns `powershell.exe` — only available on Windows. On Render (Linux), `spawn('powershell.exe')` → ENOENT error → rejects → processAndDispatchOrder catch → job FAILED. So office-doc orders never reach the agent. This is the big gap I identified earlier.

   Also note: the analyzer works fine for office files (mammoth / zip scanning). But processFile fails.

   Fix approach: **agent-side conversion.** The backend runs on Linux and cannot convert. The agent runs on Windows (where printers are) and can run PowerShell COM. So:
   - Backend: for office files, DON'T convert server-side. Instead mark job PRINTING and serve the ORIGINAL file. The `/api/agent/jobs/:id/file` route already falls back to `job.file.storagePath` if no print-ready PDF exists. But processAndDispatchOrder currently calls processFile → convertOfficeToPdf → throws → job FAILED. 
   
   Wait — let me check: in processAndDispatchOrder, processFile for an office file calls convertOfficeToPdf which spawns powershell.exe and rejects → the try/catch marks job FAILED. So the job never becomes PRINTING. To let the agent handle office: change processFile so that for office files, if powershell isn't available (or always on non-win32), return the original storagePath (like images) → job becomes PRINTING → file route falls back to storagePath → serves original docx → agent downloads it. Agent then needs to convert docx→pdf locally before printing.

   So the fix has two parts:
   a) Backend printProcessor.processFile: for office files on non-Windows, skip conversion, return original path. (Keep conversion on Windows for local/dev if useful, or always skip — simpler to skip always and let agent convert.) Actually keep it: if `process.platform === 'win32'` try convert; else return original. That way the local Windows desktop server still converts. But the deployed backend is on Render/Linux. The agent handles conversion. Simplest robust: always return original for office, agent converts. But then nup/duplex for office won't be applied server-side — agent would need to apply them. pdf-to-printer options handle duplex/copies/paperSize. Nup for office would be lost (agent can't easily nup without pdf-lib... actually agent could, but that's heavy). 

   Hmm. Tradeoff: Currently office + nup is fully broken (job FAILED). If we make agent convert docx→pdf and print with duplex/copies/paperSize, but lose nup and page-range for office, that's still a huge improvement. Page-range for office: processFile does extractPages after conversion — if we skip conversion, page-range isn't applied either. But page-range is rarely set for office (customers usually print all). Acceptable. Let me implement agent-side conversion and note nup/page-range limitation for office files.

   Actually wait — can we do better? The agent could apply nup if it had pdf-lib... The standalone agent and desktop agent don't have pdf-lib. Adding it is heavy. I'll keep it simple: agent converts office→pdf, prints with copies/duplex/paper. Document the nup limitation.

   Implementation:
   - backend printProcessor.js `processFile`: office branch → if `process.platform !== 'win32'`, return file.storagePath (let agent convert). Else keep current conversion path.
   - The file route already falls back to storagePath. Good — no server.js change needed for serving.
   - Agent (standalone + desktop): after download, if file type is office (docx/pptx/xlsx/doc/ppt/xls), convert to PDF via PowerShell COM before printing. Need the ps1 script in the agent dir (copy of convert-office-to-pdf.ps1) or inline PowerShell. I'll copy the script into both agent folders.
   - Both agents must save the downloaded file with the CORRECT extension, not always `.pdf`. Currently: standalone `const ext = job.file?.fileType === 'pdf' ? '.pdf' : '.pdf';` — always .pdf! And desktop `const filePath = path.join(this.cacheDir, `${job.id}.pdf`);`. That's a bug: even if the server serves an original .docx (fallback), the agent saves it as .pdf and pdf-to-printer can't print a docx named .pdf. So I must fix extension + conversion in both agents.

   Let me design agent change:
   ```
   const officeExts = ['docx','pptx','xlsx','doc','ppt','xls'];
   const type = job.file?.fileType || 'pdf';
   const ext = type === 'jpeg' ? 'jpg' : type;
   const filePath = path.join(cacheDir, `${job.id}.${ext}`);
   // download
   if (officeExts.includes(type)) {
     const pdfPath = path.join(cacheDir, `${job.id}.pdf`);
     await convertOfficeToPdf(filePath, pdfPath); // PowerShell COM
     filePathForPrint = pdfPath;
   } else {
     filePathForPrint = filePath;
   }
   // print filePathForPrint
   ```
   And convertOfficeToPdf uses the bundled script `convert-office-to-pdf.ps1`.

   Wait, but pdf-to-printer can also print images? It uses SumatraPDF and supports images I believe. But images get contact-sheeted server-side normally (createContactSheet) when there are multiple, or single image jobs? For a single image order, processFile returns storagePath (image) → job PRINTING → file route serves original image → agent saves as .jpg → pdf-to-printer... Actually pdf-to-printer DOES support printing images (it uses Windows spooler/Sumatra). Single images are rare (mostly multiple photos → contact sheet PDF). Keep images as-is but with correct extension; if pdf-to-printer can't print, that's pre-existing behavior. Fine.

10. **processAndDispatchOrder** sets job status PRINTING for images too (no conversion). Good.

11. **pricing.js** looks correct.

12. **analyzer.js** — fine; fallback for office page count is estimated. Acceptable.

13. **schema** — matches. No migration needed.

Now, scope: This is a lot. The user asked "What did we do so far?" and "Continue if you have next steps." So they want a summary + proceed with fixes. Given the session, the highest-value fixes:

**A. Office file printing (CRITICAL)** — the "no glitches" gap: 
   - backend: skip office conversion on non-Windows
   - agents: correct extension + PowerShell conversion
   
**B. WhatsApp Back-button strand (MAJOR)** — hide Back at step1 when waSource.

**C. Price freshness on confirm (MAJOR)** — fetch price before placing order.

**D. Guest 401 hardening (minor/latent)** — skip redirect for /guest paths, don't attach token to guest.

**E. copyOrderId/OrderTracking/superadmin/EXPIRING** — minor display; maybe quick OrderTracking fix. Skip others to keep focus. Actually the user's priority: "the shop go live without glitches". Let me do A-D and quickly fix OrderTracking ₹undefined if trivial.

Actually, let me reconsider C. The /guest/upload route (line 675/685) sets totalPrice from pricing at upload time. Settings changes update file.settings but not order.totalPrice. /price recomputes. Confirm route — let me check what /confirm uses for cash. Let me look at confirm route and payment initiate. Line 1140 updates totalPrice in /price. In confirm, does it recompute or use stored? I saw line 1142 sets totalPrice at confirm (grandTotal) — wait that's the /price route (1140-1143). The confirm route is elsewhere. Let me check the confirm route to see if it uses order.totalPrice or recomputes. Let me read around confirm route.

Also need to double check: handlePlaceOrder online path calls initiate with `uploadedOrder.id` only; initiate uses order.totalPrice (line 1186). If price stale → wrong amount charged. So fetching price before confirm is the right fix.

Let me read the confirm route quickly, then implement. Let me also check that the file route serves office original: yes line 2236 fallback to storagePath. But wait — for office files if processFile returns original storagePath, then no print-ready PDF exists, so line 2234 check fails → fallback storagePath. Good.

One more: the jobs list includes `file: { select: { id, originalName, fileType } }` — fileType present. Agent can use it. Good.
